31	
32	**[I. Introduction and Engagement Summary]{.underline}**
33	
34	Clearview Valuation Services, LLC (\"Clearview\") was retained by Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. (the \"Debtor\" or \"Cascadia\"), a Delaware corporation headquartered at 1200 SW Morrison Street, Suite 1600, Portland, OR 97205, through its restructuring counsel Whitfield & Crane LLP and in coordination with its financial advisor Pinecrest Advisory Group, LLC, to provide an independent estimate of the total enterprise value (\"TEV\") of the Debtor.
35	
36	**Purpose of Engagement.** Clearview was engaged to estimate the TEV of the Debtor on a going-concern basis as of the Petition Date (March 3, 2025) for use in connection with the Debtor\'s Second Amended Plan of Reorganization (the \"Plan\") filed in Case No. 25-30412-MLE before the Honorable Margaret L. Eriksson, United States Bankruptcy Judge, District of Oregon. The valuation is intended to support the Disclosure Statement filed April 28, 2025, the claims waterfall analysis, and the assessment of plan feasibility under 11 U.S.C. § 1129(a)(11). In addition, the valuation framework and claims waterfall set forth herein are intended to provide Debtor\'s counsel and financial advisor with a basis for evaluating the allocation of value among creditor classes under the Plan and for purposes of negotiations with the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors (the \"Committee\") and other parties in interest.
37	
38	**Scope and Limitations.** Clearview\'s analysis, as set forth in this summary report, constitutes an estimate of total enterprise value and does not constitute a fairness opinion, a solvency opinion, or an opinion regarding the legal sufficiency of any proposed plan of reorganization. Clearview has not been engaged to opine on the feasibility of the Plan under 11 U.S.C. § 1129(a)(11); feasibility analysis falls within the scope of Pinecrest Advisory Group, LLC\'s separate engagement. Clearview\'s valuation is limited to the estimation of TEV and the presentation of a claims waterfall framework for informational purposes.
39	
40	**Information Relied Upon.** In preparing this report, Clearview relied upon financial data and other information provided by the Debtor and Pinecrest Advisory Group, LLC, including but not limited to: (a) the Debtor\'s audited financial statements for fiscal years 2022, 2023, and 2024; (b) unaudited financial data for the period ending February 28, 2025; (c) five-year management projections (FY2025E--FY2029E) prepared by Pinecrest Advisory Group, LLC in consultation with Debtor\'s management; (d) industry data from publicly available sources, including the U.S. Forest Service, the National Association of Home Builders, and timber industry publications; and (e) comparable company and comparable transaction data from third-party databases. Clearview did not independently audit or verify the accuracy or completeness of such data and has assumed that the information provided is accurate and complete in all material respects.
41	
42	**Standard Disclaimers.** This summary report is subject to the detailed assumptions, limiting conditions, and qualifications set forth in Section VII herein and in Appendix A to the full valuation report. A summary of key assumptions and limiting conditions is provided in Section VII of this report. The full valuation report, dated April 25, 2025, comprising approximately 187 pages, contains the complete set of assumptions, data sources, supporting analyses, and limiting conditions.
43	
44	**[II. Company Overview]{.underline}**
45	
46	Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. is a vertically integrated timber and wood products company engaged in the ownership, management, and harvesting of timberland and the manufacturing of lumber and engineered wood products. The Debtor\'s operations span the full value chain from raw timber harvesting through finished lumber and engineered wood product manufacturing, providing diversified revenue streams across multiple segments of the forest products industry.
47	
48	**Operations and Facilities.** The Debtor\'s principal operations include the following:
49	
50	> • **Timberland Harvesting.** Cascadia owns or holds long-term harvest rights on approximately 340,000 acres of timberland located in Oregon and Washington, comprising predominantly Douglas fir, western hemlock, and western red cedar. Harvesting operations supply both Cascadia\'s own manufacturing facilities and third-party purchasers under long-term supply agreements.
51	>
52	> • **Sawmill Operations.** The Debtor operates two sawmills: (i) the Bend Mill, located at 62400 Boyd Acres Road, Bend, OR 97701, which primarily processes Douglas fir and produces dimensional lumber for residential construction markets; and (ii) the Centralia Mill, located at 1105 North Pearl Street, Centralia, WA 98531, which processes a mix of species and serves both residential and commercial lumber markets. Combined rated annual production capacity across both mills is approximately 480 million board feet.
53	>
54	> • **Laminated Veneer Lumber (LVL) Plant.** Cascadia operates a laminated veneer lumber manufacturing facility located at 3880 West 11th Avenue, Eugene, OR 97402. The LVL plant produces structural engineered wood products used in commercial and residential construction. The Eugene facility has been operating below full capacity since 2023 due to reduced demand but is projected to reach full capacity utilization by FY2028E under management\'s projections.
55	
56	**Pre-Petition Financial Summary.** For fiscal year 2024, Cascadia reported total revenue of approximately \$412 million, derived from lumber sales, LVL product sales, and log sales to third parties. The Debtor\'s employer identification number is 93-1247856.
57	
58	**Causes of Financial Distress.** The Debtor\'s financial distress is attributable to a convergence of three principal factors:
59	
60	> \(a\) *Wildfire Losses (2023).* Significant wildfire events during the 2023 fire season damaged approximately 28,000 acres of Cascadia\'s timberland in southern Oregon and disrupted harvesting operations for a period of approximately five months. Insurance recoveries were materially below replacement value, and the Debtor incurred approximately \$37 million in unreimbursed losses.
61	>
62	> \(b\) *Sustained Decline in U.S. Housing Starts.* A prolonged downturn in U.S. residential housing starts, driven by elevated mortgage interest rates and reduced affordability, has resulted in depressed demand for dimensional lumber and engineered wood products. U.S. housing starts declined from approximately 1.55 million units (annualized) in 2022 to approximately 1.28 million units (annualized) by early 2025, representing a contraction of approximately 17%.
63	>
64	> \(c\) *Over-Leveraged Capital Structure from 2021 Dividend Recapitalization.* On September 14, 2021, the Debtor completed a dividend recapitalization transaction in which Timberline Capital Partners, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, provided \$95 million in second lien notes (the \"Second Lien Notes\"). The proceeds of the Second Lien Notes were used to fund a dividend to the Debtor\'s existing equity holders. This transaction substantially increased Cascadia\'s leverage at a time when revenue and EBITDA were at cyclical highs, leaving the company poorly positioned to absorb the subsequent revenue declines and wildfire losses. The September 2021 dividend recapitalization is a subject of potential avoidance action scrutiny by the estate.
65	
66	**Capital Structure and Liabilities.** As of the Petition Date, total scheduled liabilities were approximately \$637 million. Total scheduled assets at book value were approximately \$489 million, resulting in a book-value deficit of approximately \$148 million. The Debtor\'s funded debt consists primarily of (i) a senior secured revolving credit facility and term loan with First Meridian Bank, N.A., with \$261.4 million outstanding, and (ii) the Second Lien Notes held by Timberline Capital Partners, LLC, with \$95.0 million outstanding.
67	
68	**Chapter 11 Filing and Committee Formation.** The Debtor filed a voluntary petition for relief under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code on March 3, 2025, in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Oregon. The case was assigned to the Honorable Margaret L. Eriksson. The Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors was appointed on March 17, 2025, and comprises the following five members: Northway Paper Corp. (\$14.2 million claim), Deschutes Equipment Leasing Co. (\$8.7 million unsecured deficiency claim), Columbia River Transport LLC (\$6.1 million claim), Inland Fiber Supply, Inc. (\$4.9 million claim), and the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (\$11.3 million claim). Total general unsecured claims are estimated at approximately \$187.0 million.
69	
70	**Key Contractual Relationships.** The Debtor maintains several significant contractual relationships relevant to the valuation analysis. The Centralia Mill\'s timber supply agreement with Olympic Forest Resources LLC, providing approximately \$22 million per year in raw timber supply, is proposed to be assumed under the Plan. The Bend Mill\'s equipment maintenance agreement with PacWest Industrial Services, at approximately \$1.8 million per year, is proposed to be rejected, with the Debtor anticipating comparable replacement services at similar or lower cost.
71	
72	**[III. Valuation Methodologies]{.underline}**
73	
74	In estimating the total enterprise value of Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc., Clearview employed three widely recognized valuation methodologies to triangulate a defensible range of enterprise value. The use of multiple approaches allows for cross-validation of results and reduces the risk that any single methodology\'s inherent limitations will distort the overall conclusion. The three methodologies employed are:
75	
76	1\. **Discounted Cash Flow (\"DCF\") Analysis** --- a fundamental, income-based approach that estimates enterprise value by projecting the Debtor\'s future free cash flows and discounting them to present value using an appropriate cost of capital.
77	
78	2\. **Comparable Public Company Analysis** --- a market-based approach that estimates enterprise value by reference to valuation multiples observed among publicly traded companies with comparable operations, scale, and risk profiles.
79	
80	3\. **Comparable Transaction Analysis** --- a market-based approach that estimates enterprise value by reference to valuation multiples observed in recent merger and acquisition transactions involving comparable businesses.
81	
82	Each of the three methodologies is appropriate for the valuation of a vertically integrated timber and wood products company such as Cascadia. The timber industry has several unique valuation characteristics that merit consideration across all three approaches: (a) the significant contribution of timberland assets to enterprise value, with timberland serving as both an operating asset and a store of value subject to biological growth; (b) the cyclical nature of revenue and earnings, which are closely tied to U.S. housing starts and lumber commodity prices; and (c) the role of biological growth as a natural hedge against short-term cyclical downturns, as unharvested timber continues to accrete volume and value over time.
83	
84	**Weighting of Approaches.** Clearview weighted the three valuation approaches as follows: DCF Analysis (50%), Comparable Public Company Analysis (25%), and Comparable Transaction Analysis (25%). The DCF analysis was assigned the greatest weight because it most directly captures the specific cash flow profile, capital expenditure requirements, and growth trajectory of Cascadia as a post-emergence going concern. The comparable public company and comparable transaction analyses were each assigned 25% weight, as they provide useful market-based validation of the DCF results but are subject to comparability limitations given Cascadia\'s Chapter 11 status and specific risk factors, including wildfire exposure and the ongoing restructuring.
85	
86	**III.A. Discounted Cash Flow Analysis**
87	
88	The DCF analysis estimates the present value of Cascadia\'s projected unlevered free cash flows over a five-year discrete projection period (FY2025E through FY2029E), plus the present value of a terminal value representing the Debtor\'s going-concern value beyond the projection period.
89	
90	**Projection Basis.** The DCF analysis is based on five-year management projections prepared by Pinecrest Advisory Group, LLC in consultation with Debtor\'s management. Clearview reviewed these projections for internal consistency and reasonableness but did not independently develop an alternative set of projections. Key revenue and earnings assumptions underlying the projections are summarized below.
91	
92	**Revenue Assumptions.** Projected revenue for FY2025E is \$380 million, reflecting reduced harvesting volume attributable to the ongoing effects of the 2023 wildfire damage and depressed lumber prices in the current macroeconomic environment. Revenue is projected to grow over the five-year period to \$445 million by FY2029E, driven by: (i) a gradual recovery in U.S. housing starts from approximately 1.28 million units (annualized) in early 2025 to approximately 1.45 million units by 2029; (ii) restoration of harvesting volume on fire-affected timberland; and (iii) the LVL plant in Eugene reaching full capacity utilization by FY2028E, contributing incremental revenue of approximately \$20--\$25 million per year at full run rate.
93	
94	**EBITDA Margin Assumptions.** Projected EBITDA margins range from approximately 14.5% in FY2025E (approximately \$55.1 million) to 19.2% in FY2029E (approximately \$85.4 million). The improvement in margins reflects: (i) cost optimization measures implemented during the restructuring, including headcount reductions and procurement renegotiations; (ii) the normalization of wildfire-related operational disruptions; and (iii) the incremental contribution of higher-margin LVL products as the Eugene facility scales to full capacity.
95	
96	**Capital Expenditure Assumptions.** Maintenance capital expenditures for mill operations and timberland reforestation are projected at approximately \$18 million to \$22 million per year across the projection period. These estimates include ongoing mill equipment maintenance, reforestation costs for harvested and fire-damaged acreage, and routine infrastructure upkeep. No material expansion capital expenditures are projected beyond the LVL plant capacity ramp, which is expected to be funded from existing installed capacity and modest incremental investment.
97	
98	**Terminal Value.** A terminal value was calculated using the perpetuity growth method, applying a long-term terminal growth rate of 2.0% to normalized free cash flow in the terminal year. The 2.0% terminal growth rate reflects long-term GDP-linked timber demand and is consistent with industry consensus estimates for sustainable growth in the U.S. forest products sector.
99	
100	**Discount Rate.** Clearview applied a weighted average cost of capital (\"WACC\") in the range of 10.5% to 12.0%, reflecting the risk profile of a post-emergence timber company with significant remaining leverage, exposure to cyclical commodity markets, and wildfire risk. The WACC was derived from a capital asset pricing model adjusted for company-specific risk factors, including a size premium and a company-specific risk premium reflecting Cascadia\'s Chapter 11 emergence and operational concentration in the Pacific Northwest.
101	
102	**DCF Valuation Result.** Based on the foregoing assumptions, the DCF analysis yields a TEV range of **\$390 million to \$435 million**, with a midpoint of **\$412.5 million**. The range reflects sensitivity to the WACC assumption, with the low end of the range corresponding to the 12.0% WACC and the high end corresponding to the 10.5% WACC.
103	
104	**III.B. Comparable Public Company Analysis**
105	
106	The comparable public company analysis estimates Cascadia\'s enterprise value by reference to valuation multiples observed among publicly traded companies with operations, end markets, and risk profiles broadly comparable to those of the Debtor. Clearview selected the following four comparable companies in the timber, wood products, and forest products sectors:
107	
108	> • **Evergreen Timber Corp.** --- A large-cap integrated timber company with timberland holdings, sawmill operations, and wood products manufacturing across multiple regions of the United States. Evergreen is the most directly comparable company given its vertically integrated business model, although it operates at significantly greater scale than Cascadia.
109	>
110	> • **Cascade Forest Products, Inc.** --- A mid-cap lumber and panel producer operating primarily in the Pacific Northwest and British Columbia. Cascade\'s product mix includes dimensional lumber, plywood, and oriented strand board.
111	>
112	> • **Northern Woodlands Holdings, Ltd.** --- A timber REIT with holdings concentrated in the Pacific Northwest and Southeastern United States. Northern Woodlands\' revenue is predominantly derived from log sales and timberland management fees, with limited downstream manufacturing operations.
113	>
114	> • **Pacific Lumber Industries, Inc.** --- A mid-cap sawmill operator with facilities in Oregon, Washington, and Northern California. Pacific Lumber\'s operations are heavily weighted toward dimensional lumber production for residential construction markets.
115	
116	**Multiples Analyzed.** Clearview analyzed the following valuation multiples for each comparable company: (i) EV/EBITDA on a last-twelve-months (\"LTM\") basis; (ii) EV/EBITDA on a next-twelve-months (\"NTM\") basis; (iii) EV/Revenue; and (iv) EV/Timberland Acres (where applicable). Among these metrics, EV/EBITDA was selected as the primary valuation multiple given its broad acceptance in the timber and forest products industry and its ability to normalize for differences in capital structure and tax treatment across the comparable set.
117	
118	**Selected Multiple Range.** Based on the analysis of the comparable set, Clearview selected an EV/EBITDA multiple range of 7.0x to 8.5x, which was applied to Cascadia\'s FY2025E EBITDA of approximately \$55.1 million (derived from projected FY2025E revenue of \$380 million at an EBITDA margin of approximately 14.5%). The selected range reflects the central tendency of the comparable companies\' trading multiples, with adjustments for differences in growth profile, asset quality, and end-market diversification.
119	
120	**Unadjusted TEV Range.** Application of the 7.0x to 8.5x EV/EBITDA multiple range to Cascadia\'s FY2025E EBITDA yields an unadjusted TEV range of \$385 million to \$468 million.
121	
122	**Size and Distress Discount.** Clearview applied a discount of approximately 5% to 10% to the unadjusted comparable company-derived TEV to reflect: (i) Cascadia\'s smaller scale relative to several of the comparable companies; (ii) the Debtor\'s Chapter 11 status and the associated execution risk of emergence; and (iii) the elevated wildfire risk specific to Cascadia\'s timberland holdings in southern Oregon. These factors would, in Clearview\'s judgment, cause a market participant to apply a lower multiple to Cascadia relative to the comparable set.
123	
124	**Adjusted TEV Range.** After application of the size/distress discount, the comparable public company analysis yields an adjusted TEV range of **\$365 million to \$420 million**, with a midpoint of **\$392.5 million**.
125	
126	**III.C. Comparable Transaction Analysis**
127	
128	The comparable transaction analysis estimates Cascadia\'s enterprise value by reference to valuation multiples observed in recent merger and acquisition transactions involving target companies in the timber and wood products sector. Clearview identified the following four transactions completed within the prior 36 months as most relevant:
129	
130	> • **Acquisition of Redwood Valley Lumber, Inc. by Glacier Peak Capital LLC (2024).** Redwood Valley was a mid-size integrated lumber producer with sawmill and timberland operations in Northern California. Transaction EV/EBITDA multiple: 8.2x. The premium reflected Glacier Peak\'s strategic interest in securing Pacific coast timber supply.
131	>
132	> • **Acquisition of Timberland Resources Co. by Blue Ridge Forest Holdings, LP (2023).** Timberland Resources was a timberland owner and log sales company with approximately 210,000 acres in the Southeastern United States. Transaction EV/EBITDA multiple: 7.5x. The lower multiple reflected the target\'s limited downstream manufacturing operations and geographic concentration.
133	>
134	> • **Merger of Sierra Pacific Wood Products, Inc. with Trident Forestry Group, Inc. (2023).** This was a strategic combination of two mid-cap wood products manufacturers with complementary product lines and geographic footprints. Transaction EV/EBITDA multiple: 9.1x. The premium multiple reflected the significant synergy expectations disclosed in connection with the merger.
135	>
136	> • Acquisition of Northwest Fiber Corp. by Oakvale Timber Partners, LLC (2022). Northwest Fiber was a fiber and pulp-grade timber producer in Oregon and Washington. Transaction EV/EBITDA multiple: 7.8x. The multiple reflected the target\'s exposure to cyclical pulp markets and limited diversification.
137	
138	**Median Transaction Multiple.** The median EV/EBITDA multiple across the four selected transactions is 7.9x (calculated as the average of the two middle values: 7.8x and 8.2x, yielding 8.0x, with the median falling at 7.9x when interpolated from the full distribution). The mean transaction EV/EBITDA multiple is 8.15x.
139	
140	**Unadjusted TEV.** Application of the median 7.9x EV/EBITDA multiple to Cascadia\'s FY2025E EBITDA of approximately \$55.1 million yields an unadjusted implied TEV of approximately \$435 million.
141	
142	**Distress and Restructuring Discount.** Clearview applied a discount of approximately 5% to 10% to the transaction-derived TEV to account for the Debtor\'s Chapter 11 status, the execution risk associated with plan emergence, and the absence of a competitive auction process (which would typically drive transaction multiples above intrinsic value). The transactions in the comparable set were completed in non-distressed contexts between willing buyers and sellers, and the multiples observed likely reflect strategic or financial buyer premiums that would not be fully applicable to a Chapter 11 debtor.
143	
144	**Adjusted TEV Range.** After application of the distress/restructuring discount, the comparable transaction analysis yields an adjusted TEV range of **\$392 million to \$413 million**, with a midpoint of **\$402.5 million**.
145	
146	**[IV. Valuation Conclusion]{.underline}**
147	
148	Based on the three valuation methodologies described in Section III and the weighting assigned to each, Clearview\'s conclusion regarding the total enterprise value of Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. is summarized in the table below.
149	
150	**Summary of Valuation Results**
151	
152	  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
153	  **Methodology**                      **TEV Low**    **TEV Midpoint**   **TEV High**   **Weight**
154	  ------------------------------------ -------------- ------------------ -------------- --------------
155	  Discounted Cash Flow Analysis        \$390.0M       \$412.5M           \$435.0M       50%
156	
157	  Comparable Public Company Analysis   \$365.0M       \$392.5M           \$420.0M       25%
158	
159	  Comparable Transaction Analysis      \$392.0M       \$402.5M           \$413.0M       25%
160	
161	  **Weighted Blended Result**          **\$385.0M**   **\$407.5M**       **\$430.0M**   **100%**
162	  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
163	
164	**Valuation Conclusion.** Based on the analysis described in this report, it is Clearview\'s opinion that the total enterprise value of Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. as a going concern, as of the Petition Date (March 3, 2025), falls within the range of **\$385 million to \$430 million**, with a midpoint estimate of **\$407.5 million**.
165	
166	This TEV represents the value of the Debtor\'s operating assets and business on an unlevered basis, before the deduction of funded debt and other claims against the estate. TEV reflects the aggregate value of the Debtor\'s timberland, manufacturing facilities, contracts, workforce, and intangible assets as a going concern, and assumes that the Debtor will emerge from Chapter 11 as Reorganized Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. and continue operations in the ordinary course.
167	
168	The TEV range set forth above does not include the value of avoidance action claims held by the estate. The Debtor\'s estate holds identified preference claims estimated at approximately \$9.5 million in gross recovery value. These avoidance action claims are estate causes of action that exist independent of the Debtor\'s operating business and are not reflected in the enterprise valuation. To the extent avoidance action recoveries are realized, such recoveries would represent additional distributable value available to the estate beyond the TEV-derived waterfall. The timing, net amount (after litigation costs), and ultimate allocation of avoidance action proceeds are subject to significant uncertainty and are matters to be addressed in the Plan and Disclosure Statement rather than in this valuation analysis.
169	
170	Clearview notes that the TEV range is presented as of the Petition Date (March 3, 2025) and reflects conditions, market data, and expectations as of that date. Material changes in timber markets, interest rates, housing starts, or other macroeconomic conditions subsequent to the valuation date could result in a different value conclusion if a valuation were performed as of a later date.
171	
172	**[V. Claims Waterfall Analysis]{.underline}**
173	
174	This section presents the claims waterfall analysis, which allocates the estimated TEV across the priority tiers of claims against the Debtor\'s estate. The waterfall is presented at the low case, midpoint, and high case of the TEV range established in Section IV. The purpose of the waterfall is to illustrate the allocation of value among the Debtor\'s creditor constituencies and to provide a framework for evaluating the treatment of claims under the Plan.

176	**Step 1: Total Enterprise Value**

178	  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
179	                           **Low Case**      **Midpoint**      **High Case**
180	  ------------------------ ----------------- ----------------- -----------------
181	  Total Enterprise Value   \$385.0M          \$407.5M          \$430.0M
182	
183	  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
184	
185	**Step 2: Administrative, Priority, and Secured Claims Context**
186	
187	For purposes of this waterfall, administrative and priority claims are noted as senior claims that must be paid in full under any confirmable plan pursuant to 11 U.S.C. §§ 507 and 1129(a)(9). These claims are satisfied from available cash at emergence and do not reduce TEV for purposes of the secured claim and equity allocation analysis. They are summarized here for completeness:
188	
189	> • Administrative Claims: \$12.5 million (comprising professional fees of \$8.1 million, U.S. Trustee fees of \$0.4 million, and post-petition trade payables of \$4.0 million)
190	>
191	> • Priority Tax Claims: \$3.2 million
192	>
193	> • Priority Non-Tax Claims (employee wages and benefits per §§ 507(a)(4) and (a)(5)): \$2.8 million
194	>
195	> • **Total Administrative and Priority Claims: \$18.5 million**
196	
197	**Step 3: Senior Secured Claims --- First Meridian Bank, N.A.**
198	
199	  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
200	                                          **Low Case**      **Midpoint**      **High Case**
201	  --------------------------------------- ----------------- ----------------- -----------------
202	  TEV                                     \$385.0M          \$407.5M          \$430.0M
203	
204	  Senior Secured Claim (First Meridian)   (\$261.4M)        (\$261.4M)        (\$261.4M)
205	
206	  TEV in Excess of Senior Secured Claim   \$123.6M          \$146.1M          \$168.6M
207	  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
208	
209	First Meridian Bank, N.A. holds a first-priority senior secured claim of \$261.4 million outstanding, secured by substantially all of the Debtor\'s assets. At every point across the TEV range, TEV exceeds the senior secured claim amount, and accordingly, the First Meridian claim is fully secured across the entire valuation range. Under the Plan, the senior secured claim is proposed to be reinstated with amended terms: the maturity date will be extended from June 2028 to June 2031, and the interest rate will be reduced from SOFR + 425 basis points to SOFR + 350 basis points. No cash distribution is required at the Effective Date for the secured claim itself, as the claim is being reinstated rather than paid.
210	
211	**Conclusion:** First Meridian Bank, N.A.\'s claim is fully secured across the entire TEV range.
212	
213	**Step 4: Residual Value Available for Junior Claims and Equity**
214	
215	  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
216	                                              **Low Case**      **Midpoint**      **High Case**
217	  ------------------------------------------- ----------------- ----------------- -----------------
218	  Residual Value After Senior Secured Claim   \$123.6M          \$146.1M          \$168.6M
219	
220	  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
221	
222	The residual value after satisfaction of the senior secured claim represents the value available for distribution to junior claims (the Second Lien Notes) and, to the extent residual value exists, equity.
223	
224	**Step 5: Second Lien Notes --- Timberline Capital Partners, LLC**
225	
226	Timberline Capital Partners, LLC holds \$95.0 million in face amount of Second Lien Notes. Under the Plan, Timberline\'s proposed treatment consists of two components: (i) a cash payment of \$35.0 million, and (ii) conversion of \$60.0 million of its remaining claim into new common equity of Reorganized Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc.
227	
228	The cash payment of \$35.0 million reduces the residual value available for equity allocation. The remaining analysis focuses on the equity conversion component.
229	
230	**Equity Allocation Analysis:**
231	
232	The \$60.0 million claim conversion into equity should, under standard waterfall principles, correspond to a pro rata share of the reorganized equity value equal to the ratio of the converted claim to total residual equity value. The analysis at each case is as follows:
233	
234	  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
235	                                   **Low Case**      **Midpoint**      **High Case**
236	  -------------------------------- ----------------- ----------------- -----------------
237	  Residual Equity Value (Step 4)   \$123.6M          \$146.1M          \$168.6M
238	
239	  Timberline Cash Payment          (\$35.0M)         (\$35.0M)         (\$35.0M)
240	
241	  Net Residual Equity Value        \$88.6M           \$111.1M          \$133.6M
242	  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
243	
244	Clearview notes that the equity allocation can be analyzed either as a proportion of total residual value (before the cash payment) or as a proportion of total reorganized equity (after accounting for Timberline\'s full treatment). For purposes of this analysis, Clearview presents the equity percentage as the ratio of the converted claim amount (\$60.0 million) to total residual equity value (\$146.1 million at midpoint), which represents the share of total enterprise equity value that corresponds to Timberline\'s equity conversion:
245	
246	  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
247	                                  **Low Case**      **Midpoint**      **High Case**
248	  ------------------------------- ----------------- ----------------- -----------------
249	  Converted Claim Amount          \$60.0M           \$60.0M           \$60.0M
250	
251	  Total Residual Equity Value     \$123.6M          \$146.1M          \$168.6M
252	
253	  **Implied Equity Percentage**   **48.54%**        **41.07%**        **35.59%**
254	  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
255	
256	At the midpoint TEV of \$407.5 million, Timberline\'s conversion of \$60.0 million in claims into equity implies an equity allocation of \$60.0 million ÷ \$146.1 million = **41.07%** of the new common equity of the Reorganized Debtor. At the low end of the TEV range, the implied equity percentage rises to 48.54%, and at the high end, it falls to 35.59%. **At no point in the TEV range does the mathematically derived equity percentage equal 55%.**
257	
258	Clearview understands that the Second Amended Plan of Reorganization filed April 28, 2025, states that Timberline Capital Partners, LLC will receive 55% of the new common equity of Reorganized Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. Clearview\'s waterfall analysis, as presented herein, indicates that a 55% allocation would imply Timberline is receiving equity valued at \$146.1 million × 55% = \$80.355 million (at midpoint) in exchange for converting only \$60.0 million of its claim, resulting in a **value transfer of \$20.355 million** beyond the converted claim amount at the midpoint TEV. This value transfer would be even larger at the high end of the TEV range (\$168.6 million × 55% = \$92.73 million in equity value, compared to a \$60.0 million converted claim --- a value transfer of \$32.73 million) and smaller but still significant at the low end (\$123.6 million × 55% = \$67.98 million, compared to a \$60.0 million converted claim --- a value transfer of \$7.98 million). **Clearview notes this discrepancy for the attention of Debtor\'s counsel and financial advisor.**
259	
260	**Step 6: Residual Equity Value After Timberline**
261	
262	The treatment of the equity residual depends on whether the 41.07% mathematically derived figure or the Plan\'s stated 55% figure is used:
263	
264	  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
265	                                           **At 41.07% (Mathematically Derived)**   **At 55% (Plan\'s Stated Allocation)**
266	  ---------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------
267	  Total Residual Equity Value (Midpoint)   \$146.1M                                 \$146.1M
268	
269	  Timberline Equity Value                  \$60.0M (41.07%)                         \$80.355M (55%)
270	
271	  Remaining Equity Value                   \$86.1M (58.93%)                         \$65.745M (45%)
272	  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
273	
274	The difference of \$20.355 million at midpoint (\$86.1 million minus \$65.745 million) represents additional equity value that would be available for allocation to other stakeholders --- including participants in the Management Incentive Plan (\"MIP\") pool and other equity recipients --- if the mathematically correct 41.07% figure were used rather than the Plan\'s stated 55%.
275	
276	**Step 7: General Unsecured Claims**
277	
278	Total general unsecured claims against the estate are estimated at approximately \$187.0 million. Under the Plan, general unsecured creditors are proposed to receive a cash recovery pool of \$18.7 million, representing a recovery rate of approximately 10.0% (\$18.7 million ÷ \$187.0 million). The unsecured recovery pool is to be distributed 50% on the Effective Date (\$9.35 million) and 50% on the first anniversary of the Effective Date (\$9.35 million). General unsecured creditors do not receive any equity in the Reorganized Debtor under the Plan.
279	
280	**Step 8: Old Equity Interests**
281	
282	All existing equity interests in Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. are cancelled under the Plan and receive no distribution.
283

292	
293	  Second Lien (Timberline) --- Equity   \$60.0M converted   48.54% equity             41.07% equity             35.59% equity
294	
295	  General Unsecured Creditors           \$187.0M            \$18.7M (10.0%)           \$18.7M (10.0%)           \$18.7M (10.0%)

300	**[VI. Distributable Value and Plan Feasibility Context]{.underline}**
301	
302	This section provides an analysis of the total distributable value available to fund Plan distributions, which is distinct from --- and in certain respects less than --- the TEV set forth in Section IV. While TEV measures the aggregate going-concern value of the Debtor\'s operating assets and business, distributable value represents the actual resources (cash and equity) available to satisfy claims and fund distributions under the Plan at and following the Effective Date.
303	
304	**Sources of Distributable Value**
305	
306	The principal sources of distributable value available to fund Plan distributions are as follows:
307	
308	> \(a\) **Cash on Hand at Emergence.** Based on projections prepared by Pinecrest Advisory Group, LLC and referenced in the Disclosure Statement, the Debtor is projected to have approximately \$68.0 million in unrestricted cash on hand at emergence (estimated Effective Date: August 15, 2025). This amount reflects projected operating cash flows during the Chapter 11 period, net of ordinary-course operating expenses and post-petition obligations.
309	>
310	> \(b\) **New Equity Value.** At the TEV midpoint, total residual equity value (after deduction of the senior secured claim) is \$146.1 million. This value is not cash; it is allocated to recipients of new common equity in the Reorganized Debtor, including Timberline Capital Partners, LLC and participants in the Management Incentive Plan. The new equity value does not fund cash distributions.
311	>
312	> \(c\) **Avoidance Action Recoveries.** The Debtor\'s estate holds identified preference claims estimated at approximately \$9.5 million in gross recovery value. These avoidance actions are estate causes of action that are not included in the TEV and represent additional distributable value beyond the enterprise-value-derived waterfall. Avoidance action proceeds, if realized, would be available for distribution to creditors or retention by the reorganized estate, depending on Plan allocation provisions.

314	> \(d\) **Potential Additional Recoveries.** The litigation trust established under the Plan may pursue claims beyond identified preferences, including potential fraudulent transfer and other avoidance actions. 385	
386	> 1\. **Going-Concern Assumption.** The Debtor will continue as a going concern and emerge from Chapter 11 as Reorganized Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. in accordance with the Second Amended Plan of Reorganization. The valuation does not consider a liquidation scenario or a forced-sale scenario.
387	>
388	> 2\. **Reasonableness of Management Projections.** The five-year management projections (FY2025E--FY2029E) prepared by Pinecrest Advisory Group, LLC in consultation with Debtor\'s management are reasonable and achievable under the Plan. Clearview reviewed these projections for internal consistency and reasonableness but did not independently develop alternative projections or stress-test the projections under adverse scenarios.
389	>
390	> 3\. **No Material Adverse Changes.** There will be no material adverse changes to timber markets, the regulatory environment, or wildfire risk beyond those already reflected in the management projections. In particular, the projections assume no major wildfire events affecting Cascadia\'s timberland during the projection period and a gradual recovery in U.S. housing starts consistent with consensus economic forecasts.

392	> 4\. **Reinstated Senior Secured Facility.** The senior secured credit facility with First Meridian Bank, N.A. will be reinstated with the amended terms proposed under the Plan, including extension of the maturity date from June 2028 to June 2031 and reduction of the interest rate from SOFR + 425 basis points to SOFR + 350 basis points.

398	> 7\. **Exclusion of Avoidance Action Recoveries from TEV.** Avoidance action recoveries estimated at approximately \$9.5 million (gross) are excluded from TEV and treated as additional distributable value with uncertain timing. 36	The Plan provides for the comprehensive restructuring of the Debtor\'s outstanding obligations and the continuation of the Debtor\'s business operations as a going concern. Eriksson. 184	**Section 1.2 --- Rules of Interpretation**
185	
186	For purposes of this Plan, the following rules of interpretation shall apply:
187	
188	\(a\) The word \"or\" is not exclusive, and the use of \"or\" shall be deemed to include \"and/or\" unless the context clearly requires otherwise.
189	
190	\(b\) The words \"include,\" \"includes,\" and \"including\" shall be deemed to be followed by the phrase \"but not limited to\" or \"without limitation\" regardless of whether such phrase actually follows such words.
191	
192	\(c\) The use of the singular shall include the plural and vice versa, and the use of one gender shall include all genders, as the context may require.
193	
194	\(d\) All headings and captions in this Plan are for convenience of reference only and shall not be considered in interpreting or construing this Plan or any provision hereof.
195	
196	\(e\) Defined terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them throughout this Plan, the Disclosure Statement, and all Exhibits and the Plan Supplement, unless otherwise expressly provided or the context clearly requires a different meaning.
197	
198	\(f\) References to statutes, regulations, or rules shall include all amendments thereto and successor provisions, whether adopted before or after the date of this Plan, unless otherwise expressly stated.
199	
200	\(g\) Unless otherwise specified, all references to articles, sections, exhibits, and schedules are to the respective articles, sections, exhibits, and schedules of or to this Plan.
201	
202	\(h\) Any term used but not defined herein that is defined in the Bankruptcy Code or the Bankruptcy Rules shall have the meaning ascribed to such term therein.

205

When the last day of any such period falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday (as defined in Bankruptcy Rule 9006(a)), the period shall be extended to the next day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday. Unless otherwise specified, all references to \"days\" shall mean calendar days.
207	
208	**Section 1.4 --- Governing Law**
209	
210	Except to the extent that the Bankruptcy Code or the Bankruptcy Rules apply, the rights, obligations, and duties arising under this Plan shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of Oregon, without giving effect to the principles of conflicts of law thereof. To the extent that corporate governance matters are implicated, the internal affairs of the Reorganized Debtor shall be governed by the General Corporation Law of the State of Delaware. In the event of any inconsistency between the Bankruptcy Code and any other applicable law, the Bankruptcy Code shall control.
211	
212	**[ARTICLE II --- ADMINISTRATIVE AND PRIORITY CLAIMS (UNCLASSIFIED)]{.underline}**
213	
214	Pursuant to section 1123(a)(1) of the Bankruptcy Code, Administrative Claims and Priority Tax Claims are not classified and are excluded from the Classes set forth in Article III. The holders of such Claims are not entitled to vote on the Plan.
215	
216	**Section 2.1 --- Administrative Claims**
217	
218	Each holder of an Allowed Administrative Claim shall receive, in full and final satisfaction, settlement, release, and discharge of such Claim, Cash in an amount equal to the full Allowed amount of such Administrative Claim on the later of (a) the Effective Date, (b) the date on which such Administrative Claim becomes an Allowed Administrative Claim, or (c) such other date as may be agreed upon by the holder of such Claim and the Debtor or the Reorganized Debtor, or as may be fixed by the Bankruptcy Court. 221	>
222	> \(b\) U.S. Trustee quarterly fees: approximately \$0.4 million;
223	>
224	> \(c\) Post-petition trade payables and other ordinary course obligations: approximately \$4.0 million.
225	
226	All Professional Fee Claims shall be subject to allowance by the Bankruptcy Court pursuant to sections 330 and 331 of the Bankruptcy Code. All professionals seeking allowance of Professional Fee Claims shall file their final fee applications with the Bankruptcy Court within sixty (60) days after the Effective Date. The Reorganized Debtor shall pay each Allowed Professional Fee Claim within ten (10) Business Days after entry of a Final Order allowing such Claim, or as otherwise ordered by the Bankruptcy Court. All requests for compensation or reimbursement of expenses pursuant to sections 327, 328, 330, 331, or 503(b) of the Bankruptcy Code for services rendered before the Effective Date must be filed and served in accordance with applicable orders of the Bankruptcy Court.
227	
228	**Section 2.2 --- Priority Tax Claims**
229	
230	Each holder of an Allowed Priority Tax Claim shall receive, in full and final satisfaction, settlement, release, and discharge of such Claim, Cash in an amount equal to the full Allowed amount of such Priority Tax Claim on the Effective Date (or the date on which such Claim becomes an Allowed Priority Tax Claim, if later). The estimated total amount of Priority Tax Claims is approximately \$3.2 million. Alternatively, the Debtor may elect, in its sole discretion, to pay any Allowed Priority Tax Claim in regular installment payments, in Cash, of a total value as of the Effective Date equal to the Allowed amount of such Claim, over a period ending not later than five (5) years after the Petition Date, with interest at the rate required under applicable non-bankruptcy law, pursuant to section 1129(a)(9)(C) of the Bankruptcy Code; provided, however, the Debtor currently intends to pay all Allowed Priority Tax Claims in full in Cash on the Effective Date. Nothing in this Section 2.2 shall affect the Debtor\'s or the Reorganized Debtor\'s right to object to any Priority Tax Claim on any ground permitted by the Bankruptcy Code, the Bankruptcy Rules, or applicable non-bankruptcy law.
231	
232	**Section 2.3 --- U.S. Trustee Fees**
233	
234	All fees payable under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6) and any applicable interest thereon shall be paid by the Debtor or the Reorganized Debtor in full on the Effective Date (with respect to fees that have accrued and are due and payable as of the Effective Date) and shall continue to be paid by the Reorganized Debtor when due and owing until the earliest of the date upon which the Chapter 11 Case is closed, dismissed, or converted to a case under another chapter of the Bankruptcy Code. The current estimate of such fees, included within the \$0.4 million referenced in Section 2.1(b) above, reflects the anticipated quarterly fees through the estimated Effective Date.
235	
236	**Section 2.4 --- DIP Facility Claims**
237	
238	All obligations arising under the DIP Facility provided by First Meridian Bank, N.A. shall be paid in full in Cash on the Effective Date, including all outstanding principal, accrued and unpaid interest, fees, and expenses, unless otherwise agreed in writing between the Debtor or the Reorganized Debtor and First Meridian. Alternatively, the DIP Facility may be rolled into or replaced by the Senior Secured Credit Facility as reinstated and amended under the Plan, with the consent of First Meridian. As of the date hereof, the Debtor and First Meridian are in discussions regarding the treatment of the DIP Facility and anticipate that the outstanding balance under the DIP Facility will be satisfied through a combination of Cash repayment and roll-up into the Amended Credit Agreement. The specific mechanics of such treatment shall be set forth in the Plan Supplement.
239	
240	**[ARTICLE III --- CLASSIFICATION OF CLAIMS AND INTERESTS]{.underline}**
241	
242	**Section 3.1 --- Summary of Classification**
243	
244	Pursuant to section 1122 of the Bankruptcy Code, the following table summarizes the classification of all Claims against and Interests in the Debtor under this Plan. Administrative Claims and Priority Tax Claims, as described in Article II, are not classified pursuant to section 1123(a)(1) of the Bankruptcy Code and are not included in the Classes set forth below. A Claim or Interest shall be classified in a particular Class only to the extent that such Claim or Interest qualifies within the description of that Class and shall be classified in a different Class to the extent that any remainder of such Claim or Interest qualifies within the description of such different Class.
245	
246	  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
247	  **Class**         **Description**                             **Impairment**    **Entitled to Vote**
248	  ----------------- ------------------------------------------- ----------------- -----------------------
249	  Class 1           Priority Non-Tax Claims (§ 507(a)(4)/(5))   Unimpaired        No (deemed to accept)
250	
251	  Class 2           First Meridian Secured Claim                Impaired          Yes
252	
253	  Class 3           Second Lien Note Claim (Timberline)         Impaired          Yes
254	
255	  Class 4           General Unsecured Claims                    Impaired          Yes
256	
257	  Class 5           Intercompany Claims                         Impaired          No (deemed to reject)
258	
259	  Class 6           Existing Equity Interests                   Impaired          No (deemed to reject)
260	
261	  Class 7           Section 510(b) Claims                       Impaired          No (deemed to reject)
262	  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
263	
264	The classification of Claims and Interests set forth herein is based upon the nature and priority of each Claim or Interest, as required by sections 1122 and 1123 of the Bankruptcy Code. A Claim or Interest is classified in a particular Class only to the extent that the Claim or Interest falls within the description of that Class. To the extent that a Claim or Interest falls within the description of more than one Class, such Claim or Interest shall be treated as a separate Claim or Interest in each such Class, but only to the extent that the aggregate amount of distributions to such holder does not exceed the Allowed amount of such holder\'s Claim or Interest.
265	
266	**Section 3.2 --- Special Provision Regarding Unimpaired Claims**
267	
268	In accordance with section 1126(f) of the Bankruptcy Code, holders of Unimpaired Claims are conclusively presumed to have accepted the Plan. Accordingly, holders of Claims in Class 1 are not entitled to vote to accept or reject the Plan and are deemed to have accepted the Plan. In accordance with section 1126(g) of the Bankruptcy Code, holders of Claims or Interests that are to receive no distribution under the Plan on account of such Claims or Interests are deemed to have rejected the Plan. Accordingly, holders of Claims or Interests in Classes 5, 6, and 7 are not entitled to vote to accept or reject the Plan and are deemed to have rejected the Plan. Votes of acceptance or rejection of the Plan are being solicited only from holders of Claims in Classes 2, 3, and 4.
269	
270	**[ARTICLE IV --- TREATMENT OF CLAIMS AND INTERESTS]{.underline}**
271	
272	**Section 4.1 --- Class 1: Priority Non-Tax Claims**
273	
274	Class 1 consists of all Priority Non-Tax Claims against the Debtor, including Claims entitled to priority under section 507(a)(4) of the Bankruptcy Code (for allowed unsecured claims for contributions to an employee benefit plan arising from services rendered within 180 days before the Petition Date or the date of cessation of the Debtor\'s business, whichever occurs first, for each employee, to the extent of \$15,150 per employee) and section 507(a)(5) of the Bankruptcy Code (for allowed unsecured claims for contributions to an employee benefit plan). Class 1 is Unimpaired under the Plan. Each holder of an Allowed Priority Non-Tax Claim shall receive, in full and final satisfaction, settlement, release, and discharge of such Claim, Cash in the full Allowed amount of such Claim, payable on the later of the Effective Date or the date on which such Claim becomes an Allowed Claim. The estimated aggregate amount of Priority Non-Tax Claims is approximately \$2.8 million. These claims primarily arise from pre-petition employee wages, salaries, and commissions earned within 180 days prior to the Petition Date, as well as contributions to employee benefit plans. Because Class 1 Claims are Unimpaired, holders of Class 1 Claims are conclusively presumed to have accepted the Plan and are not entitled to vote.
275	
276	**Section 4.2 --- Class 2: First Meridian Secured Claim**
277	
278	Class 2 consists of the First Meridian Secured Claim in the amount of \$261.4 million as of the Petition Date. Class 2 is Impaired under the Plan. In full and final satisfaction, settlement, release, and discharge of the First Meridian Secured Claim, the Allowed Class 2 Claim shall be reinstated with amended terms pursuant to the Amended Credit Agreement, which shall contain the following material terms:
279	
280	> \(a\) **Maturity Extension.** The maturity date of the Senior Secured Credit Facility shall be extended from June 2028 to June 2031, representing a three (3)-year extension of the existing maturity date.
281	>
282	> \(b\) **Interest Rate Reduction.** The interest rate under the Senior Secured Credit Facility shall be reduced from SOFR + 425 basis points to SOFR + 350 basis points, representing a reduction of 75 basis points.
283	>
284	> \(c\) **Continuation of Security Interest.** First Meridian shall retain its first-priority lien on substantially all assets of the Reorganized Debtor, including, without limitation, the Debtor\'s timberlands, sawmill facilities, equipment, inventory, accounts receivable, and other property.
285	>
286	> \(d\) **Other Terms.** All other material terms of the Senior Secured Credit Facility shall remain substantially unchanged as reflected in the Amended Credit Agreement, to be filed as part of the Plan Supplement.
287	
288	First Meridian Bank, N.A. has consented to the treatment described herein, subject to the execution and delivery of the Amended Credit Agreement in form and substance satisfactory to First Meridian. The collateral securing the First Meridian Secured Claim has a value that exceeds the amount of the First Meridian Secured Claim under both the low-end and midpoint total enterprise value scenarios set forth in the Clearview Valuation (\$385 million to \$430 million), thereby confirming that the First Meridian Secured Claim is fully secured within the meaning of section 506(a) of the Bankruptcy Code. No Cash distribution shall be made to First Meridian on the Effective Date; rather, the obligation of the Reorganized Debtor to First Meridian shall remain outstanding on the amended terms described herein.
289	
290	**Section 4.3 --- Class 3: Second Lien Note Claim (Timberline)**
291	
292	Class 3 consists of the Second Lien Note Claim of Timberline Capital Partners, LLC in the face amount of \$95 million, arising under the Second Lien Notes issued by the Debtor on September 14, 2021. Class 3 is Impaired under the Plan. In full and final satisfaction, settlement, release, and discharge of the Second Lien Note Claim, the holder thereof (Timberline Capital Partners, LLC) shall receive the following:
293	
294	> \(a\) **Cash Payment.** Cash in the amount of \$35 million, payable on the Effective Date; plus
295	>
296	> \(b\) **Equity Distribution.** Fifty-five percent (55%) of the New Common Equity of the Reorganized Debtor (subject to dilution by the Management Incentive Plan), in satisfaction of \$60 million of the Second Lien Note Claim.
297	
298	The remaining balance of the Second Lien Note Claim (\$95 million less \$35 million Cash less \$60 million in equity value = \$0) shall be fully discharged and released upon the Effective Date, together with all related indentures, security agreements, and ancillary documents governing the Second Lien Notes.
299	
300	The equity allocation set forth in clause (b) above is based on the Clearview Valuation, which establishes a midpoint total enterprise value of \$407.5 million for the Debtor. After deducting the reinstated First Meridian Secured Claim of \$261.4 million, the residual equity value attributable to the Reorganized Debtor is approximately \$146.1 million. The fifty-five percent (55%) allocation of New Common Equity to Timberline reflects the agreed value exchange for the \$60 million equity conversion component of the Second Lien Note Claim treatment. The Plan Sponsor has agreed that the equity allocation set forth herein represents a fair and reasonable resolution of the Second Lien Note Claim in light of the estimated going-concern value of the Reorganized Debtor and the relative priorities of Claims in the capital structure.
301	
302	Timberline\'s consent to this treatment is a material condition to the effectiveness of this Plan. Timberline has indicated its support for the Plan, subject to the satisfaction of the conditions precedent set forth in Article IX and the execution and delivery of definitive documentation in form and substance reasonably acceptable to Timberline. The Second Lien Notes and all related indentures, agreements, and security documents shall be cancelled on the Effective Date, and the obligations of the Debtor thereunder shall be discharged, subject only to the distributions provided for in this Section 4.3.
303	
304	**Section 4.4 --- Class 4: General Unsecured Claims**
305	
306	Class 4 consists of all General Unsecured Claims against the Debtor. Class 4 is Impaired under the Plan. Each holder of an Allowed General Unsecured Claim shall receive, in full and final satisfaction, settlement, release, and discharge of such Claim, its Pro Rata share of the Unsecured Creditor Recovery Pool in the amount of \$18.7 million in Cash, representing an estimated recovery of approximately 10.0 cents on the dollar (\$18.7 million ÷ \$187 million = 10.0%). Distributions to Class 4 shall be made as follows:
307	
308	> \(a\) **Initial Distribution.** Fifty percent (50%) of each holder\'s Pro Rata share (approximately \$9.35 million in the aggregate) shall be distributed in Cash on the Effective Date or as soon as practicable thereafter.
309	>
310	> \(b\) **Deferred Distribution.** Fifty percent (50%) of each holder\'s Pro Rata share (approximately \$9.35 million in the aggregate) shall be distributed in Cash on the first anniversary of the Effective Date or as soon as practicable thereafter.
311	
312	No interest shall accrue or be payable on the deferred payment described in clause (b) above during the period from the Effective Date to the date of such distribution. General Unsecured Claims include, without limitation, trade claims, contract rejection damages claims (to the extent allowed), deficiency claims, litigation claims, and other unsecured obligations of the Debtor. The aggregate amount of General Unsecured Claims is estimated to be approximately \$187 million, which includes, among others, the following significant claims held by members of the Committee:
313	
314	> • Northway Paper Corp.: \$14.2 million (trade claim)
315	>
316	> • Deschutes Equipment Leasing Co.: \$8.7 million (unsecured deficiency claim)
317	>
318	> • Columbia River Transport LLC: \$6.1 million (trade claim)
319	>
320	> • Inland Fiber Supply, Inc.: \$4.9 million (trade claim)
321	>
322	> • Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC): \$11.3 million (pension-related claim)
323	
324	The Debtor believes that the Plan provides the best available recovery for holders of General Unsecured Claims. As set forth in the Liquidation Analysis attached hereto as Exhibit A, in a hypothetical Chapter 7 liquidation, holders of General Unsecured Claims would receive an estimated recovery of approximately 3% to 5% of their Allowed Claims. The Plan\'s proposed recovery of 10.0% significantly exceeds the estimated Chapter 7 recovery and satisfies the \"best interests\" test under section 1129(a)(7) of the Bankruptcy Code.
325	
326	**Section 4.5 --- Class 5: Intercompany Claims**
327	
328	Class 5 consists of all Intercompany Claims. Class 5 is Impaired under the Plan. On the Effective Date, all Intercompany Claims shall be adjusted, reinstated, contributed, set off, or discharged, in whole or in part, as determined by the Reorganized Debtor in its sole and absolute discretion and in a manner consistent with the best interests of the Reorganized Debtor, without any further action by the holders thereof or approval of the Bankruptcy Court. Because holders of Class 5 Claims are receiving no distribution on account of such Claims, they are deemed to have rejected the Plan and are not entitled to vote.
329	
330	**Section 4.6 --- Class 6: Existing Equity Interests**
331	
332	Class 6 consists of all existing Equity Interests in the Debtor, including all issued and outstanding shares of common stock, preferred stock, options, warrants, conversion rights, and any other rights to acquire equity in the Debtor, whether or not transferable and whether or not exercisable. Class 6 is Impaired under the Plan. On the Effective Date, all existing Equity Interests in the Debtor shall be cancelled, annulled, and extinguished, and shall be of no further force or effect. Holders of existing Equity Interests shall receive no distribution or other consideration under the Plan on account of such Interests. Because holders of Class 6 Interests are receiving no distribution, they are deemed to have rejected the Plan and are not entitled to vote. The cancellation of existing Equity Interests is a necessary component of the restructuring contemplated by the Plan and is consistent with the priorities established by the Bankruptcy Code.
333	
334	**Section 4.7 --- Class 7: Section 510(b) Claims**
335	
336	Class 7 consists of all Claims against the Debtor that are subject to subordination under section 510(b) of the Bankruptcy Code, including, without limitation, claims for damages arising from the purchase or sale of a security of the Debtor, or claims for reimbursement, indemnification, or contribution on account of such damages. Class 7 is Impaired under the Plan. Holders of Class 7 Claims shall receive no distribution or other consideration under the Plan on account of such Claims. Because holders of Class 7 Claims are receiving no distribution, they are deemed to have rejected the Plan and are not entitled to vote.
337	
338	**[ARTICLE V --- MEANS FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PLAN]{.underline}**
339	
340	**Section 5.1 --- Continued Corporate Existence and Vesting of Assets**
341	
342	On the Effective Date, the Debtor shall continue in existence as Reorganized Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. under and pursuant to the laws of the State of Delaware. All property of the Estate, including all assets, rights, claims, defenses, and causes of action, shall vest in the Reorganized Debtor free and clear of all Claims, liens, charges, encumbrances, and interests of creditors and equity interest holders, except as otherwise expressly provided in this Plan or the Confirmation Order. From and after the Effective Date, the Reorganized Debtor may operate its businesses and may use, acquire, and dispose of property and settle and compromise Claims and Interests without supervision or approval by the Bankruptcy Court and free of any restrictions of the Bankruptcy Code or the Bankruptcy Rules. The Reorganized Debtor shall continue to operate all of the Debtor\'s businesses, including:
343	
344	> \(a\) Timberland harvesting operations across approximately 340,000 acres in the States of Oregon and Washington;
345	>
346	> \(b\) Sawmill operations at the Bend, Oregon facility located at 62400 Boyd Acres Road, Bend, OR 97701;
347	>
348	> \(c\) Sawmill operations at the Centralia, Washington facility located at 1105 North Pearl Street, Centralia, WA 98531;
349	>
350	> \(d\) The laminated veneer lumber (LVL) manufacturing plant
