24	
25	For the avoidance of doubt, the \$35 million Cash payment to satisfy the Class 3 Cash distribution will be funded by Timberline Capital Partners, LLC and paid to the Reorganized Debtor (or directly to satisfy the Second Lien Note Claim, as applicable). The remaining Effective Date distributions --- consisting of Administrative Claims, Priority Tax Claims, Priority Non-Tax Claims, and the first installment of the Unsecured Creditor Recovery Pool --- shall be funded from the Debtor\'s Cash on hand and available liquidity. The financial projections attached hereto as Exhibit B demonstrate that the Reorganized Debtor will have sufficient Cash and liquidity to fund all required distributions on the Effective Date and to meet its ongoing obligations, thereby satisfying the feasibility requirement of section 1129(a)(11) of the Bankruptcy Code.
26	
27	**Section 5.3 --- Issuance of New Common Equity**
28	
29	On the Effective Date, the Reorganized Debtor shall be authorized to issue the New Common Equity in accordance with the Governance Documents. The authorized shares of New Common Equity shall be issued as follows:
30	
31	> \(a\) Fifty-five percent (55%) of the New Common Equity shall be issued to Timberline Capital Partners, LLC in satisfaction of the equity conversion component of the Class 3 treatment described in Section 4.3 hereof (subject to dilution by the Management Incentive Plan).
32	>
33	> \(b\) The remaining forty-five percent (45%) of the New Common Equity shall be held by the Reorganized Debtor as authorized but unissued shares, subject to the reserve for the Management Incentive Plan described in Section 5.7 hereof.
34	
35	The issuance of the New Common Equity pursuant to this Plan shall be exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and any applicable state or local securities laws, pursuant to section 1145 of the Bankruptcy Code. The New Common Equity shall not be listed on any national securities exchange. All recipients of New Common Equity shall receive such equity subject to the terms of the Governance Documents and any applicable shareholders\' agreement or registration rights agreement to be included in the Plan Supplement.
36	
37	**Section 5.4 --- Corporate Governance of the Reorganized Debtor**
38	
39	On the Effective Date, the amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws of the Reorganized Debtor (the \"Governance Documents\") shall become effective. The initial board of directors of the Reorganized Debtor (the \"New Board\") shall consist of five (5) members, as follows:
40	
41	> \(a\) Three (3) directors designated by Timberline Capital Partners, LLC;
42	>
43	> \(b\) One (1) director designated by the Committee; and
44	>
45	> \(c\) One (1) independent director mutually selected by Timberline Capital Partners, LLC and the Committee.
46	
47	Each member of the New Board shall serve an initial term of two (2) years from the Effective Date, subject to the provisions of the Governance Documents regarding removal, resignation, and the filling of vacancies. The identities of the proposed members of the New Board shall be disclosed in the Plan Supplement no later than fourteen (14) days prior to the Confirmation Hearing. The Governance Documents shall be substantially in the forms included in the Plan Supplement and shall contain customary provisions for a privately held Delaware corporation, including provisions regarding indemnification of directors and officers and limitation of director liability to the fullest extent permitted by the General Corporation Law of the State of Delaware.
48	
49	**Section 5.5 --- Cancellation of Existing Securities and Agreements**
50	
51	On the Effective Date, except as otherwise expressly provided in this Plan: (a) all existing Equity Interests in the Debtor, including all shares of common stock, preferred stock, options, warrants, and other rights to acquire equity, shall be cancelled, annulled, and extinguished, and shall be of no further force or effect; (b) the Second Lien Notes and all related indentures, notes, security agreements, guarantees, and ancillary documents shall be cancelled and discharged, subject to the distributions provided under Class 3 of this Plan; and (c) all obligations of the Debtor under any cancelled instruments, indentures, or agreements shall be discharged and released. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Senior Secured Credit Facility shall not be cancelled but shall be amended and restated as provided in Section 4.2 and Section 5.6 of this Plan. The cancellation of existing securities and agreements shall not alter the obligation of the Reorganized Debtor to make distributions as provided in this Plan.
52	
53	**Section 5.6 --- Senior Secured Credit Facility Amendment**
54	
55	On the Effective Date, the Debtor and First Meridian Bank, N.A. shall enter into the Amended Credit Agreement reflecting the following terms:
56	
57	> \(a\) Extension of the maturity date from June 2028 to June 2031;
58	>
59	> \(b\) Reduction of the applicable interest rate from SOFR + 425 basis points to SOFR + 350 basis points;
60	>
61	> \(c\) Continuation of First Meridian\'s first-priority lien on substantially all assets of the Reorganized Debtor; and
62	>
63	> \(d\) Such other terms as are substantially consistent with the existing Senior Secured Credit Facility.
64	
65	First Meridian Bank, N.A. has consented in principle to the amended terms described herein, subject to the negotiation and execution of the Amended Credit Agreement in form and substance satisfactory to First Meridian. The Amended Credit Agreement shall be filed with the Bankruptcy Court as part of the Plan Supplement no later than fourteen (14) days prior to the Confirmation Hearing. All liens and security interests securing the obligations under the Amended Credit Agreement shall continue in full force and effect without the need for any further action by the Reorganized Debtor or First Meridian.
66	
67	**Section 5.7 --- Management Incentive Plan**
68	
69	On or promptly after the Effective Date, the Reorganized Debtor shall adopt the Management Incentive Plan, reserving ten percent (10%) of the New Common Equity (on a fully diluted basis) for grants to post-emergence management and key employees of the Reorganized Debtor. The Management Incentive Plan shall have the following material terms:
70	
71	> \(a\) **Equity Pool.** Ten percent (10%) of the New Common Equity shall be reserved for issuance under the MIP.
72	>
73	> \(b\) **Vesting Schedule.** Awards under the MIP shall vest ratably at twenty-five percent (25%) per year over a four (4)-year period from the date of grant, subject to continued employment and such other vesting conditions as the board of directors of the Reorganized Debtor may determine.
74	>
75	> \(c\) **Dilution.** The MIP equity pool shall dilute all holders of New Common Equity on a pro rata basis, including Timberline\'s fifty-five percent (55%) allocation.
76	>
77	> \(d\) **Administration.** The specific award amounts, participants, exercise prices or grant values, and other terms of awards under the MIP shall be determined by the board of directors of the Reorganized Debtor in its sole discretion following the Effective Date.
78	>
79	> \(e\) **Plan Supplement.** The term sheet for the MIP shall be filed as part of the Plan Supplement no later than fourteen (14) days prior to the Confirmation Hearing.
80	
81	The adoption of the MIP is necessary to attract, retain, and incentivize key management personnel of the Reorganized Debtor in the post-emergence period and is an essential component of the Debtor\'s restructuring strategy.
82	
83	**Section 5.8 --- Key Employee Retention Bonuses**
84	
85	The Reorganized Debtor shall assume and honor the key employee retention bonus obligations totaling \$3.4 million covering twelve (12) senior employees of the Debtor. Such retention bonuses were approved by the Debtor\'s board of directors prior to the Petition Date and are critical to maintaining operational continuity through the reorganization process and the post-emergence period. The retention bonus obligations include payments to the Debtor\'s chief operating officer, chief financial officer, vice presidents of operations, and other senior personnel whose continued employment is essential to the operation of the Debtor\'s timberland harvesting operations, sawmill facilities, and the Eugene LVL plant. The Reorganized Debtor shall pay the retention bonuses in accordance with their original terms, and such obligations shall constitute assumed obligations of the Reorganized Debtor on and after the Effective Date. The Debtor submits that the retention bonus program is necessary to ensure the stability and continuity of the Debtor\'s management team, which in turn is essential to the successful implementation of the Plan and the maximization of value for all creditors.
86	
87	**Section 5.9 --- Litigation Trust and Avoidance Actions**
88	
89	On the Effective Date, a Litigation Trust shall be established pursuant to the Litigation Trust Agreement for the purpose of investigating, prosecuting, and resolving Avoidance Actions and other causes of action belonging to the Estate that are preserved for the benefit of the Reorganized Debtor. The material terms of the Litigation Trust shall be as follows:
90	
91	> \(a\) **Funding.** The Litigation Trust shall be funded with an initial Cash contribution of \$500,000 from the Reorganized Debtor on the Effective Date, to be used for the investigation, prosecution, and resolution of Avoidance Actions.
92	>
93	> \(b\) **Litigation Trustee.** A Litigation Trustee shall be appointed by the Reorganized Debtor, with the consent of the Committee (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed). The identity of the proposed Litigation Trustee shall be disclosed in the Plan Supplement.
94	>
95	> \(c\) **Estimated Recoveries.** Based upon the Debtor\'s preliminary analysis, the estimated recoverable preference claims total approximately \$9.5 million. There can be no assurance, however, that the Litigation Trust will recover all or any portion of such amount.
96	>
97	> \(d\) **Distribution of Proceeds.** Net proceeds of Avoidance Actions (after payment of the Litigation Trustee\'s fees and expenses and the costs of prosecuting such actions) shall be retained by the Reorganized Debtor and shall inure to the benefit of the Reorganized Debtor\'s estate and all stakeholders generally.
98	>
99	> \(e\) **Standing.** The Reorganized Debtor shall have standing to pursue all Avoidance Actions post-Effective Date through the Litigation Trust, and the Litigation Trustee shall have authority to investigate, prosecute, compromise, settle, or abandon any Avoidance Action in the exercise of its reasonable business judgment.
100	>
101	> \(f\) **Termination.** The Litigation Trust shall terminate upon the earlier of (i) the resolution of all Avoidance Actions (whether by final judgment, settlement, or abandonment) or (ii) the third anniversary of the Effective Date, unless extended by order of the Bankruptcy Court upon motion of the Litigation Trustee.
102	
103	The Litigation Trust Agreement shall be substantially in the form included in the Plan Supplement and shall contain such other provisions as are customary for litigation trusts established in Chapter 11 cases, including provisions regarding reporting, compensation of the Litigation Trustee, and indemnification.
104	
105	**Section 5.10 --- Preservation of Causes of Action**
106	
107	In accordance with section 1123(b)(3)(B) of the Bankruptcy Code, the Reorganized Debtor shall retain and may enforce, sue on, settle, or compromise (or decline to do so) all causes of action of the Debtor and the Estate, including, without limitation, all Avoidance Actions, whether arising before or after the Petition Date, in any court or other tribunal, including, without limitation, in an adversary proceeding filed in the Chapter 11 Case. The Reorganized Debtor\'s or Litigation Trust\'s right to commence, prosecute, or settle any such cause of action shall not be impaired or otherwise limited by the Plan, the Disclosure Statement, or the Confirmation Order. No entity may rely on the absence of a specific reference in this Plan, the Disclosure Statement, or the Plan Supplement to any particular cause of action as an indication that the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, or the Litigation Trust will not pursue such cause of action.
108	
109	**Section 5.11 --- Exemption from Certain Transfer Taxes**
110	
111	Pursuant to section 1146(a) of the Bankruptcy Code, the issuance, distribution, transfer, or exchange of any property pursuant to, in contemplation of, or in connection with this Plan, or the issuance, distribution, transfer, or exchange of any debt, equity, or other instrument or security pursuant to, in contemplation of, or in connection with this Plan, including, without limitation, the issuance of the New Common Equity, the execution and delivery of the Amended Credit Agreement, and any transfers of property to the Reorganized Debtor or the Litigation Trust, shall not be subject to any document recording tax, stamp tax, conveyance fee, intangibles or similar tax, mortgage tax, real estate transfer tax, mortgage recording tax, or other similar tax or governmental assessment, and the Confirmation Order shall direct the appropriate state or local governmental officials or agents to forgo the collection of any such tax or governmental assessment and to accept for filing and recordation any of the foregoing instruments or other documents without the payment of any such tax or governmental assessment.
112	
113	**[ARTICLE VI --- PROVISIONS GOVERNING DISTRIBUTIONS]{.underline}**
114	
115	**Section 6.1 --- Distribution Dates**
116	
117	Distributions to holders of Allowed Claims under this Plan shall be made on the Effective Date, or as soon as practicable thereafter, except as otherwise provided herein. Distributions to holders of Disputed Claims that subsequently become Allowed Claims shall be made in accordance with Section 7.3. The deferred distribution to holders of Class 4 General Unsecured Claims (the second installment of fifty percent (50%) of each holder\'s Pro Rata share) shall be made on the first anniversary of the Effective Date, or as soon as practicable thereafter. In the event that any Distribution Date falls on a day that is not a Business Day, the applicable distribution shall be made on the next succeeding Business Day.
118	
119	**Section 6.2 --- Distributions by the Disbursing Agent**
120	
121	The Reorganized Debtor, or such other entity as the Reorganized Debtor may designate, shall serve as the Disbursing Agent for all distributions required under this Plan. All distributions shall be made by the Disbursing Agent in accordance with the terms of this Plan and the Confirmation Order. The Disbursing Agent shall not be required to give any bond or surety or other security for the performance of its duties unless otherwise ordered by the Bankruptcy Court. The Disbursing Agent shall be indemnified and held harmless by the Reorganized Debtor for any acts or omissions taken in good faith in connection with the distributions required under this Plan.
122	
123	**Section 6.3 --- Manner of Payment**
124	
125	Cash distributions under this Plan shall be made, at the election of the Disbursing Agent, by check, wire transfer, automated clearing house (ACH) transfer, or other customary means of payment. Distributions of New Common Equity shall be made by book entry notation or, if requested by the recipient, by physical stock certificates. All distributions shall be deemed made when deposited in the United States mail, first class postage prepaid, when sent by wire transfer or ACH, or when otherwise delivered in a manner customary for distributions of the applicable type.
126	
127	**Section 6.4 --- Undeliverable or Unclaimed Distributions**
128	
129	If any distribution under this Plan is undeliverable (including distributions returned by the United States Postal Service as undeliverable) or remains unclaimed for a period of ninety (90) days after the applicable Distribution Date, such distribution shall be deemed unclaimed. Any holder of an Allowed Claim that does not assert a claim for an undeliverable or unclaimed distribution within such ninety (90)-day period shall have its Claim for such distribution discharged, and the amount of such distribution shall revert to and become the property of the Reorganized Debtor, and such holder\'s Claim shall be forever barred and discharged. Nothing in this Section 6.4 shall require the Disbursing Agent to attempt to locate any holder of an Allowed Claim.
130	
131	**Section 6.5 --- Disputed Claims Reserve**
132	
133	On or as soon as practicable after the Effective Date, the Disbursing Agent shall establish a reserve (the \"Disputed Claims Reserve\") for distributions on account of Disputed Claims. The Disputed Claims Reserve shall consist of Cash in an amount equal to the Pro Rata share of distributions that would be payable to holders of Disputed Claims if such Disputed Claims were Allowed in their full face amounts (or such lesser amounts as estimated by the Bankruptcy Court pursuant to section 502(c) of the Bankruptcy Code). Cash held in the Disputed Claims Reserve shall be deposited in a segregated, interest-bearing account maintained by the Disbursing Agent, and interest earned on such account shall be the property of the Reorganized Debtor. Upon the allowance or disallowance of any Disputed Claim by a Final Order, the Disbursing Agent shall make distributions to the holder of such Allowed Claim in accordance with the Plan, or return the reserved Cash to the Reorganized Debtor in the case of disallowance, as applicable.
134	
135	**Section 6.6 --- De Minimis Distributions**
136	
137	No Cash distribution of less than fifty dollars (\$50.00) shall be made under this Plan. Any amounts not distributed by reason of this Section 6.6 shall revert to and become the property of the Reorganized Debtor.
138	
139	**Section 6.7 --- Setoffs and Recoupment**
140	
141	The Debtor and the Reorganized Debtor may, but shall not be required to, set off against any Allowed Claim and the distributions to be made pursuant to this Plan on account thereof, any claims, rights, and causes of action of any nature whatsoever that the Debtor, the Estate, or the Reorganized Debtor may hold against the holder of such Allowed Claim, pursuant to section 553 of the Bankruptcy Code or applicable non-bankruptcy law. Neither the failure to set off nor the allowance of any Claim under this Plan shall constitute a waiver or release by the Debtor, the Estate, or the Reorganized Debtor of any such claims, rights, and causes of action that the Debtor, the Estate, or the Reorganized Debtor may possess against such holder.
142	
143	**Section 6.8 --- Allocation of Distributions Between Principal and Interest**
144	
145	All distributions under this Plan shall be allocated first to the principal amount of the applicable Allowed Claim and then, to the extent the distribution exceeds the principal amount, to any interest accrued thereon. This allocation shall apply for all purposes, including federal, state, and local tax purposes.
146	
147	**[ARTICLE VII --- TREATMENT OF DISPUTED CLAIMS]{.underline}**
148	
149	**Section 7.1 --- Objections to Claims**
150	
151	After the Effective Date, the Reorganized Debtor shall have the exclusive right and authority to file, settle, compromise, withdraw, or otherwise resolve objections to Claims, except that the Litigation Trustee shall have the authority to prosecute and resolve Avoidance Actions on behalf of the Litigation Trust. All objections to Claims must be filed with the Bankruptcy Court and served on the holders of such Claims no later than one hundred eighty (180) days after the Effective Date, unless such deadline is extended by order of the Bankruptcy Court upon motion of the Reorganized Debtor. The filing of an objection to a Claim shall render such Claim a Disputed Claim until such time as the objection is resolved by a Final Order or by agreement of the parties.
152	
153	**Section 7.2 --- Estimation of Claims**
154	
155	The Debtor or the Reorganized Debtor may, at any time, request that the Bankruptcy Court estimate any Disputed Claim pursuant to section 502(c) of the Bankruptcy Code for purposes of allowance, distribution, or voting, regardless of whether the Debtor or the Reorganized Debtor has previously objected to such Claim or whether the Bankruptcy Court has ruled on any such objection. The Bankruptcy Court shall retain jurisdiction to estimate any Disputed Claim at any time during the litigation concerning the objection to such Claim, including during the pendency of any appeal relating to any such objection.
156	
157	**Section 7.3 --- No Distributions Pending Allowance**
158	
159	No distributions shall be made under this Plan on account of a Disputed Claim until such Claim becomes an Allowed Claim by Final Order or by agreement of the parties. Upon allowance, the holder of such newly Allowed Claim shall receive distributions in accordance with the provisions of this Plan applicable to such Claim.
160	
161	**[ARTICLE VIII --- EXECUTORY CONTRACTS AND UNEXPIRED LEASES]{.underline}**
162	
163	**Section 8.1 --- Assumption of Executory Contracts and Unexpired Leases**
164	
165	On the Effective Date, each Executory Contract and Unexpired Lease listed on Exhibit C hereto as \"Assumed\" shall be assumed by the Reorganized Debtor pursuant to sections 365(a) and 1123(b)(2) of the Bankruptcy Code. Any monetary defaults under assumed Executory Contracts and Unexpired Leases shall be cured in accordance with Section 8.3 hereof. The assumption of each such Executory Contract or Unexpired Lease shall be effective as of the Effective Date, and each such contract or lease shall vest in the Reorganized Debtor in accordance with Section 5.1 hereof. Key assumed contracts include, among others, the following:
166	
167	> \(a\) **Timber Supply Agreement** dated March 15, 2019, between Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. and Olympic Forest Resources LLC, with an annual value of approximately \$22 million per year. The assumption of this agreement is critical to the continued operation of the Centralia, Washington sawmill facility.
168	>
169	> \(b\) Such other Executory Contracts and Unexpired Leases as are listed on Exhibit C as \"Assumed.\"
170	
171	The Debtor\'s determination to assume any Executory Contract or Unexpired Lease shall be subject to the approval of the Bankruptcy Court. Any non-debtor counterparty to an assumed Executory Contract or Unexpired Lease that disputes the proposed cure amount or the Debtor\'s ability to provide adequate assurance of future performance may file an objection with the Bankruptcy Court prior to the Confirmation Hearing.
172	
173	**Section 8.2 --- Rejection of Executory Contracts and Unexpired Leases**
174	
175	On the Effective Date, each Executory Contract and Unexpired Lease listed on Exhibit C hereto as \"Rejected\" shall be rejected by the Debtor pursuant to sections 365(a) and 1123(b)(2) of the Bankruptcy Code. The Debtor\'s determination to reject any Executory Contract or Unexpired Lease shall be subject to the business judgment standard --- that is, the Debtor exercises sound business judgment in determining that the rejection of such contract or lease is in the best interests of the Estate and its creditors. Key rejected contracts include, among others, the following:
176	
177	> \(a\) **Equipment Maintenance Agreement** dated July 1, 2020, between Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. and PacWest Industrial Services, with an annual value of approximately \$1.8 million per year. The Debtor has determined, in the exercise of its business judgment, that the rejection of this agreement is in the best interests of the Estate because the services provided thereunder can be obtained from alternative providers at a lower cost.
178	>
179	> \(b\) Such other Executory Contracts and Unexpired Leases as are listed on Exhibit C as \"Rejected.\"
180	
181	Any Claims arising from the rejection of an Executory Contract or Unexpired Lease shall be treated as General Unsecured Claims in Class 4 and shall be subject to the provisions of this Plan governing such Claims, including the applicable bar date for filing rejection damages claims set forth in Section 8.4.
182	
183	**Section 8.3 --- Cure of Defaults**
184	
185	Any monetary defaults under Executory Contracts and Unexpired Leases to be assumed under this Plan shall be cured through payment of the applicable cure amount in Cash on the Effective Date, or on such other terms as may be agreed upon by the non-debtor counterparty and the Reorganized Debtor. The Debtor shall serve a notice on each non-debtor counterparty to an assumed Executory Contract or Unexpired Lease, setting forth the proposed cure amount, at least twenty-one (21) days prior to the Confirmation Hearing. If a non-debtor counterparty disputes the proposed cure amount, such dispute shall be resolved by the Bankruptcy Court at or before the Confirmation Hearing, unless the parties agree to an alternative resolution procedure.
186	
187	**Section 8.4 --- Bar Date for Rejection Damages Claims**
188	
189	Claims arising from the rejection of an Executory Contract or Unexpired Lease must be filed with the Bankruptcy Court within thirty (30) days after the later of (a) the Effective Date or (b) the date of the order approving the rejection of such contract or lease. Any holder of a rejection damages Claim that fails to file a proof of claim within such thirty (30)-day period shall have its Claim disallowed and forever barred from assertion against the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, or their property.
190	
191	**Section 8.5 --- Contracts Not Listed**
192	
193	Any Executory Contract or Unexpired Lease of the Debtor that is not listed on Exhibit C and that has not been previously assumed or rejected by order of the Bankruptcy Court shall be deemed assumed by the Reorganized Debtor on the Effective Date. The deemed assumption of such contracts and leases shall be subject to the cure provisions of Section 8.3 to the extent applicable.
194	
195	**[ARTICLE IX --- CONDITIONS PRECEDENT TO CONFIRMATION AND THE EFFECTIVE DATE]{.underline}**
196	
197	**Section 9.1 --- Conditions to Confirmation**
198	
199	The following conditions must be satisfied or waived in accordance with Section 9.3 prior to confirmation of this Plan:
200	
201	> \(a\) The Plan complies with all applicable provisions of the Bankruptcy Code, including the requirements of section 1129(a) of the Bankruptcy Code.
202	>
203	> \(b\) The Confirmation Order is in form and substance reasonably acceptable to the Debtor, First Meridian Bank, N.A., and Timberline Capital Partners, LLC.
204	>
205	> \(c\) The Disclosure Statement has been approved by the Bankruptcy Court as containing adequate information within the meaning of section 1125 of the Bankruptcy Code.
206	>
207	> \(d\) All Plan Supplement documents, including the Governance Documents, the Amended Credit Agreement, the MIP term sheet, and the Litigation Trust Agreement, have been filed with the Bankruptcy Court.
208	>
209	> \(e\) The Bankruptcy Court has entered the Confirmation Order in accordance with the terms of this Plan and applicable provisions of the Bankruptcy Code and the Bankruptcy Rules.
210	
211	**Section 9.2 --- Conditions to the Effective Date**
212	
213	The following conditions must be satisfied or waived in accordance with Section 9.3 prior to the occurrence of the Effective Date:
214	
215	> \(a\) The Confirmation Order has become a Final Order, meaning it is no longer subject to appeal, certiorari, or further review, or any such appeals have been resolved in favor of confirmation.
216	>
217	> \(b\) Thirty (30) calendar days have elapsed since the entry of the Confirmation Order, or such shorter period as the Bankruptcy Court may order.
218	>
219	> \(c\) The Amended Credit Agreement between the Reorganized Debtor and First Meridian Bank, N.A. has been executed and delivered and is in full force and effect.
220	>
221	> \(d\) All documents, instruments, and agreements necessary to implement this Plan, including the Governance Documents, the Litigation Trust Agreement, and the MIP term sheet, have been executed and delivered by the parties thereto.
222	>
223	> \(e\) The Reorganized Debtor has sufficient Cash on hand to make all distributions and payments required on the Effective Date as set forth in this Plan, including the distributions described in Sections 2.1, 2.2, 4.1, 4.3(a), and 4.4(a).
224	>
225	> \(f\) The New Common Equity has been duly authorized and issued in accordance with the Governance Documents and this Plan.
226	>
227	> \(g\) The Governance Documents have been adopted and are in full force and effect.
228	>
229	> \(h\) The Litigation Trust has been established and the Litigation Trustee has been appointed in accordance with Section 5.9 of this Plan.
230	>
231	> \(i\) All governmental and regulatory approvals and consents, if any, required for the implementation of this Plan have been obtained.
232	
233	**Section 9.3 --- Waiver of Conditions**
234	
235	The conditions precedent set forth in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 of this Plan may be waived, in whole or in part, by the Debtor (with the consent of Timberline Capital Partners, LLC and First Meridian Bank, N.A., to the extent that such conditions are for the benefit of such parties), without notice, leave, or order of the Bankruptcy Court and without any formal action other than proceeding to confirm or consummate the Plan. The failure of the Debtor to exercise any of the foregoing rights shall not be deemed a waiver of any other rights under the Plan, and each such right shall be deemed an ongoing right that may be asserted at any time.
236	
237	**Section 9.4 --- Effect of Non-Occurrence of Conditions**
238	
239	If the Effective Date does not occur within one hundred twenty (120) days after the Confirmation Date (unless such period is extended by order of the Bankruptcy Court upon motion of the Debtor), then upon motion by the Debtor made before the expiration of such period (as it may have been extended), the Confirmation Order shall be vacated by the Bankruptcy Court, and the Plan shall be null and void in all respects, and nothing contained in the Plan or the Disclosure Statement shall (a) constitute a waiver or release of any Claims by or against, or any Interests in, the Debtor; (b) prejudice in any manner the rights of the Debtor, any holder of a Claim or Interest, or any other entity; or (c) constitute an admission, acknowledgment, offer, or undertaking of any sort by the Debtor, any holder of a Claim or Interest, or any other entity.
240	
241	**[ARTICLE X --- RELEASE, EXCULPATION, AND INJUNCTION PROVISIONS]{.underline}**
242	
243	**Section 10.1 --- Discharge**
244	
245	On the Effective Date, pursuant to section 1141(d) of the Bankruptcy Code, and except as otherwise expressly provided in this Plan or the Confirmation Order, the Debtor shall be discharged from any and all Claims and debts that arose before the Confirmation Date, and all such Claims and debts shall be deemed satisfied, discharged, and released in full, and all holders of Claims and Interests shall be precluded from asserting against the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, the Estate, or any of their respective assets or properties any other or further Claims or Interests based upon any act, omission, transaction, or other activity of any kind or nature that occurred before the Confirmation Date. The discharge granted pursuant to this Section 10.1 operates as an injunction against the commencement or continuation of any action, employment of process, or act to collect, recover, or offset any debt discharged hereunder, to the fullest extent authorized under section 524 of the Bankruptcy Code.
246	
247	**Section 10.2 --- Injunction**
248	
249	On and after the Effective Date, all entities that have held, hold, or may hold Claims against or Interests in the Debtor or the Estate are permanently enjoined from taking any of the following actions against or affecting the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, or the Released Parties, or any of their respective assets or properties, on account of any such Claims or Interests:
250	
251	> \(a\) Commencing, conducting, or continuing in any manner, directly or indirectly, any suit, action, or other proceeding of any kind against the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, or the Released Parties (including, without limitation, any proceeding in a judicial, arbitral, administrative, or other forum);
252	>
253	> \(b\) Enforcing, levying, attaching (including any prejudgment attachment), collecting, or otherwise recovering by any manner or means any judgment, award, decree, or order against the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, or the Released Parties;
254	>
255	> \(c\) Creating, perfecting, or otherwise enforcing in any manner, directly or indirectly, any lien, encumbrance, or other claim against the Reorganized Debtor or any of its assets or properties on account of a discharged Claim or Interest; and
256	>
257	> \(d\) Asserting any right of setoff, subrogation, or recoupment of any kind against any obligation due the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, or any of their respective assets or properties on account of a discharged Claim or Interest.
258	
259	**Section 10.3 --- Exculpation**
260	
261	The Exculpated Parties --- consisting of the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, the Committee, and each of their respective current and former officers, directors, managers, employees, advisors, attorneys, financial advisors, accountants, investment bankers, agents, and professionals, in each case solely in their capacity as such --- shall not have or incur any liability for any act taken or omitted to be taken in connection with, related to, or arising out of the Chapter 11 Case, the formulation, preparation, dissemination, negotiation, or filing of the Plan, the Disclosure Statement, or any contract, instrument, release, or other agreement or document created or entered into in connection with the Plan, the filing of the Chapter 11 Case, the pursuit of confirmation of the Plan, the consummation of the Plan, or the administration of the Plan or the property to be distributed under the Plan, except for liability arising from willful misconduct, gross negligence, or fraud as determined by a Final Order of the Bankruptcy Court or other court of competent jurisdiction. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the Exculpated Parties shall be entitled to reasonably rely upon the advice of counsel with respect to their duties and responsibilities under this Plan. The exculpation provided in this Section 10.3 is an integral part of this Plan and is essential to its implementation.
262	
263	**Section 10.4 --- Third-Party Releases (Consensual and Non-Consensual)**
264	
265	**(a) Released Parties.** As used in this Plan, the \"Released Parties\" shall mean, collectively:
266	
267	> \(i\) the Debtor and the Reorganized Debtor;
268	>
269	> \(ii\) all current and former officers and directors of the Debtor;
270	>
271	> \(iii\) First Meridian Bank, N.A., in its capacities as Senior Secured Lender, administrative agent under the Senior Secured Credit Facility, and DIP Lender;
272	>
273	> \(iv\) Timberline Capital Partners, LLC, in its capacities as holder of the Second Lien Notes and Plan Sponsor;
274	>
275	> \(v\) each of the foregoing\'s respective affiliates, subsidiaries, parents, predecessors, successors, assigns, officers, directors, managers, employees, agents, attorneys, financial advisors, accountants, investment bankers, and professionals; and
276	>

18	
19	On the Effective Date, the Debtor and the Reorganized Debtor, on behalf of themselves, the Estate, and all holders of Claims and Interests, shall forever release and waive all claims, obligations, suits, judgments, damages, demands, debts, rights, causes of action, and liabilities whatsoever against the Released Parties, whether known or unknown, foreseen or unforeseen, existing or hereafter arising, in law, equity, or otherwise, that the Debtor, the Estate, or the Reorganized Debtor would have been legally entitled to assert in their own right (whether individually or collectively) or on behalf of any holder of a Claim or Interest or any other entity, based on or related to, or in any manner arising from, in whole or in part, the Debtor, the Debtor\'s business, the Chapter 11 Case, the Plan, the Disclosure Statement, or any related transaction, agreement, or document; provided, however, that nothing in this Section 10.5 shall release (a) the right of the Reorganized Debtor to enforce the terms of this Plan and the Confirmation Order, or (b) Avoidance Actions preserved under the Litigation Trust pursuant to Section 5.9, which shall be limited to preference claims against non-Released Parties. This release is integral to this Plan and is given by the Debtor and the Reorganized Debtor in consideration of the contributions, distributions, and other benefits provided under the Plan by the Released Parties.
20	
21	**[ARTICLE XI --- CONFIRMATION AND RELATED PROVISIONS]{.underline}**
22	
23	**Section 11.1 --- Confirmation Requirements**
24	
25	The Debtor requests confirmation of this Plan pursuant to section 1129(a) of the Bankruptcy Code. The Debtor believes that the Plan satisfies all applicable requirements of section 1129(a), including:
26	
27	> \(a\) **Section 1129(a)(1): Compliance with the Code.** The Plan complies with all applicable provisions of the Bankruptcy Code, including sections 1122 and 1123.
28	>
29	> \(b\) **Section 1129(a)(2): Proponent Compliance.** The Debtor, as proponent of the Plan, has complied with all applicable provisions of the Bankruptcy Code, including sections 1125 and 1126.
30	>
31	> \(c\) **Section 1129(a)(3): Good Faith.** The Plan has been proposed in good faith and not by any means forbidden by law. The Plan was negotiated at arm\'s length among the Debtor, First Meridian, Timberline, and the Committee.
32	>
33	> \(d\) **Section 1129(a)(4): Payments for Services.** Any payments made or to be made to any person for services or for costs and expenses in connection with the Chapter 11 Case, or in connection with the Plan and incident to the Chapter 11 Case, have been approved by, or are subject to the approval of, the Bankruptcy Court as reasonable.
34	>

51	**Section 11.2 --- Best Interests Test**
52	
53	The Debtor submits that each holder of a Claim in an Impaired Class will receive under this Plan at least as much as such holder would receive in a hypothetical Chapter 7 liquidation of the Debtor. As set forth in detail in the Liquidation Analysis attached hereto as Exhibit A, in a hypothetical Chapter 7 liquidation, the Debtor estimates that: (a) the First Meridian Secured Claim would be satisfied in full from the liquidation of the Debtor\'s assets, even under the low-end scenario; (b) Timberline\'s Second Lien Note Claim would receive a partial recovery, dependent on the liquidation scenario; and (c) holders of General Unsecured Claims would receive an estimated recovery of approximately 3% to 5% of their Allowed Claims. Under this Plan, holders of General Unsecured Claims will receive an estimated recovery of 10.0%, which significantly exceeds the estimated Chapter 7 recovery. 213	**Key Assumptions Underlying Liquidation Values:**
214	
215	The timberlands have been valued at a significant discount to book value because a forced or expedited sale of 340,000 acres in Oregon and Washington would depress pricing materially below the going-concern appraised value. The timber market is characterized by a limited number of potential acquirers capable of purchasing a timberland portfolio of this size, and a fire-sale disposition would likely attract opportunistic buyers at steep discounts. The sawmill facilities in Bend and Centralia have been valued based on comparable industrial facility sales in the Pacific Northwest, with additional discounts applied for the specialized nature of the equipment and the costs associated with environmental compliance and permitting. The LVL plant in Eugene is a purpose-built manufacturing facility with limited alternative use, warranting a significant liquidation discount. Working capital and accounts receivable are estimated at a discount reflecting the collection risk and administrative costs associated with a trustee-administered wind-down. Other assets, including vehicles, mobile equipment, and intellectual property, have been valued based on auction data and comparable transactions.

239	**Notes to the Waterfall:**
240	
241	In the low-end scenario, the total liquidation value of \$276 million is insufficient to satisfy all priority and secured claims. After payment of Chapter 7 Trustee fees (\$8.28 million), estimated wind-down administrative costs (\$15 million --- which are higher than in Chapter 11 due to the complexity and cost of a trustee-administered wind-down of a multi-facility timber operation), Priority Tax Claims (\$3.2 million), Priority Non-Tax Claims (\$2.8 million), and the First Meridian Secured Claim (\$261.4 million), there is a shortfall of approximately \$14.68 million, resulting in no recovery for general unsecured creditors. In this scenario, First Meridian\'s secured claim may be only partially satisfied, although the Debtor believes it is more likely that the low-end scenario would still yield sufficient proceeds to satisfy the First Meridian Secured Claim, given the conservative nature of the low-end estimates.
242	
243	In the midpoint scenario, approximately \$10.95 million would remain for distribution to unsecured creditors after satisfaction of all priority and secured claims. However, this amount must be shared with the Timberline unsecured deficiency claim. Timberline\'s Second Lien Note Claim of \$95 million would receive a partial recovery from its second-priority lien on the Debtor\'s assets, with any deficiency claim participating as a general unsecured claim. Assuming Timberline\'s second lien recovery is approximately \$10 million to \$20 million (depending on the liquidation scenario), the remaining unsecured deficiency claim of \$75 million to \$85 million would dilute the unsecured pool available to other general unsecured creditors. The resulting estimated recovery for general unsecured creditors (other than Timberline\'s deficiency) would be approximately 3% to 5%.
244	
245	In the high-end scenario, approximately \$36.58 million would remain. Even in this scenario, after accounting for Timberline\'s deficiency claim and its dilutive effect on the unsecured pool, general unsecured creditor recoveries would remain materially below the 10.0% recovery provided under the Plan.

44	
45	**[ARTICLE III]{.underline}**
46	
47	**[BACKGROUND OF THE DEBTOR AND EVENTS LEADING TO CHAPTER 11]{.underline}**
48	
49	**Section 3.1 --- Overview of the Debtor\'s Business**
50	
51	Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. is a Delaware corporation headquartered at 1200 SW Morrison Street, Suite 1600, Portland, Oregon 97205. Cascadia is a vertically integrated timber and wood products company engaged in the harvesting, processing, manufacturing, and sale of timber, lumber, and engineered wood products throughout the Pacific Northwest and broader North American markets. The Debtor was incorporated in the State of Delaware in 2004 and has maintained its principal place of business in Portland, Oregon since its inception.
52	
53	The Debtor\'s operations span the entire value chain of the timber and wood products industry, from standing timber harvesting through finished product manufacturing and distribution. Cascadia manages and harvests timber from approximately **340,000 acres** of timberland located across Oregon and Washington, including holdings in the Cascade Range, the Coast Range, and the southern Puget Sound lowlands. These timberland holdings represent the Debtor\'s core asset base and provide a sustainable supply of raw materials for the Debtor\'s downstream manufacturing operations.
54	
55	The Debtor\'s manufacturing operations are conducted through three principal facilities:
56	
57	> **(a)** **Bend Sawmill** --- Located at 62400 Boyd Acres Road, Bend, Oregon 97701, the Bend Sawmill is a dimensional lumber mill capable of producing approximately 220 million board feet of lumber per year. The Bend facility processes primarily Douglas fir and ponderosa pine harvested from the Debtor\'s Central Oregon timberland holdings and from third-party log purchases.
58	>
59	> **(b)** **Centralia Sawmill** --- Located at 1105 North Pearl Street, Centralia, Washington 98531, the Centralia Sawmill is a dimensional lumber facility with production capacity of approximately 180 million board feet per year. The Centralia facility processes primarily Douglas fir and western hemlock. A significant portion of the raw material supply for the Centralia mill is sourced through a long-term timber supply agreement with Olympic Forest Resources LLC, valued at approximately \$22 million per year, which provides the facility with a stable and cost-effective log supply independent of the Debtor\'s owned timberland.
60	>
61	> **(c)** **Eugene LVL Plant** --- Located at 3880 West 11th Avenue, Eugene, Oregon 97402, the Eugene facility manufactures laminated veneer lumber (\"LVL\"), an engineered wood product used principally in residential and commercial construction for headers, beams, and other structural applications. The Eugene plant has an annual production capacity of approximately 85 million cubic feet of LVL.
62	
63	The Debtor\'s business is organized into three principal operating segments: (i) timber harvesting and log sales, which involves the harvesting of standing timber from the Debtor\'s owned timberland and the sale of logs to the Debtor\'s own mills and to third-party purchasers; (ii) lumber manufacturing, encompassing the Bend and Centralia sawmill operations and the production and sale of dimensional lumber; and (iii) engineered wood products, consisting of the production and sale of LVL products from the Eugene facility. In the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, the Debtor\'s pre-petition annual revenue was approximately **\$412 million**, with the lumber manufacturing segment representing approximately 55% of total revenue, timber harvesting and log sales approximately 28%, and engineered wood products approximately 17%.
64	
65	The Debtor employs approximately **1,400 full-time employees** across all facilities and its Portland corporate headquarters, including approximately 580 employees at the Bend Sawmill, approximately 420 employees at the Centralia Sawmill, approximately 280 employees at the Eugene LVL Plant, and approximately 120 employees at corporate headquarters. The Debtor\'s workforce includes a significant number of skilled and specialized employees with expertise in timber harvesting, lumber grading, mill operations, and engineered wood product manufacturing.
66	
67	Cascadia operates within the highly competitive Pacific Northwest timber and wood products industry, competing with both large integrated producers and smaller regional operators. Key competitive factors include timberland quality and location, log supply reliability, manufacturing efficiency, customer relationships, product quality, and freight and logistics costs. The Pacific Northwest region is one of the most productive timber-growing regions in the world, and the Debtor\'s extensive timberland holdings and vertically integrated operations provide it with a competitive cost advantage relative to non-integrated peers.
68	
69	**Section 3.2 --- Capital Structure**
70	
71	As of the Petition Date, the Debtor\'s capital structure consisted of the following principal obligations:
72	
73	**Senior Secured Credit Facility.** The Debtor is party to a senior secured credit facility (the \"Senior Secured Credit Facility\") in the aggregate principal amount of **\$275 million**, consisting of (i) an asset-based revolving loan facility (the \"ABL Facility\") and (ii) a term loan facility (the \"Term Loan\"), in each case with **First Meridian Bank, N.A.** (\"First Meridian\") as administrative agent and collateral agent for the lenders thereunder. The Senior Secured Credit Facility is secured by a first-priority lien on substantially all of the Debtor\'s assets, including the Debtor\'s timberland holdings, real property, equipment, inventory, accounts receivable, intellectual property, and general intangibles. As of the Petition Date (March 3, 2025), the aggregate outstanding balance under the Senior Secured Credit Facility was approximately **\$261.4 million**, consisting of approximately \$186.0 million outstanding under the Term Loan and approximately \$75.4 million outstanding under the ABL Facility. The Senior Secured Credit Facility bears interest at a floating rate equal to the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (\"SOFR\") plus **425 basis points** per annum, with a SOFR floor of 0.50%. The original maturity date of the Senior Secured Credit Facility is **June 2028**.
74	
75	**Second Lien Notes.** In connection with the dividend recapitalization transaction described in Section 3.3 below, the Debtor issued **\$95 million** in aggregate principal amount of second lien secured notes (the \"Second Lien Notes\") to **Timberline Capital Partners, LLC** (\"Timberline\"), a Delaware limited liability company. The Second Lien Notes are secured by a second-priority lien on substantially all of the Debtor\'s assets, subordinate in all respects to the first-priority liens securing the Senior Secured Credit Facility pursuant to an intercreditor agreement between First Meridian and Timberline dated September 14, 2021. The Second Lien Notes bear interest at a fixed rate of 9.50% per annum, payable semi-annually, with a maturity date of September 2026. As of the Petition Date, the full principal amount of **\$95 million** remained outstanding under the Second Lien Notes, together with accrued and unpaid interest.
76	
77	**General Unsecured Obligations.** In addition to the secured obligations described above, the Debtor has approximately **\$187 million** in total general unsecured claims. These general unsecured obligations include trade debt owed to suppliers and vendors, equipment lease deficiency claims, logistics and transportation obligations, raw materials vendor claims, and unfunded pension obligations owed to the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation. The general unsecured claims are not secured by any lien on the Debtor\'s assets and are structurally junior to the Senior Secured Credit Facility and the Second Lien Notes.
78	
79	In total, the Debtor\'s **total scheduled liabilities** as of the Petition Date were approximately **\$637 million** (consisting of \$261.4 million in senior secured debt, \$95 million in second lien debt, approximately \$187 million in general unsecured obligations, and approximately \$93.6 million in other liabilities including accrued interest, employee obligations, and contingent claims). The Debtor\'s **total scheduled assets** at book value were approximately **\$489 million**, resulting in a balance-sheet deficit of approximately \$148 million.
80	
81	**Equity Interests.** All outstanding equity interests in the Debtor are held by a combination of the Whitaker family (approximately 40%), which founded the predecessor business in 1987, and various institutional equity holders who acquired their interests in connection with private placements and secondary transactions.
82	
83	**Section 3.3 --- The 2021 Dividend Recapitalization**
84	
85	On **September 14, 2021**, the Debtor completed a dividend recapitalization transaction (the \"2021 Dividend Recapitalization\"). In this transaction, Timberline Capital Partners, LLC purchased the \$95 million in Second Lien Notes described in Section 3.2 above. The proceeds from the issuance of the Second Lien Notes were used primarily to fund a one-time special dividend to the Debtor\'s existing equity holders in the aggregate amount of approximately \$88 million, with the remaining proceeds applied to transaction costs and fees.
86	
87	The 2021 Dividend Recapitalization increased the Debtor\'s total funded indebtedness from approximately \$275 million (consisting solely of the Senior Secured Credit Facility) to approximately \$370 million (consisting of the Senior Secured Credit Facility and the Second Lien Notes). At the time the transaction was consummated, it was supported by a solvency opinion delivered by an independent financial advisory firm, which concluded that the Debtor was solvent on both a balance-sheet and cash-flow basis immediately after giving effect to the transaction.
88	
89	However, the substantial increase in leverage resulting from the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization significantly reduced the Debtor\'s financial flexibility and contributed materially to the financial distress that ultimately precipitated the Chapter 11 filing, as described in greater detail in Section 3.4 below. The additional \$95 million in funded debt, together with the associated interest obligations, consumed a disproportionate share of the Debtor\'s operating cash flow and left the company with inadequate reserves to absorb the operational and market headwinds that emerged in 2022 and 2023.
90	
91	**Section 3.4 --- Events Leading to Chapter 11 Filing**
92	
93	The Debtor\'s financial distress and ultimate need to seek relief under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code resulted from the convergence of three principal factors:
94	
95	> **(a) Wildfire Losses (2023).** During the summer and fall of 2023, significant wildfires affected portions of the Debtor\'s Oregon timberland holdings, particularly in the Central Cascade region east of the Bend Sawmill. The wildfires damaged or destroyed harvestable timber on approximately 28,000 acres, representing roughly 8% of the Debtor\'s total timberland holdings. While the Debtor maintained property insurance on its facilities, its timberland was only partially insured, and the Debtor incurred substantial uninsured losses estimated at approximately \$35 million in standing timber value. In addition to the direct economic loss, the wildfire damage impaired the Debtor\'s future harvesting capacity on the affected acreage and required significant remediation and replanting expenditures that further strained the Debtor\'s liquidity.
96	>
97	> **(b) Decline in Housing Starts.** Beginning in late 2022 and continuing through 2024, the U.S. housing market experienced a sustained decline in housing starts driven by elevated mortgage interest rates and broader macroeconomic uncertainty. Total U.S. housing starts declined from approximately 1.55 million units in 2022 to approximately 1.35 million units in 2024, representing a decline of approximately 13%. This reduction in homebuilding activity directly reduced demand for the Debtor\'s dimensional lumber and LVL products, compressing sales volumes and margins at both sawmills and at the Eugene LVL Plant. Average realized prices for dimensional lumber declined approximately 22% from their mid-2022 peaks, significantly impacting the Debtor\'s revenue and profitability.
98	>
99	> **(c) Over-Leveraged Capital Structure.** As described in Section 3.3, the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization left the Debtor with an unsustainable capital structure. Following the recapitalization, the Debtor\'s total debt-to-EBITDA ratio exceeded 5.5x, a level that left insufficient financial cushion to absorb the operational headwinds from the wildfire losses and the housing market downturn. Annual debt service obligations---including interest payments on both the Senior Secured Credit Facility and the Second Lien Notes---consumed approximately 35% of the Debtor\'s operating cash flow, leaving inadequate liquidity for capital expenditures, working capital needs, and the wildfire remediation costs described above.
100	
101	By the fourth quarter of 2024, the Debtor was unable to meet certain financial maintenance covenants under the Senior Secured Credit Facility, including the minimum debt service coverage ratio and the maximum leverage ratio. In January 2025, the Debtor and First Meridian entered into a forbearance agreement pursuant to which First Meridian agreed to forbear from exercising its default remedies through March 15, 2025, subject to certain milestones and conditions. The Debtor utilized the forbearance period to engage financial and legal restructuring advisors and to explore strategic alternatives, including an out-of-court restructuring, a sale process, and an in-court reorganization.
102	
103	Ultimately, the Debtor and its advisors determined that a Chapter 11 reorganization provided the optimal path to preserve the going-concern value of the business, maximize recoveries for all creditor constituencies, and emerge with a sustainable capital structure. On **March 3, 2025** (the \"Petition Date\"), Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. filed a voluntary petition for relief under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Oregon, initiating the case captioned *In re Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc.*, Case No. 25-30412-MLE, assigned to the Honorable Margaret L. Eriksson.
104	
105	**Section 3.5 --- Significant Events During the Chapter 11 Case**
106	
107	Since the Petition Date, a number of significant events have occurred in the Chapter 11 case:
108	
109	**Appointment of the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors.** On **March 17, 2025**, the United States Trustee for the District of Oregon appointed the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors (the \"Committee\") pursuant to Section 1102 of the Bankruptcy Code. The Committee is comprised of the following members, each of which holds a significant general unsecured claim against the Debtor\'s estate:
110

276	
277	The Debtor retained **Clearview Valuation Services, LLC** (\"Clearview\") to prepare an independent valuation of the Debtor as a going concern for purposes of the Plan and this Disclosure Statement. Clearview\'s complete valuation analysis is attached as **Exhibit A** to this Disclosure Statement and is summarized in the Clearview Valuation Summary Report filed separately with the Court. The following is a summary of Clearview\'s conclusions.
278	
279	Clearview employed three principal valuation methodologies: (i) a discounted cash flow (\"DCF\") analysis based on the financial projections prepared by Pinecrest Advisory Group, LLC; (ii) a comparable public company analysis utilizing trading multiples of publicly traded timber and wood products companies; and (iii) a comparable transaction analysis utilizing transaction multiples from precedent mergers and acquisitions in the timber and forest products sector. Each methodology was weighted based on Clearview\'s professional judgment and the availability and reliability of the relevant data inputs.
280	
281	Based on the foregoing analysis, Clearview estimated the **total enterprise value (\"TEV\")** of the Reorganized Debtor to be in the range of **\$385 million to \$430 million**, with a **midpoint TEV of \$407.5 million**. The Debtor believes that the midpoint TEV of \$407.5 million is the most appropriate basis for the Plan\'s claims waterfall analysis and recovery calculations.
282	
283	The claims waterfall analysis at the midpoint TEV is as follows:
284	
285	> Total Enterprise Value (midpoint): **\$407.5 million**
286	>
287	> Less: Senior Secured Claim (First Meridian, reinstated at par): **(\$261.4 million)**
288	>
289	> **Residual Equity Value: \$146.1 million** (\$407.5M − \$261.4M = \$146.1M)
290	>
291	> Equity allocation to Timberline Capital Partners, LLC (per Plan): **55%** of residual equity value = \$146.1 million × 55% = **\$80.355 million**
292	>
293	> Remaining equity value (45%): \$146.1 million × 45% = **\$65.745 million** (available for the Management Incentive Plan and Reorganized Debtor treasury)
294	
295	The residual equity value of \$146.1 million is sufficient to support the equity-based distributions contemplated by the Plan. Timberline Capital Partners, LLC, as the holder of 55% of the new common equity, would hold equity with an implied value of approximately \$80.355 million at the midpoint TEV, in addition to the \$35 million cash payment it will receive on the Effective Date. Clearview\'s valuation report provides sensitivity analyses across a range of assumptions regarding discount rates, terminal growth rates, and comparable company and transaction multiples.

381	**Section 11.1 --- Overview**
382	
383	Pursuant to Section 1129(a)(7) of the Bankruptcy Code, commonly known as the \"best interests of creditors\" test, the Bankruptcy Court may not confirm the Plan unless each holder of a claim or interest in an impaired class that has not accepted the Plan will receive or retain under the Plan, on account of such claim or interest, property of a value, as of the effective date of the Plan, that is not less than the amount such holder would receive if the Debtor were liquidated under Chapter 7 of the Bankruptcy Code.
384	
385	To assist the Court and parties in interest in evaluating whether the Plan satisfies the best interests test, the Debtor retained Clearview Valuation Services, LLC to prepare a liquidation analysis estimating the recoveries that creditors and interest holders would receive in a hypothetical Chapter 7 liquidation of the Debtor\'s assets. The complete liquidation analysis is attached as part of **Exhibit A** to this Disclosure Statement. The following is a summary of Clearview\'s liquidation analysis and conclusions.
386	
387	**Section 11.2 --- Estimated Liquidation Values**
388	
389	Clearview estimated the orderly liquidation values of the Debtor\'s principal asset categories as follows:
390	
391	**Table: Estimated Liquidation Values**
392	
393	  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
394	  **Asset Category**                       **Book Value**    **Estimated Liquidation Value (Low)**   **Estimated Liquidation Value (High)**
395	  ---------------------------------------- ----------------- --------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------
396	  Timberland (340,000 acres)               \$285M            \$195M                                  \$225M
397	
398	  Sawmill --- Bend, OR                     \$62M             \$28M                                   \$35M
399	
400	  Sawmill --- Centralia, WA                \$58M             \$26M                                   \$33M
401	
402	  LVL Plant --- Eugene, OR                 \$44M             \$18M                                   \$24M
403	
404	  Inventory & Accounts Receivable          \$31M             \$22M                                   \$26M
405	
406	  Other Assets (equipment, vehicles, IP)   \$9M              \$4M                                    \$6M
407	
408	  **Total**                                **\$489M**        **\$293M**                              **\$349M**
409	  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
410	
411	The liquidation values represent orderly liquidation values, meaning the estimated proceeds that would be realized if the Debtor\'s assets were sold in an organized and supervised manner over a reasonable period of time (estimated at six to twelve months), rather than in a forced or distressed sale. Clearview\'s estimates reflect the significant discount to going-concern and book values that would result from the loss of the Debtor\'s vertically integrated operational platform, customer relationships, workforce, and timber supply agreements in a liquidation scenario.
412	
413	Estimated Chapter 7 administrative and liquidation costs --- including the fees and expenses of a Chapter 7 trustee (at the statutory maximum of 3% of distributions), wind-down costs associated with the cessation of operations and the sale of assets, environmental remediation and decommissioning costs, and professional fees for the Chapter 7 estate --- are estimated at approximately **\$18 million to \$24 million**.
414	
415	After deducting estimated liquidation costs, the **net liquidation proceeds** are estimated to range from approximately **\$269 million** (low scenario: \$293M − \$24M) to approximately **\$331 million** (high scenario: \$349M − \$18M).
416	
417	**Section 11.3 --- Distribution Waterfall in Liquidation**
418	
419	The following is a summary of the estimated distribution waterfall under a hypothetical Chapter 7 liquidation, based on the net liquidation proceeds estimated above:
420	
421	**Senior Secured Claims (First Meridian Bank, N.A.) --- \$261.4 million.** First Meridian\'s senior secured claim would be entitled to first-priority distribution from the net liquidation proceeds. Under both the low and high liquidation scenarios, the net liquidation proceeds (\$269 million and \$331 million, respectively) would be sufficient to pay First Meridian\'s \$261.4 million claim in full, although in the low scenario the margin is narrow. In extreme stress scenarios below the low range, First Meridian could potentially face a deficiency, but Clearview considers such scenarios unlikely.
422	
423	**Administrative and Priority Claims --- approximately \$18.5 million.** After satisfaction of the senior secured claim, the next layer in the waterfall consists of administrative claims (\$12.5 million), priority tax claims (\$3.2 million), and priority non-tax claims (\$2.8 million), totaling approximately \$18.5 million.
424	
425	**Residual Available for Second Lien and Unsecured Creditors:**
426	
427	> *Low Scenario:* Net liquidation proceeds of \$269 million, less \$261.4 million for the senior secured claim, less \$18.5 million for administrative and priority claims = **negative \$10.9 million**. Under the low liquidation scenario, there would be insufficient proceeds to pay all administrative, priority, and second lien claims in full. Timberline\'s \$95 million second lien claim would receive only a partial recovery, and holders of general unsecured claims would receive **\$0**.
428	>
429	> *High Scenario:* Net liquidation proceeds of \$331 million, less \$261.4 million for the senior secured claim, less \$18.5 million for administrative and priority claims = **\$51.1 million** available for distribution to Timberline\'s \$95 million second lien claim. Timberline would receive a partial recovery of approximately **53.8%** (\$51.1M ÷ \$95M). After full exhaustion of the \$51.1 million residual by the second lien claim, no funds would remain for distribution to holders of general unsecured claims. General unsecured creditors would receive **\$0**.
430	
431	**Conclusion.** Under both the low and high liquidation scenarios, holders of Allowed General Unsecured Claims (Class 6) would receive **\$0** in a hypothetical Chapter 7 liquidation. The Plan\'s proposed recovery of **10.0%** --- representing \$18.7 million in aggregate distributions on \$187 million in estimated general unsecured claims --- therefore exceeds the liquidation floor by the full amount of the distribution. The best interests of creditors test under Section 1129(a)(7) of the Bankruptcy Code is accordingly satisfied with respect to Class 6 and all other impaired classes under the Plan.
432	
433	Similarly, Timberline Capital Partners, LLC would receive a recovery of only 0% to approximately 53.8% on its \$95 million second lien claim in a liquidation, compared to the aggregate consideration of \$35 million in cash plus 55% of the new common equity of the Reorganized Debtor under the Plan, which the Debtor believes represents a materially superior recovery.
434	
435	*\[Section XII omitted --- Alternatives to the Plan\]*
436	
437	**[ARTICLE XIII]{.underline}**
438	
439	**[RISK FACTORS]{.underline}**
440	
441	The following is a summary of certain risk factors that should be considered by creditors and other parties in interest in evaluating the Plan and this Disclosure Statement. This summary is not exhaustive, and creditors should consult with their own advisors regarding the risks specific to their individual circumstances.
442	
443	**Section 13.1 --- Risks Related to the Business**
444	
445	**Commodity Price Volatility.** Lumber and wood product prices are subject to significant volatility driven by housing market conditions, seasonal demand patterns, international trade dynamics, and supply disruptions (including those caused by natural disasters, insect infestations, and regulatory actions). A sustained decline in lumber prices below the levels assumed in the Debtor\'s financial projections could reduce revenue and EBITDA below projected levels, potentially impairing the Reorganized Debtor\'s ability to service its debt obligations and fund the deferred unsecured creditor distribution.
446	
447	**Wildfire Risk.** The Debtor\'s timberland holdings in Oregon and Washington are located in regions that are subject to significant and increasing wildfire risk, particularly during the summer and fall fire seasons. As demonstrated by the 2023 wildfire losses described in Section 3.4, wildfire events can result in substantial uninsured losses and impairment of the Debtor\'s timberland asset base. The Debtor maintains property insurance on its manufacturing facilities but has only limited insurance coverage for standing timber losses. Additional wildfire events could materially reduce the value of the Debtor\'s timberland, impair future harvesting capacity, and require significant remediation expenditures.
448	
449	**Housing Market Conditions.** The Debtor\'s revenue is materially dependent on the level of U.S. housing starts, which drives demand for dimensional lumber, engineered wood products, and other building materials. Continued elevated interest rates or a broader economic downturn could depress housing starts below the levels assumed in the Debtor\'s financial projections, reducing demand for the Debtor\'s products and compressing sales volumes and margins.
450	
451	**Customer Concentration.** A significant portion of the Debtor\'s revenue is derived from a limited number of customers, including large homebuilders, wholesale distributors, and retail building materials dealers. The loss of one or more major customers, whether due to competitive pressures, customer financial difficulties, or changes in procurement practices, could materially affect the Debtor\'s revenue and profitability.
452	
453	**Key Employee Retention.** The success of the reorganized business is materially dependent on the retention of certain key senior employees who possess specialized expertise in timberland management, sawmill operations, engineered wood product manufacturing, and the Pacific Northwest timber market. The Plan provides for retention bonuses totaling **\$3.4 million** for **12 senior employees** to mitigate the risk of key employee departures during and following the reorganization. These individuals represent the core operational leadership of the Debtor and possess institutional knowledge and industry relationships that would be difficult and costly to replace. The competitive labor market for experienced timber industry executives has intensified in recent years, and the Debtor is aware of active recruitment efforts by competitor firms. Notwithstanding the Retention Bonuses, there can be no assurance that all key employees will remain with the Reorganized Debtor following the Effective Date, and the departure of one or more key employees could adversely affect the Reorganized Debtor\'s operations and financial performance.
454	
455	**Section 13.2 --- Risks Related to the Plan**
456	
457	**Confirmation Risk.** The Plan is subject to confirmation by the Bankruptcy Court under Section 1129 of the Bankruptcy Code, which requires, among other things, acceptance by at least one impaired class of claims. If one or more impaired classes reject the Plan, the Debtor would need to seek confirmation under the \"cramdown\" provisions of Section 1129(b), which impose additional requirements including the absolute priority rule and the requirement that the Plan not discriminate unfairly against any rejecting class. There can be no assurance that the Bankruptcy Court will confirm the Plan under either the consensual or cramdown standards.
458	
459	**Feasibility Risk.** The Debtor\'s ability to make all distributions required under the Plan depends on the accuracy of the financial projections prepared by Pinecrest Advisory Group, LLC. Actual cash flows may differ materially from projections due to the risks and uncertainties described in this Article XIII. The Debtor projects **\$68 million** in cash at emergence, providing an estimated **\$5.15 million** cushion above the **\$62.85 million** in required Effective Date distributions. While the Debtor believes that this cushion, together with the availability of the exit revolving credit facility and projected post-emergence cash flow, is adequate to fund all Plan obligations, there can be no assurance that actual cash at emergence will equal or exceed the projected amount, or that post-emergence operating results will be sufficient to fund the deferred distribution of \$9.35 million to Class 6 creditors on the first anniversary of the Effective Date.
460	
461	**Timberline Support Risk.** The Plan depends on the continued support and participation of Timberline Capital Partners, LLC as the Plan\'s equity sponsor. Timberline has committed to convert \$60 million of its second lien claim to new equity and to accept a \$35 million cash payment in full and final satisfaction of its \$95 million claim. If Timberline were to withdraw its support --- whether due to a material adverse change in the Debtor\'s business, a dispute regarding the terms of the Plan, or any other reason --- the Debtor would need to seek an alternative Plan sponsor or an alternative restructuring transaction, which could significantly delay the Debtor\'s emergence from Chapter 11 and could reduce recoveries to all creditor classes.
462	
463	**Release and Exculpation Risk.** The Plan includes broad third-party release and exculpation provisions that are designed to facilitate the reorganization by providing certainty and finality to all parties. However, third-party release provisions in Chapter 11 plans are subject to legal challenge, and the law regarding the enforceability of non-consensual third-party releases varies among judicial circuits and continues to evolve. If the Bankruptcy Court declines to approve the release provisions, or if such provisions are subsequently invalidated on appeal, certain parties (including Timberline Capital Partners, LLC, the Debtor\'s officers and directors, and First Meridian Bank, N.A.) could face post-confirmation litigation exposure, which could affect their willingness to support the Plan and could adversely affect the Reorganized Debtor\'s operations and financial condition.
464	
465	**Interest Rate Risk.** The reinstated Senior Secured Credit Facility bears interest at a floating rate of SOFR + 350 basis points. Increases in SOFR above the levels assumed in the Debtor\'s financial projections could raise the Reorganized Debtor\'s annual debt service costs above projected levels, reducing free cash flow available for other obligations and working capital needs.
466	
467	**Avoidance Action Recovery Risk.** The Litigation Trust established under the Plan is expected to pursue approximately **\$9.5 million** in identified preference claims and other avoidance actions. However, actual recoveries from avoidance action litigation may be substantially less than the estimated amount due to litigation risks, settlement dynamics, the potential assertion of affirmative defenses by defendants, and the costs of prosecution. Avoidance action recoveries are retained by the Reorganized Debtor\'s estate and are not dedicated to any specific creditor class, and there can be no guarantee that any particular level of recovery will be achieved.
468	
469	**Regulatory and Environmental Risk.** The Debtor\'s timber operations are subject to extensive federal and state environmental regulations, including the federal Endangered Species Act, the Oregon Forest Practices Act, the Washington Forest Practices Act, the Clean Water Act, and various other environmental statutes and regulations. Changes in regulatory requirements --- including changes in the listing status of threatened or endangered species that inhabit the Debtor\'s timberland, restrictions on harvesting practices, or the imposition of new environmental compliance obligations --- could increase the Debtor\'s operating costs, restrict its harvesting capacity, or otherwise adversely affect the Reorganized Debtor\'s financial performance.
470	
471	**Section 13.3 --- Risks Related to Voting and Acceptance**
472	
473	The Plan requires acceptance by at least one impaired class of claims in order to be confirmed on a consensual basis under Section 1129(a)(8) of the Bankruptcy Code. A class of claims is deemed to have accepted the Plan if creditors holding at least two-thirds in amount and more than one-half in number of the voting claims in that class vote to accept.
474	
475	Class 6 (General Unsecured Claims) is the primary impaired voting class whose acceptance is being solicited. Class 5 (Timberline Capital Partners, LLC) is also impaired and entitled to vote, and Timberline has committed to vote in favor of the Plan. If Class 6 rejects the Plan, the Debtor intends to seek cramdown confirmation under Section 1129(b), relying on the acceptance of Class 5 as the requisite accepting impaired class. In a cramdown scenario, the Debtor must demonstrate that the Plan does not discriminate unfairly and is \"fair and equitable\" with respect to each rejecting class. The absolute priority rule under Section 1129(b)(2)(B) provides that, with respect to a rejecting class of unsecured claims, no holder of any junior claim or interest may receive or retain any property under the Plan on account of such junior claim or interest unless each senior rejecting class has been paid in full or has consented to such treatment.
476	
477	Creditors holding Class 6 claims are strongly encouraged to vote in favor of the Plan, which provides a recovery of 10.0 cents on the dollar --- a materially better outcome than the \$0 recovery that would result from a Chapter 7 liquidation, as demonstrated by the liquidation analysis set forth in Article XI.
478	
479	*\[Sections XIV through XVI omitted --- Recommendation, Conclusion, and Exhibits\]*

paras=re.findall(r"<w:p[ >].*?</w:p>",d,re.S)
out=[]
def runtext(r):
    t="".join(re.findall(r"<w:t[^>]*>([^<]*)</w:t>",r))
    if "<w:tab/>" in r: t=" | "+t
    st = re.search(r"<w:strike(?: w:val=\"(?:1|true)\")?/>",r) is not None
    return t, st
for p in paras:
    s=""
    for m in re.finditer(r"(<w:ins [^>]*>.*?</w:ins>)|(<w:r[ >].*?</w:r>)",p,re.S):
        if m.group(1):
            t="".join(runtext(r)[0] for r in re.findall(r"<w:r[ >].*?</w:r>",m.group(1),re.S))
            s+="[[INS:"+t+"]]"
        else:
            t,st=runtext(m.group(2))
            s+= ("~~"+t+"~~") if (st and t) else t
    s=s.replace("~~~~","")
    if s.strip(): out.append(html.unescape(s))
open("/workspace/txt/red_marked.txt","w").write("\n".join(out))
print(len(out), sum(x.count("~~") for x in out)//2)
EOF
