1	IN THE UNITED STATES BANKRUPTCY COURT
2	FOR THE DISTRICT OF OREGON
3	Case No. 25-30412-MLE Chapter 11
4	Hon. Margaret L. Eriksson
5	SECOND AMENDED PLAN OF REORGANIZATION OF CASCADIA TIMBER HOLDINGS, INC., A DELAWARE CORPORATION, PURSUANT TO CHAPTER 11 OF THE UNITED STATES BANKRUPTCY CODE
6	Filed: April 28, 2025
7	REDLINE MARKUP — Proposed Modifications by the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors Transmitted May 19, 2025
8	Prepared by:
9	WHITFIELD & CRANE LLP 900 SW Fifth Avenue, Suite 2400 Portland, Oregon 97204 Telephone: (503) 555-8200 Facsimile: (503) 555-8201 Sandra K. Morrow, Lead Partner
10	Redline Markup by:
11	RIDGELINE STRAUSS LLP 111 SW Columbia Street, Suite 1500 Portland, Oregon 97201 Telephone: (503) 555-3100 Facsimile: (503) 555-3101 David Hwan Chen, Lead Partner
12	TRACKED CHANGES LEGEND
13	This document reflects the proposed modifications of the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors (the "Committee") to the Second Amended Plan of Reorganization filed by the Debtor on April 28, 2025 (Dkt. No. 387). Because this document is transmitted in a format that simulates tracked changes for review purposes, the following conventions are used throughout:
14	•  Deletions are shown as: ~~strikethrough text~~
15	•  Insertions are shown as: **[[INS:new text]]**
16	•  Margin comments are shown as: [COMMENT – D. Chen: comment text]
17	All tracked changes are attributed to David Hwan Chen, Ridgeline Strauss LLP, and bear the date of May 19, 2025. This redline contains a total of forty-seven (47) proposed modifications, comprising twelve (12) substantive changes, sixteen (16) conforming or semi-substantive changes, fifteen (15) cosmetic or definitional clarifications, and four (4) corrections to Exhibit C. The Committee reserves all rights to propose additional modifications at or before the Disclosure Statement hearing currently scheduled for June 12, 2025.
18	Right-click to update Table of Contents
19	ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS AND RULES OF INTERPRETATION
20	Section 1.1 — Definitions
21	Unless the context otherwise requires, the following terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them below when used in this Second Amended Plan of Reorganization (together with all Exhibits and the Plan Supplement, the "Plan"). Any term used herein that is not defined but is used in the Bankruptcy Code or the Bankruptcy Rules shall have the meaning ascribed to such term therein.
22	"Administrative Claim" means a Claim for costs and expenses of administration of the Chapter 11 Case that is entitled to priority under Sections 503(b) and 507(a)(2) of the Bankruptcy Code, including, without limitation, (a) any actual and necessary costs and expenses incurred after the Petition Date of preserving the Estate and operating the business of the Debtor, (b) Professional Fee Claims, and (c) all fees and charges assessed against the Estate pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1930 **[[INS:, including, without limitation, Claims arising under Sections 503(b) and 507(a)(2) of the Bankruptcy Code]]**.
23	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Adding express cross-reference to the applicable Bankruptcy Code sections for completeness.]
24	"Allowed Claim" means a Claim or any portion thereof (a) that has been allowed by a Final Order of the Bankruptcy Court, (b) that is listed in the Schedules as liquidated, non-contingent, and undisputed, and for which no proof of claim has been filed and no objection has been interposed, (c) as to which no objection to the allowance thereof has been interposed within the applicable period of limitation fixed by the Plan, the Bankruptcy Code, the Bankruptcy Rules, or the Bankruptcy Court, or (d) that is allowed pursuant to the terms of the Plan. An Allowed Claim shall be net of any amounts previously paid on account of such Claim. The allowance of a Claim shall be determined in accordance with ~~Section 5.1~~ **[[INS:Article V, Section 5.1]]** of this Plan and applicable provisions of the Bankruptcy Code and Bankruptcy Rules.
25	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Reformatting internal cross-reference for precision.]
26	"Avoidance Actions" means any and all claims, actions, proceedings, or causes of action arising under Sections 502, 510, 541, 542, 543, 544, 545, 547, 548, 549, 550, 551, 552, or 553 of the Bankruptcy Code, or under similar or related state or federal statutes and common law, including fraudulent transfer, fraudulent conveyance, and preference actions.
27	**[[INS:"Avoidance Action Recovery Pool" means all net proceeds recovered by the Litigation Trust from Avoidance Actions (as defined in Section 7.4), after deduction of reasonable costs and expenses of prosecution (including Litigation Trustee fees, attorneys' fees, expert fees, and other litigation expenses), which proceeds shall be distributed exclusively to holders of Allowed General Unsecured Claims in accordance with Section 4.3(c).]]**
28	[COMMENT – D. Chen: New defined term needed for the avoidance action proceeds distribution mechanism proposed by the Committee. Estimated recovery: $9.5M gross based on identified preference claims. The Committee believes this term is necessary to clarify the exclusive distribution mechanism for these recoveries.]
29	"Ballot" means ~~the form of ballot~~ **[[INS:the official form of ballot approved by the Bankruptcy Court]]** accompanying the Disclosure Statement upon which holders of Claims in impaired Classes entitled to vote shall indicate their acceptance or rejection of the Plan.
30	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Clarifying that the ballot must be the Court-approved form.]
31	"Bankruptcy Code" means title 11 of the United States Code, 11 U.S.C. §§ 101–1532, as now in effect or hereafter amended, and as applicable to the Chapter 11 Case.
32	"Bankruptcy Court" means the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Oregon, or such other court having jurisdiction over the Chapter 11 Case.
33	"Bankruptcy Rules" means the Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure as promulgated by the United States Supreme Court under 28 U.S.C. § 2075, including any Local Bankruptcy Rules of the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Oregon, as now in effect or hereafter amended.
34	"Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, a Sunday, or a day on which commercial banks in Portland, Oregon, are authorized or required by law or executive order to close, including any day on which a federal legal holiday is observed **[[INS:or any other day on which the Bankruptcy Court is closed]]**.
35	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Including Court closure days in the definition of non-Business Days for completeness.]
36	"Cash" means legal tender of the United States of America or equivalents thereof, including checks, wire transfers, and other immediately available funds.
37	"Chapter 11 Case" means the case commenced by the filing of a voluntary petition for relief under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code by Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. on January 6, 2025, pending before the Bankruptcy Court and assigned Case No. 25-30412-MLE.
38	"Claim" means a "claim" as defined in Section 101(5) of the Bankruptcy Code, including any right to payment or right to an equitable remedy for breach of performance, whether or not such right is reduced to judgment, liquidated, unliquidated, fixed, contingent, matured, unmatured, disputed, undisputed, legal, equitable, secured, or unsecured.
39	"Class" means a category of Claims or Equity Interests classified pursuant to Article III of this Plan.
40	"Collateral" means any property of the Estate subject to a valid, perfected, and unavoidable Lien to secure the payment of a Claim, to the extent of the value of the interest of the holder of such Claim in such property, as determined pursuant to Section 506(a) of the Bankruptcy Code.
41	"Committee" means the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors appointed in the Chapter 11 Case by the United States Trustee on January 24, 2025, as such committee may be reconstituted from time to time.
42	"Confirmation Date" means **[[INS:the date on which the Clerk of the Bankruptcy Court enters]] the ~~date of entry of the~~ Confirmation Order ~~by the Bankruptcy Court~~ [[INS:on the docket of the Chapter 11 Case]]**.
43	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Clarifying that the Confirmation Date is determined by the docket entry, not the oral ruling.]
44	"Confirmation Order" means the order of the Bankruptcy Court confirming this Plan pursuant to Section 1129 of the Bankruptcy Code.
45	"Debtor" means Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation, as debtor and debtor-in-possession in the Chapter 11 Case.
46	"DIP Facility" means that certain Senior Secured Superpriority Debtor-in-Possession Credit Agreement, dated as of January 15, 2025, by and between the Debtor and First Meridian Bank, N.A., as lender, in the aggregate principal amount of $25,000,000, as approved by the Bankruptcy Court pursuant to interim and final orders entered on January 16, 2025 and February 10, 2025, respectively.
47	"Disclosure Statement" means the Disclosure Statement for the Second Amended Plan of Reorganization of Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc., as approved by the Bankruptcy Court pursuant to Section 1125 of the Bankruptcy Code, together with all exhibits and supplements thereto.
48	"Distribution Agent" means the entity or entities selected by the Reorganized Debtor to make distributions under the Plan, which may be the Reorganized Debtor itself or a third-party disbursing agent.
49	"Effective Date" means the first Business Day on which all conditions precedent to the effectiveness of this Plan set forth in Article IX hereof have been satisfied or waived in accordance with the terms of this Plan. ~~The conditions precedent to the Effective Date are set forth in Section 9.1 of this Plan.~~ **[[INS:The conditions precedent to the Effective Date include: (a) the Confirmation Order shall have become a Final Order; (b) all documents and agreements necessary to implement the Plan shall have been executed and delivered; (c) all governmental and regulatory approvals shall have been obtained; (d) the New Common Equity shall have been issued; (e) the DIP Facility shall have been repaid or converted; and (f) the Reorganized Debtor shall have sufficient Cash on hand to make all required Effective Date distributions, each as more fully set forth in Section 9.1 of this Plan.]]**
50	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Reformatting definition to add clause numbering for each condition precedent. No substantive change to the conditions themselves at this point; the substantive condition change (supplemental disclosure) appears in Article IX.]
51	"Equity Conversion Amount" means the amount of ~~$60,000,000~~ **[[INS:Sixty Million Dollars ($60,000,000)]]** of the Second Lien Note Claims to be converted into New Common Equity on the Effective Date in accordance with Section 4.2 of this Plan.
52	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Spelling out dollar amount for formal consistency.]
53	"Equity Interest" means any equity security (as defined in Section 101(16) of the Bankruptcy Code) in the Debtor, including all issued and outstanding shares of common stock, preferred stock, or other ownership interests in the Debtor, and any rights, warrants, options, or other agreements to acquire an equity security.
54	"Estate" means the estate of the Debtor created pursuant to Section 541 of the Bankruptcy Code upon the commencement of the Chapter 11 Case.
55	"Exhibit" means any exhibit attached to this Plan or filed as part of the Plan Supplement, in each case as such exhibit may be amended, modified, or supplemented from time to time.
56	"Final Order" means an order or judgment of the Bankruptcy Court (or other court of competent jurisdiction) entered on the docket of the Chapter 11 Case that has not been reversed, vacated, stayed, modified, or amended, and as to which (a) the time to appeal, petition for certiorari, or move for a new trial, reargument, or rehearing has expired and no appeal, petition for certiorari, or motion for a new trial, reargument, or rehearing shall then be pending, or (b) if an appeal, writ of certiorari, new trial, reargument, or rehearing thereof has been sought, such order or judgment shall have been affirmed by the highest court to which such order was appealed, or certiorari shall have been denied, or a new trial, reargument, or rehearing shall have been denied or resulted in no modification of such order, and the time to take any further appeal, petition for certiorari, or move for a new trial, reargument, or rehearing shall have expired.
57	"First Meridian" means First Meridian Bank, N.A., a national banking association, in its capacity as agent and lender under the Senior Secured Credit Facility.
58	"General Unsecured Claim" means any Claim against the Debtor that is not an Administrative Claim, a Priority Tax Claim, a Priority Non-Tax Claim, a Senior Secured Claim, a Second Lien Note Claim, or an Intercompany Claim, including, without limitation, trade payables, rejection damages claims, deficiency claims (if any), litigation claims, and other unsecured obligations of the Debtor.
59	"Governmental Unit" means a "governmental unit" as defined in Section 101(27) of the Bankruptcy Code.
60	"Intercompany Claim" means any Claim held by the Debtor against any of its direct or indirect subsidiaries, or held by any direct or indirect subsidiary of the Debtor against the Debtor or any other direct or indirect subsidiary.
61	"Lien" means a "lien" as defined in Section 101(37) of the Bankruptcy Code, including any charge against or interest in property to secure payment of a debt or performance of an obligation.
62	"Litigation Trust" means the trust established pursuant to Section 6.7 of this Plan for the purpose of prosecuting, settling, or otherwise resolving Avoidance Actions and Retained Actions for the benefit of the Estate and, where applicable, for distribution to holders of Allowed General Unsecured Claims.
63	"Management Incentive Plan" or "MIP" means the equity-based incentive compensation plan providing for the issuance of up to ~~10%~~ **[[INS:7%]] of the New Common Equity (on a fully diluted basis) to eligible employees and officers of the Reorganized ~~Debtor~~ [[INS:Company]]**, vesting over four (4) years at a rate of twenty-five percent (25%) per annum, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the MIP term sheet to be included in the Plan Supplement.
64	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Reducing MIP pool from 10% to 7% reduces dilution and benefits unsecured creditors' potential future recovery in the event of a subsequent liquidity event. The Committee believes 7% is a market-standard MIP allocation for a mid-market timber company and is sufficient to incentivize post-emergence management.]
65	"New Common Equity" means the shares of common stock of the Reorganized Debtor, of which ~~55%~~ **[[INS:41.07%]]** shall be issued to Timberline Capital Partners, LLC, on account of the Equity Conversion Amount, subject to dilution by the Management Incentive Plan. The remaining shares of New Common Equity shall be held by the Reorganized Debtor for issuance under the MIP or as otherwise provided herein.
66	[COMMENT – D. Chen: The 55% figure is arithmetically incorrect. Per the Clearview Valuation Summary, TEV midpoint of $407.5M less $261.4M senior secured = $146.1M residual equity value. $60M conversion ÷ $146.1M = 41.07%. This appears to be a mathematical error in the Debtor's Plan, not a substantive disagreement. See Clearview report at pp. 8–9. The Committee requests that the Debtor confirm whether the 55% figure was derived using a different methodology, and if so, to disclose such methodology.]
67	"Person" means an individual, corporation, partnership, limited liability company, joint venture, association, joint stock company, trust, unincorporated organization, **[[INS:governmental entity,]]** or other entity.
68	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Adding "governmental entity" to the defined categories for completeness.]
69	"Petition Date" means January 6, 2025, the date on which the Debtor commenced the Chapter 11 Case by filing a voluntary petition for relief under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code.
70	"Plan Supplement" means the supplement or supplements to this Plan containing certain documents and forms of documents relevant to the implementation and consummation of this Plan, including the forms of the amended certificate of incorporation and bylaws of the Reorganized Debtor, the MIP term sheet, the New Common Equity documentation, and such other documents as may be necessary to effectuate the transactions contemplated by the Plan, **[[INS:all as more fully described in the list of Exhibits attached hereto]]**. The Plan Supplement shall be filed with the Bankruptcy Court at least seven (7) days before the Voting Deadline.
71	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Adding cross-reference to the Exhibit list for completeness.]
72	"Priority Non-Tax Claim" means a Claim entitled to priority under Sections 507(a)(4) or 507(a)(5) of the Bankruptcy Code, including claims for wages, salaries, and employee benefit plan contributions earned within the applicable period prior to the Petition Date.
73	"Priority Tax Claim" means a Claim of a Governmental Unit of the kind entitled to priority in payment under Section 507(a)(8) of the Bankruptcy Code.
74	"Pro Rata" means the proportion that an Allowed Claim in a particular Class bears to the aggregate amount of all Allowed Claims in such Class, including Disputed Claims that have been estimated for distribution purposes.
75	"Professional Fee Claim" means a Claim by a professional person retained by the Debtor or the Committee pursuant to Sections 327, 328, or 1103 of the Bankruptcy Code for compensation and reimbursement of expenses, as allowed by the Bankruptcy Court under Sections 330 and 331 of the Bankruptcy Code.
76	"Released Parties" means, collectively, (a) the Debtor, (b) the Reorganized Debtor, (c) the Committee and each of its members (solely in their capacities as such), (d) all current and former officers and directors of the Debtor, (e) all professionals retained by the Debtor or the Committee in the Chapter 11 Case, and (f) with respect to each of the foregoing, their respective advisors, accountants, attorneys, consultants, and agents, in each case acting in their respective capacities as such **[[INS:; provided, however, that for purposes of the releases set forth in Sections 8.1 and 8.2, "Released Parties" shall not include Timberline Capital Partners, LLC, or its affiliates, officers, directors, members, or agents, with respect to any claims, causes of action, or rights arising out of or related to the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization (as defined in Section 8.1)]]**.
77	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Conforming amendment to the definition of "Released Parties" consistent with the release carve-out set forth in Section 8.1 for the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization claims. The Committee cannot agree to release potential constructive fraudulent transfer claims without a full investigation.]
78	"Reorganized Debtor" ~~means Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc., as reorganized on and after the Effective Date in accordance with the Plan.~~ **[[INS:(also referred to herein as "Reorganized Company") means Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc., as reorganized on and after the Effective Date in accordance with the Plan.]]**
79	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Suggesting "Reorganized Company" as alternative defined term for clarity; we use both interchangeably throughout the Committee's markup.]
80	"Retained Actions" means all claims, causes of action, rights of action, suits, and proceedings of the Debtor or the Estate, whether in law or in equity, whether known or unknown, that the Debtor or the Estate may hold against any Person, other than Avoidance Actions, which shall be retained by and vest in the Reorganized Debtor on the Effective Date.
81	"Schedules" means the schedules of assets and liabilities filed by the Debtor in the Chapter 11 Case pursuant to Section 521(a)(1) of the Bankruptcy Code, as such schedules may have been amended or supplemented from time to time.
82	"Second Lien Note Claims" means all Claims arising under or in connection with the Second Lien Note Purchase Agreement dated September 14, 2021, by and between the Debtor and Timberline Capital Partners, LLC, including all principal, accrued and unpaid interest, fees, expenses, and other obligations thereunder, in the aggregate face amount of approximately Ninety-Five Million Dollars ($95,000,000).
83	"Secured Claim" means a Claim that is secured by a Lien on property in which the Estate has an interest, to the extent of the value of the interest of the holder of such Claim in such property, as determined pursuant to Section 506(a) of the Bankruptcy Code.
84	"Senior Secured Claims" means all Claims arising under or in connection with the Senior Secured Credit Agreement dated June 15, 2018, by and between the Debtor and First Meridian Bank, N.A., as agent, including all principal, accrued and unpaid interest, fees, expenses, and other obligations thereunder, in the aggregate amount of approximately Two Hundred Sixty-One Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars ($261,400,000).
85	"Timberline" means Timberline Capital Partners, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, in its capacity as holder of the Second Lien Note Claims and as the provider of the Equity Conversion Amount.
86	"U.S. Trustee" means the United States Trustee for the District of Oregon.
87	"Unsecured Creditor Recovery Pool" means the aggregate amount of ~~$18,700,000~~ **[[INS:$28,000,000]] to be distributed to holders of Allowed General Unsecured Claims, which shall be distributed as follows: (a) ~~50%~~ [[INS:75%]] of such amount (i.e., ~~$9,350,000~~ [[INS:$21,000,000]]) on the Effective Date, and (b) ~~50%~~ [[INS:25%]] of such amount (i.e., ~~$9,350,000~~ [[INS:$7,000,000]]) on the first anniversary of the Effective Date [[INS:, together with interest accrued thereon at the federal judgment rate (28 U.S.C. § 1961) in effect as of the Confirmation Date (currently 5.24% per annum) from the Effective Date through the date of distribution]]**.
88	[COMMENT – D. Chen: The Committee believes unsecured creditors are entitled to a recovery rate reflecting at minimum 14.97% ($28M ÷ $187M). The Debtor's proposed 10% recovery is inadequate given the total enterprise value and the significant value being conferred on junior classes. The 75/25 front-loading is necessary to reduce creditor execution risk and reflects standard practice in plans where deferred distributions are contemplated. Interest on the deferred portion at the federal judgment rate is standard and compensates creditors for the time value of money. The Committee reserves all rights to seek a higher recovery amount at confirmation.]
89	"Voting Deadline" means the date and time established by the Bankruptcy Court by which all Ballots for the acceptance or rejection of the Plan must be received by the Distribution Agent **[[INS:(5:00 p.m. Pacific Time)]]**, as set forth in the order approving the Disclosure Statement.
90	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Adding specific time zone for the Voting Deadline for clarity.]
91	Section 1.2 — Rules of Interpretation
92	For purposes of this Plan, unless otherwise provided herein: (a) whenever the context requires, terms used herein shall include the plural as well as the singular and the singular as well as the plural; (b) any reference in this Plan to a contract, instrument, release, or other agreement or document being in a particular form or on particular terms and conditions means that such document shall be substantially in such form or substantially on such terms and conditions; (c) any reference in this Plan to an existing document or Exhibit filed or to be filed shall mean such document or Exhibit, as it may have been or may be amended, modified, or supplemented from time to time; (d) unless otherwise specified, all references to Sections are to Sections of this Plan, and all references to Articles are to Articles of this Plan; (e) the words "herein," "hereof," "hereto," "hereunder," and other words of similar import refer to this Plan in its entirety rather than to only a particular portion of this Plan; (f) captions and headings to Articles and Sections are inserted for convenience of reference only, are not a part of this Plan, and shall not be used to interpret this Plan; (g) the word "including" and words of similar import shall mean "including, without limitation"; and (h) the rules of construction set forth in Section 102 of the Bankruptcy Code shall apply to the construction of this Plan.
93	**[[INS:Unless otherwise specified, all references to Sections are to Sections of this Plan and all references to Exhibits are to Exhibits attached hereto or included in the Plan Supplement.]]**
94	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Standard clarifying provision regarding references to Sections and Exhibits.]
95	Section 1.3 — Computation of Time
96	Unless otherwise specifically stated herein, the provisions of Bankruptcy Rule 9006(a) shall apply in computing any period of time prescribed or allowed by this Plan. If the date on which any action is required to be taken under this Plan falls on a day that is not a Business Day, such action shall be required to be taken on the next succeeding Business Day.
97	Section 1.4 — Governing Law
98	Unless a rule of law or procedure is supplied by federal law (including the Bankruptcy Code and the Bankruptcy Rules), and to the extent that this Plan does not otherwise expressly provide for the governance of a particular matter, (a) the laws of the State of Delaware shall govern all matters concerning the corporate governance of the Reorganized Debtor, including the issuance of the New Common Equity, and (b) the laws of the State of Oregon shall govern the construction and interpretation of any contractual provisions contained in or relating to this Plan.
99	ARTICLE II — ADMINISTRATIVE CLAIMS AND PRIORITY CLAIMS
100	Section 2.1 — Administrative Claims
101	Except as otherwise provided in this Plan, each holder of an Allowed Administrative Claim shall receive, in full and final satisfaction, release, and discharge of such Allowed Administrative Claim, Cash in an amount equal to the full unpaid amount of such Allowed Administrative Claim on the Effective Date, or as soon thereafter as is reasonably practicable; provided, however, that Allowed Administrative Claims representing liabilities incurred in the ordinary course of business by the Debtor during the Chapter 11 Case shall be paid in the ordinary course of business in accordance with the terms and conditions of any agreements governing such obligations. The Debtor estimates that total Allowed Administrative Claims will be approximately $12,500,000, consisting of the following categories:
102	(a) Professional Fee Claims. All Allowed Professional Fee Claims, estimated at approximately $8,100,000 in the aggregate, shall be paid in full in Cash on the Effective Date or as soon thereafter as is reasonably practicable following entry of an order of the Bankruptcy Court approving such fees and expenses. All professionals seeking allowance of Professional Fee Claims shall file final fee applications with the Bankruptcy Court no later than sixty (60) days after the Effective Date.
103	(b) U.S. Trustee Fees. All fees payable to the United States Trustee pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1930 through the Effective Date, estimated at approximately $400,000, shall be paid in full in Cash on the Effective Date.
104	(c) Post-Petition Trade Payables. All Allowed Administrative Claims arising from post-petition trade payables incurred in the ordinary course of the Debtor's business, estimated at approximately $4,000,000, shall be paid in full in Cash on the Effective Date or in the ordinary course of business in accordance with the terms and conditions governing such obligations.
105	(d) ~~Retention Bonus Obligations. The Reorganized Debtor shall assume and honor the Key Employee Retention Bonus Program (totaling $3,400,000 for twelve (12) senior employees), which obligations shall constitute Allowed Administrative Claims and shall be paid in accordance with the terms of such program.~~
106	[COMMENT – D. Chen: The retention bonuses totaling $3.4M have not been subjected to § 503(c) scrutiny. Section 503(c)(1) imposes strict requirements on retention transfers to insiders, including evidence of bona fide outside offers. Specifically, § 503(c)(1) requires that the court find that (i) the transfer is essential to retention of the individual because the individual has a bona fide job offer from another business at the same or greater rate of compensation, (ii) the services provided by the individual are essential to the survival of the business, and (iii) the amount of the transfer is not greater than ten times the amount of a similar transfer made to nonmanagement employees. These payments appear to be disguised priority payments benefiting insiders at the expense of unsecured creditors. The Committee reserves all rights to object to these payments under § 503(c) and Section 1129(a)(4).]
107	All requests for payment of Administrative Claims (other than Professional Fee Claims, which shall be subject to the procedures described above) must be filed with the Bankruptcy Court and served on the Reorganized Debtor and its counsel no later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date. Any Administrative Claim for which a request for payment is not timely filed shall be forever barred and discharged.
108	Section 2.2 — Priority Tax Claims
109	Each holder of an Allowed Priority Tax Claim shall receive, in full and final satisfaction, release, and discharge of such Allowed Priority Tax Claim, Cash in an amount equal to the full unpaid amount of such Allowed Priority Tax Claim on the Effective Date, or, at the election of the Debtor, in regular installment payments in accordance with Section 1129(a)(9)(C) of the Bankruptcy Code over a period not to exceed five (5) years after the Petition Date with interest at the rate determined under applicable nonbankruptcy law. The Debtor estimates that total Allowed Priority Tax Claims will be approximately $3,200,000, consisting primarily of state and local property tax obligations and federal and state income tax claims for the pre-petition period.
110	Section 2.3 — Priority Non-Tax Claims
111	Each holder of an Allowed Priority Non-Tax Claim under Sections 507(a)(4) and 507(a)(5) of the Bankruptcy Code shall receive, in full and final satisfaction, release, and discharge of such Allowed Priority Non-Tax Claim, Cash in an amount equal to the full unpaid amount of such Allowed Priority Non-Tax Claim on the Effective Date, or as soon thereafter as is reasonably practicable. The Debtor estimates that total Allowed Priority Non-Tax Claims will be approximately $2,800,000, consisting primarily of pre-petition employee wage claims and employee benefit plan contribution obligations.
112	Section 2.4 — U.S. Trustee Fees
113	All fees payable to the United States Trustee pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6) and any applicable interest thereon shall be paid in full in Cash on the Effective Date and shall continue to be paid by the Reorganized Debtor on a quarterly basis thereafter until the earlier of the closing of the Chapter 11 Case or the entry of an order converting the Chapter 11 Case to a case under Chapter 7 of the Bankruptcy Code. The Debtor estimates that U.S. Trustee fees accrued through the Effective Date will be approximately $400,000.
114	ARTICLE III — CLASSIFICATION OF CLAIMS AND EQUITY INTERESTS
115	Section 3.1 — Summary of Classification
116	Pursuant to Section 1122 of the Bankruptcy Code, the following is a summary of the classification of Claims and Equity Interests under this Plan. Administrative Claims and Priority Claims are not classified pursuant to Section 1123(a)(1) of the Bankruptcy Code and are treated separately in Article II. All Claims and Equity Interests not classified or otherwise treated under Article II are classified as follows:

151	ARTICLE IV — TREATMENT OF CLAIMS AND EQUITY INTERESTS
152	Section 4.1 — Class 1: Senior Secured Claims (First Meridian Bank, N.A.)
153	Each holder of an Allowed Senior Secured Claim in Class 1 shall receive, in full and final satisfaction, release, and discharge of such Allowed Senior Secured Claim, the following treatment: the Senior Secured Claims shall be reinstated with amended terms as follows: (a) the maturity date shall be extended from June 15, 2028 to June 15, 2031; (b) the interest rate shall be reduced from SOFR plus 425 basis points per annum to SOFR plus 350 basis points per annum; (c) the amortization schedule shall be amended as set forth in the amended credit agreement to be included in the Plan Supplement; and (d) all existing Liens securing the Senior Secured Claims shall remain in full force and effect as provided under the Senior Secured Credit Agreement, as amended. The aggregate outstanding principal balance of the Senior Secured Claims is approximately $261,400,000 as of the Petition Date. The Debtor represents that the value of the Collateral securing the Senior Secured Claims exceeds the amount of such Claims based on the Clearview Valuation Summary included in the Disclosure Statement. First Meridian Bank, N.A. has consented to the treatment of its Claims under this Plan. Class 1 is Unimpaired under the Plan and is conclusively presumed to have accepted the Plan pursuant to Section 1126(f) of the Bankruptcy Code. Holders of Class 1 Claims are not entitled to vote on the Plan.
154	Section 4.2 — Class 2: Second Lien Note Claims (Timberline Capital Partners, LLC)
155	Each holder of an Allowed Second Lien Note Claim in Class 2 shall receive, in full and final satisfaction, release, and discharge of such Allowed Second Lien Note Claim, the following treatment:
156	(a) Cash Payment. A Cash payment of Thirty-Five Million Dollars ($35,000,000), payable on the Effective Date; and
157	(b) Equity Conversion. Conversion of Sixty Million Dollars ($60,000,000) of the Second Lien Note Claims (the Equity Conversion Amount) into ~~55%~~ **[[INS:41.07%]]** of the New Common Equity of the Reorganized Debtor (subject to dilution by the Management Incentive Plan).
158	[COMMENT – D. Chen: See comment at definition of "New Common Equity." The 55% figure is mathematically incorrect based on the Debtor's own valuation. $60M ÷ $146.1M residual equity value = 41.07%. The Committee understands that Timberline may disagree with this correction, but the Committee believes that the Plan must reflect an arithmetically accurate equity allocation. If Timberline believes it is entitled to 55% of the New Common Equity, it must provide a valuation justification for such allocation.]

The treatment described above results in an aggregate recovery to Timberline of $35,000,000 in Cash plus equity valued at approximately $60,000,000 (based on the Clearview Valuation Summary midpoint). Class 2 is Impaired under the Plan and is entitled to vote to accept or reject the Plan. Timberline Capital Partners, LLC has indicated its agreement to support the Plan, subject to and conditioned upon the treatment of the Second Lien Note Claims as set forth in this Section 4.2.

161	Each holder of an Allowed General Unsecured Claim in Class 3 shall receive, in full and final satisfaction, release, and discharge of such Allowed General Unsecured Claim, its Pro Rata share of the Unsecured Creditor Recovery Pool, distributed as follows:
162	(a) Effective Date Distribution. On the Effective Date, the Distribution Agent shall distribute to each holder of an Allowed General Unsecured Claim its Pro Rata share of ~~$9,350,000~~ **[[INS:$21,000,000]] (representing ~~50%~~ [[INS:75%]]** of the Unsecured Creditor Recovery Pool).
163	(b) Anniversary Distribution. On the first anniversary of the Effective Date, the Distribution Agent shall distribute to each holder of an Allowed General Unsecured Claim its Pro Rata share of ~~$9,350,000~~ **[[INS:$7,000,000, plus accrued interest at the federal judgment rate (28 U.S.C. § 1961) in effect as of the Confirmation Date (currently 5.24% per annum) from the Effective Date through the date of distribution]] (representing ~~50%~~ [[INS:25%]] of the Unsecured Creditor Recovery Pool [[INS:, plus accrued interest]]**).
164	**[[INS:(c) Avoidance Action Recovery Pool. In addition to the distributions under Sections 4.3(a) and (b), holders of Allowed General Unsecured Claims shall receive, on a Pro Rata basis, one hundred percent (100%) of the net proceeds from the Avoidance Action Recovery Pool (as defined in Section 1.1), as and when such proceeds are recovered by the Litigation Trust and distributed in accordance with Section 6.7(c). For the avoidance of doubt, the Avoidance Action Recovery Pool distributions are in addition to, and not in lieu of, the Unsecured Creditor Recovery Pool distributions described in Sections 4.3(a) and (b).]]**
165	~~(c)~~ **[[INS:(d)]] *Voting and Recovery Rate.* Class 3 is Impaired under the Plan and is entitled to vote to accept or reject the Plan. The estimated recovery rate for holders of Allowed General Unsecured Claims under this Plan is ~~approximately 10.0%~~ [[INS:approximately 14.97% (exclusive of potential Avoidance Action Recovery Pool distributions, which, if fully realized, could increase the aggregate recovery to approximately 20.05%)]]** of their Allowed General Unsecured Claims.
166	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Avoidance action proceeds (estimated at $9.5M based on identified preference claims against approximately fifteen counterparties) should benefit unsecured creditors, not the reorganized estate. These are estate causes of action that exist for the benefit of the creditor body under well-established case law. For the avoidance of doubt, General Unsecured Claims include, without limitation, trade payables, rejection damages claims arising from the rejection of executory contracts and unexpired leases, and any unsecured deficiency claims. Holders of Allowed General Unsecured Claims shall not be entitled to receive any distribution under this Plan in excess of the face amount of their respective Allowed Claims.

169	All Intercompany Claims shall, at the sole discretion of the Debtor (or, after the Effective Date, the Reorganized Debtor), be reinstated, adjusted, compromised, settled, or cancelled, as determined to be in the best interests of the Reorganized Debtor and its estate. No distributions shall be made on account of Intercompany Claims unless the Debtor elects to reinstate such Claims. Class 4 is Unimpaired or, to the extent any Intercompany Claims are cancelled, deemed to reject the Plan. Holders of Intercompany Claims are not entitled to vote on the Plan.
170	Section 4.5 — Class 5: Equity Interests
171	All existing Equity Interests in Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. shall be cancelled, annulled, and extinguished on the Effective Date, and shall be of no further force or effect. Holders of Equity Interests shall not receive or retain any property under the Plan on account of such Equity Interests. Class 5 is Impaired under the Plan and is deemed to reject the Plan. Accordingly, holders of Equity Interests in Class 5 are not entitled to vote on the Plan, and the votes of such holders shall not be solicited. Any certificates or instruments previously evidencing Equity Interests shall be deemed cancelled and of no further force or effect on and after the Effective Date.
172	ARTICLE V — ACCEPTANCE OR REJECTION OF THE PLAN
173	Section 5.1 — Voting Classes
174	The following Classes are Impaired under the Plan and are entitled to vote to accept or reject the Plan:
175	(a) Class 2 — Second Lien Note Claims; and (b) Class 3 — General Unsecured Claims.
176	The following Classes are Unimpaired under the Plan and are conclusively presumed to have accepted the Plan:
177	(a) Class 1 — Senior Secured Claims.
178	The following Classes are Impaired and receive no distribution under the Plan, and are therefore deemed to have rejected the Plan:
179	(a) Class 5 — Equity Interests.
180	Class 4 (Intercompany Claims) is either Unimpaired (deemed to accept) or, to the extent any such Claims are cancelled, deemed to reject. **[[INS:For the avoidance of doubt, each holder of a Claim or Interest in an impaired Class that is entitled to receive a distribution under the Plan is entitled to vote to accept or reject the Plan.]]**
181	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Clarifying voting eligibility.]
182	Section 5.2 — Acceptance by Impaired Classes
183	Pursuant to Section 1126(c) of the Bankruptcy Code, an impaired Class of Claims has accepted the Plan if the Plan has been accepted by the holders of at least two-thirds (2/3) in dollar amount and more than one-half (1/2) in number of the Allowed Claims of such Class that have actually voted to accept or reject the Plan. For purposes of determining whether a Class has accepted the Plan, only the votes of holders of Allowed Claims in such Class that have timely and properly submitted a Ballot shall be counted. Any Claim held by a holder that is designated under Section 1126(e) of the Bankruptcy Code shall not be counted for purposes of determining acceptance or rejection.
184	Section 5.3 — Cramdown
185	If any impaired Class entitled to vote fails to accept the Plan by the requisite statutory majority, the Debtor reserves the right to (a) request that the Bankruptcy Court confirm the Plan pursuant to Section 1129(b) of the Bankruptcy Code, notwithstanding the failure of such Class to accept the Plan, and/or (b) amend the Plan in accordance with Section 1127 of the Bankruptcy Code to the extent necessary to satisfy the requirements of confirmation. The Debtor's right to seek confirmation under Section 1129(b) is without prejudice to any party's right to object to such confirmation. **[[INS:For the avoidance of doubt, if the Debtor seeks confirmation of the Plan under Section 1129(b), the provisions of Section 11.9 of this Plan shall apply.]]**
186	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Adding cross-reference to new Section 11.9 (cramdown and absolute priority rule compliance).]
187	ARTICLE VI — MEANS FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PLAN
188	Section 6.1 — Continued Corporate Existence
189	On and after the Effective Date, Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc. shall continue to exist as the Reorganized Debtor (Reorganized Cascadia Timber Holdings, Inc.), a corporation organized under the laws of the State of Delaware. The certificate of incorporation and bylaws of the Reorganized Debtor shall be amended and restated as of the Effective Date substantially in the forms included in the Plan Supplement. Such amended and restated organizational documents shall, among other things, (a) authorize the issuance of the New Common Equity, (b) prohibit the issuance of nonvoting equity securities to the extent required by Section 1123(a)(6) of the Bankruptcy Code, and (c) contain such other provisions as are necessary to effectuate the transactions contemplated by this Plan.
190	Section 6.2 — Sources of Cash for Plan Distributions
191	Cash distributions under the Plan shall be funded from the following sources:
192	(a) Cash on hand as of the Effective Date (projected to be approximately $68,000,000 based on the financial projections included in the Disclosure Statement and summarized in Exhibit B hereto);
193	(b) the Cash Payment from Timberline in the amount of $35,000,000, payable on the Effective Date pursuant to Section 4.2(a);
194	(c) proceeds of the DIP Facility, to the extent available and not otherwise repaid or refinanced; and
195	(d) operating revenues of the Debtor generated in the ordinary course of business between the Confirmation Date and the Effective Date.
196	The Debtor represents that it will have sufficient Cash on hand as of the Effective Date to satisfy all Cash distribution obligations arising on the Effective Date under the Plan. Based on the Debtor's financial projections, the aggregate Effective Date Cash requirements are estimated at approximately $62,850,000, consisting of: Administrative Claims ($12,500,000), Priority Tax Claims ($3,200,000), Priority Non-Tax Claims ($2,800,000), Class 1 debt service ($0, as Class 1 is reinstated), Class 2 Cash Payment ($35,000,000), and Class 3 Effective Date Distribution ($9,350,000). The projected Cash at emergence of $68,000,000 provides a cushion of approximately $5,150,000 above projected Effective Date Cash requirements.
197	Section 6.3 — Issuance of New Common Equity
198	On the Effective Date, the Reorganized Debtor shall be authorized to issue the New Common Equity. ~~55%~~ **[[INS:41.07%]] of the New Common Equity shall be issued and delivered to Timberline Capital Partners, LLC, on account of the Equity Conversion Amount pursuant to Section 4.2(b). The remaining ~~45%~~ [[INS:58.93%]]** of the New Common Equity shall be held by the Reorganized Debtor (subject to dilution by the Management Incentive Plan as described in Section 6.4). The issuance of the New Common Equity pursuant to this Plan shall be exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933 and any applicable state or local law requiring registration of the issuance of securities, to the maximum extent permitted by Section 1145 of the Bankruptcy Code. All shares of New Common Equity issued pursuant to this Plan shall be duly authorized, validly issued, fully paid, and nonassessable.
199	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Equity percentages corrected consistent with the definition of "New Common Equity" in Section 1.1 and the treatment of Class 2 in Section 4.2.]
200	Section 6.4 — Management Incentive Plan

1	Section 6.4 — Management Incentive Plan
2	On or after the Effective Date, the Reorganized Debtor shall implement the Management Incentive Plan, which shall reserve ~~10%~~ **[[INS:7%]] of the New Common Equity (on a fully diluted basis) for issuance to eligible employees and officers of the Reorganized ~~Debtor~~ [[INS:Company]]** in accordance with the terms of the MIP. The MIP equity pool shall vest over four (4) years from the Effective Date at a rate of twenty-five percent (25%) per annum, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the MIP term sheet to be included in the Plan Supplement. The MIP equity pool shall dilute all holders of New Common Equity on a pro rata basis. The Board of Directors of the Reorganized Debtor shall have discretion to determine the individual allocation of MIP equity among eligible employees and officers, subject to the aggregate pool limits set forth herein. The terms of the MIP, including eligibility criteria, performance conditions (if any), and acceleration provisions, shall be set forth in the MIP term sheet filed as part of the Plan Supplement.
3	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Reducing the MIP pool from 10% to 7% reduces dilution of equity value and benefits unsecured creditors' potential future recovery in the event the reorganized entity undergoes a subsequent liquidity event or equity distribution. The Committee believes 7% is a market-standard MIP allocation for a mid-market timber and forest products company and is sufficient to incentivize post-emergence management. The 3% reduction in the MIP pool frees up additional equity value that supports the overall recovery framework for unsecured creditors.]
4	Section 6.5 — Corporate Governance of Reorganized Debtor
5	The Board of Directors of the Reorganized Debtor shall consist of five (5) members, constituted as follows:
6	(a) ~~Three (3)~~ **[[INS:Two (2)]]** directors designated by Timberline Capital Partners, LLC;
7	(b) ~~One (1)~~ **[[INS:Two (2)]]** director(s) designated by the Committee (or, after the dissolution of the Committee, by the holders of Allowed General Unsecured Claims holding in the aggregate more than fifty percent (50%) of the total amount of Allowed General Unsecured Claims); and
8	(c) One (1) independent director selected jointly by Timberline and the Committee (or its successors).
9	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Given the significant unsecured creditor recovery at stake and the potential for post-emergence distributions (including from the Avoidance Action Recovery Pool), the Committee believes it is appropriate to have two board representatives to ensure adequate oversight of the Reorganized Debtor's operations and financial management. The Committee notes that, even with two board seats, Timberline and the jointly-selected independent director will constitute a majority of the board.]
10	The initial directors shall be identified in the Plan Supplement to be filed no later than seven (7) days before the Voting Deadline. Each director shall serve until his or her successor is duly elected or appointed. The Reorganized Debtor's amended and restated bylaws shall provide for standard director and officer indemnification protections, shall establish audit, compensation, and governance committees, and shall contain such other provisions as are customary for a corporation of the size and nature of the Reorganized Debtor.
11	Section 6.6 — Retention of Key Employees
12	~~Section 6.6 — Retention of Key Employees. The Reorganized Debtor shall assume all obligations under the Key Employee Retention Bonus Program approved by the Board of Directors of the Debtor on February 15, 2025, totaling $3,400,000 in the aggregate for twelve (12) senior employees, payable in accordance with the terms thereof, which obligations shall be treated as Allowed Administrative Claims. The Key Employee Retention Bonus Program was designed to incentivize the retention of employees whose continued service is essential to the successful reorganization and post-emergence operations of the Debtor. Payment under the program shall be made in two equal installments: (i) $1,700,000 on the Effective Date and (ii) $1,700,000 on the six-month anniversary of the Effective Date, subject to continued employment of the applicable employee on each payment date.~~
13	[COMMENT – D. Chen: This section must be stricken in its entirety. Retention bonus payments totaling $3.4M for insiders have not been subjected to § 503(c) review. Under § 503(c)(1), the Debtor must demonstrate that each recipient has a bona fide job offer at equal or greater compensation and that the transfer does not exceed statutory limits. No such showing has been made. Additionally, see new Section 11.9 regarding the absolute priority rule implications of these payments. To the extent the Debtor believes that retention bonuses are necessary, the Debtor should file a separate motion under § 503(c) and bear the burden of demonstrating compliance with the statutory requirements. The Committee will vigorously oppose any attempt to pay these bonuses without proper judicial scrutiny.]
14	Section 6.7 — Litigation Trust
15	(a) Establishment of Litigation Trust. On the Effective Date, a Litigation Trust shall be established for the purpose of prosecuting, settling, or otherwise resolving all Avoidance Actions and Retained Actions transferred to the Litigation Trust pursuant to this Section 6.7. The Litigation Trust shall be administered by a Litigation Trustee, who shall be selected by the ~~Debtor~~ **[[INS:Committee, with the consent of the Debtor (not to be unreasonably withheld)]]**. The identity of the proposed Litigation Trustee shall be disclosed in the Plan Supplement filed with the Bankruptcy Court.
16	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Since avoidance action proceeds are to be distributed to unsecured creditors under the proposed Avoidance Action Recovery Pool, the Committee should have the primary role in selecting the Litigation Trustee. The consent requirement ensures the Debtor has input, but the Committee, as the representative of the creditor constituency that stands to benefit from these actions, should have the leading role.]
17	(b) Transfer of Avoidance Actions and Retained Actions. On the Effective Date, all Avoidance Actions and Retained Actions shall be transferred to and vest in the Litigation Trust. The Litigation Trustee shall have the exclusive authority, on behalf of the Litigation Trust, to prosecute, settle, compromise, abandon, or otherwise resolve such actions in a manner consistent with the Litigation Trustee's fiduciary duties. The Litigation Trust shall be funded with an initial amount of $500,000 in Cash, to be provided by the Reorganized Debtor on the Effective Date, to fund the initial costs and expenses of the Litigation Trustee.
18	**[[INS:(c) Distribution of Avoidance Action Proceeds. All net proceeds recovered by the Litigation Trust from Avoidance Actions, after deduction of reasonable costs and expenses of prosecution (including Litigation Trustee fees, attorneys' fees, expert witness fees, and other litigation expenses), shall be distributed exclusively to holders of Allowed General Unsecured Claims, on a Pro Rata basis, as part of the Avoidance Action Recovery Pool defined in Section 1.1.
