19	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Avoidance action proceeds are property of the estate that should benefit unsecured creditors. The reorganized entity should not retain these proceeds when unsecured creditors are receiving less than full recovery. The identified preference claims total approximately $9.5M gross, based on the Committee's independent analysis of pre-petition payments made to approximately fifteen counterparties within the ninety-day preference period. The Committee's analysis suggests net recoveries (after costs) of approximately $6.0M to $7.5M, which would increase the effective unsecured creditor recovery rate by an additional 3.2% to 4.0%.]
20	The Litigation Trust shall terminate upon the earlier of (i) the resolution of all Avoidance Actions and Retained Actions and the distribution of all proceeds therefrom, or (ii) the third anniversary of the Effective Date, unless extended by order of the Bankruptcy Court upon motion of the Litigation Trustee.
21	ARTICLE VII — TREATMENT OF EXECUTORY CONTRACTS AND UNEXPIRED LEASES
22	Section 7.1 — Assumption of Executory Contracts
23	On the Effective Date, the Debtor shall assume, pursuant to Sections 365 and 1123 of the Bankruptcy Code, each executory contract and unexpired lease listed on Exhibit C (Assumed Contracts) attached hereto. The assumption of executory contracts and unexpired leases pursuant to this Section 7.1 shall be effective as of the Effective Date without the need for any further notice to or action, order, or approval of the Bankruptcy Court, except as otherwise required by the Bankruptcy Code. The assumed executory contracts and unexpired leases include, without limitation, the timber supply agreement between the Debtor and Olympic Forest Resources LLC providing for the supply of raw timber to the Debtor's Centralia, Washington mill at an annual value of approximately $22,000,000. All cure amounts required to be paid pursuant to Section 365(b)(1) of the Bankruptcy Code in connection with the assumption of executory contracts and unexpired leases shall be paid by the Reorganized Debtor in Cash on the Effective Date, or as soon thereafter as is reasonably practicable, unless the Debtor and the applicable counterparty agree to alternative cure arrangements.
24	Section 7.2 — Rejection of Executory Contracts
25	On the Effective Date, the Debtor shall reject, pursuant to Sections 365 and 1123 of the Bankruptcy Code, each executory contract and unexpired lease listed on Exhibit C (Rejected Contracts) attached hereto. The Debtor, in the exercise of its ~~business judgment~~ **[[INS:reasonable determination that the continued performance of such contract or lease would impose a material net burden on the estate or the Reorganized Debtor]]**, has determined to reject the executory contracts and unexpired leases identified on Exhibit C (Rejected Contracts). The rejected executory contracts and unexpired leases include, without limitation, the equipment maintenance agreement between the Debtor and PacWest Industrial Services providing for maintenance services at the Debtor's Bend, Oregon mill at an annual cost of approximately $1,800,000.
26	[COMMENT – D. Chen: The "business judgment" standard is overly broad and provides insufficient protection for counterparties to executory contracts. The Committee proposes a "material net burden" standard that provides more meaningful review and ensures that contracts are not rejected merely for the convenience of the Reorganized Debtor. Counterparties whose contracts are rejected suffer real economic harm — their rejection damages claims are treated as General Unsecured Claims and will recover only a fraction of their contractual entitlements. A meaningful rejection standard is appropriate and consistent with the obligations of a plan proponent under the Bankruptcy Code.]
27	Any damages arising from the rejection of an executory contract or unexpired lease shall be treated as a General Unsecured Claim in Class 3, subject to the bar date provisions of Section 7.3 of this Plan and the claims allowance procedures of Article V.
28	Section 7.3 — Bar Date for Rejection Damages Claims
29	If the rejection of an executory contract or unexpired lease under this Plan gives rise to a Claim by the counterparty to such contract or lease, such Claim shall be forever barred and shall not be enforceable against the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, or the Estate unless a proof of claim is filed with the Bankruptcy Court and served upon the Reorganized Debtor and its counsel within thirty (30) days after the later of (a) the Effective Date or (b) the date of entry of an order of the Bankruptcy Court authorizing rejection of such contract or lease. All such Claims shall be subject to the claims objection and resolution procedures set forth in Article V of this Plan.
30	Section 7.4 — Avoidance Actions
31	The Estate's Avoidance Actions are preserved and shall be transferred to the Litigation Trust on the Effective Date in accordance with Section 6.7 of this Plan. The Debtor has identified approximately $9,500,000 in potential Avoidance Actions, consisting primarily of preference claims under Section 547 of the Bankruptcy Code against approximately fifteen (15) counterparties who received payments during the ninety (90) days preceding the Petition Date. The prosecution, settlement, and distribution of proceeds from Avoidance Actions shall be governed by the Litigation Trust provisions set forth in Section 6.7.
32	ARTICLE VIII — RELEASES, EXCULPATION, AND INJUNCTION
33	Section 8.1 — Releases by the Debtor and the Estate
34	Effective as of the Effective Date, and except as otherwise expressly provided herein, the Debtor and the Estate, on behalf of themselves and their predecessors, successors, assigns, subsidiaries, and affiliates, shall be deemed to have unconditionally and irrevocably released and discharged the Released Parties from any and all claims, obligations, suits, judgments, damages, demands, debts, rights, causes of action, liabilities, and remedies whatsoever, whether known or unknown, foreseen or unforeseen, existing or hereafter arising, in law, equity, or otherwise, that are based in whole or in part upon any act or omission, transaction, event, or other occurrence taking place on or before the Effective Date in any way relating to the Debtor, the Chapter 11 Case, the Plan, the Disclosure Statement, or any related agreement, instrument, or document.
35	The foregoing releases are approved by the Bankruptcy Court pursuant to Section 1123(b) of the Bankruptcy Code and are an essential component of this Plan. The Debtor has determined, in the exercise of its business judgment, that the releases set forth in this Section 8.1 are appropriate and in the best interests of the Debtor, the Estate, and all parties in interest.
36	**[[INS:; provided, however, that the foregoing releases shall not extend to any claims, causes of action, or rights of the Debtor or the Estate against Timberline Capital Partners, LLC, or its affiliates, officers, directors, members, or agents, arising out of or related to the dividend recapitalization transaction consummated on or about September 14, 2021 (the "2021 Dividend Recapitalization"), including but not limited to any claims or causes of action arising under Sections 544, 547, 548, or 550 of the Bankruptcy Code or applicable state fraudulent transfer or fraudulent conveyance laws. All such claims, causes of action, and rights are expressly preserved and shall be transferred to the Litigation Trust on the Effective Date for prosecution, settlement, or other resolution in accordance with Section 6.7 of this Plan.]]**
37	[COMMENT – D. Chen: The 2021 Dividend Recapitalization was the proximate cause of the Debtor's over-leveraged capital structure and ultimate insolvency. On or about September 14, 2021, Timberline arranged for the Debtor to issue $95M in second lien notes, the proceeds of which were used to fund a dividend distribution that primarily benefited existing equity holders (including entities affiliated with Timberline). Timberline extracted approximately $95M in value through second lien notes issued in connection with this transaction. Potential constructive fraudulent transfer claims exist under both Section 548 of the Bankruptcy Code and the Oregon Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (ORS 95.200 et seq.). The Committee's preliminary analysis suggests that the Debtor may have been insolvent at the time of, or rendered insolvent by, the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization, and that the Debtor did not receive reasonably equivalent value for the obligations it incurred. The Committee cannot agree to release these claims without a full investigation. This carve-out is non-negotiable.]
38	Section 8.2 — Releases by Holders of Claims and Equity Interests (Third-Party Releases)
39	(a) Consensual Releases. Each holder of a Claim or Equity Interest that votes in favor of the Plan or that does not timely opt out of the releases contained herein by checking the appropriate box on its Ballot or opt-out form shall be deemed to have released the Released Parties from any and all claims, obligations, suits, judgments, damages, demands, debts, rights, causes of action, liabilities, and remedies whatsoever, whether known or unknown, foreseen or unforeseen, existing or hereafter arising, in law, equity, or otherwise, that are based in whole or in part upon any act or omission, transaction, event, or other occurrence taking place on or before the Effective Date in any way relating to the Debtor, the Chapter 11 Case, the Plan, the Disclosure Statement, or any related agreement, instrument, or document **[[INS:; provided that such consensual releases shall not extend to claims against Timberline Capital Partners, LLC arising out of or related to the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization, as set forth in Section 8.1]]**.
40	~~(b) Non-Consensual Releases. Notwithstanding anything in Section 8.2(a) to the contrary, as of the Effective Date, each holder of a Claim or Equity Interest that does not vote in favor of the Plan and does not opt out of the releases contained herein shall also be deemed to have released the Released Parties from any and all claims, obligations, suits, judgments, damages, demands, debts, rights, causes of action, liabilities, and remedies whatsoever, whether known or unknown, foreseen or unforeseen, existing or hereafter arising, in law, equity, or otherwise, that are based in whole or in part upon any act or omission, transaction, event, or other occurrence taking place on or before the Effective Date in any way relating to the Debtor, the Chapter 11 Case, the Plan, the Disclosure Statement, or any related agreement, instrument, or document. The foregoing non-consensual releases are an integral part of the Plan and are necessary for the successful reorganization of the Debtor. The Debtor believes that the non-consensual releases are appropriate based on the record of the Chapter 11 Case and the contribution of the Released Parties to the restructuring process, and that such releases satisfy the standards for approval of non-consensual releases under applicable law.~~
41	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Non-consensual third-party releases are impermissible in the Ninth Circuit and likely impermissible nationwide following the Supreme Court's decision in Harrington v. Purdue Pharma L.P., 144 S. Ct. 2071 (2024). In Harrington, the Supreme Court held that § 1123(b)(6) does not authorize a release and injunction that effectively seeks to discharge claims against a nondebtor without the consent of affected claimants. The Ninth Circuit has long held that non-consensual non-debtor releases are generally impermissible absent exceptional circumstances, and no such circumstances exist here. The Committee objects to any non-consensual release provision and will oppose confirmation of any Plan containing such a provision. The consensual release in Section 8.2(a) is retained with appropriate carve-outs consistent with Section 8.1.]
42	Section 8.3 — Exculpation
43	Effective as of the Effective Date, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, none of the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, the Committee, or any of their respective members, officers, directors, employees, advisors, attorneys, professionals, accountants, or agents (acting in their respective capacities as such) shall have or incur any liability for any claim, cause of action, or other assertion of liability of any kind for any act taken or omitted to be taken in connection with, related to, or arising out of, the Chapter 11 Case, the formulation, negotiation, preparation, dissemination, implementation, administration, or confirmation of the Plan, the Disclosure Statement, or any contract, instrument, release, or other agreement or document created or entered into in connection with the Plan, or any other act taken or omitted to be taken in connection with or in contemplation of the restructuring of the Debtor; provided, however, that the foregoing exculpation shall not apply to any act or omission that constitutes willful misconduct, gross negligence, or fraud, in each case as determined by a Final Order.
44	Section 8.4 — Injunction
45	Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Plan or the Confirmation Order, effective as of the Effective Date, all Persons who have held, hold, or may hold Claims against or Equity Interests in the Debtor that arose before the Effective Date are permanently enjoined from: (a) commencing or continuing in any manner any action or other proceeding of any kind against the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, or the Released Parties with respect to any such Claim or Equity Interest; (b) the enforcement, attachment, collection, or recovery by any manner or means of any judgment, award, decree, or order against the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, or the Released Parties on account of any such Claim or Equity Interest; (c) creating, perfecting, or enforcing any encumbrance of any kind against the property of the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, or the Released Parties on account of any such Claim or Equity Interest; and (d) any act, in any manner and in any place, that does not conform to or comply with the provisions of this Plan to the extent such act relates to a Claim or Equity Interest arising before the Effective Date **[[INS:; provided, however, that the injunction shall not bar claims or causes of action expressly preserved under Sections 8.1 and 8.2 of this Plan, including claims related to the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization]]**.
46	ARTICLE IX — CONDITIONS PRECEDENT TO THE EFFECTIVE DATE
47	Section 9.1 — Conditions to the Effective Date
48	The Effective Date shall not occur unless and until each of the following conditions has been satisfied or waived in accordance with Section 9.2 of this Plan:
49	(a) The Confirmation Order shall have become a Final Order and shall not be subject to any stay, whether pending appeal or otherwise.
50	(b) All documents and agreements necessary to implement the Plan, including the amended and restated certificate of incorporation and bylaws of the Reorganized Debtor, the New Common Equity documentation, and the MIP term sheet, shall have been executed and delivered in forms reasonably satisfactory to the Debtor, Timberline, and First Meridian.
51	(c) All governmental and regulatory approvals and consents necessary to implement the Plan shall have been obtained, and all applicable waiting periods shall have expired.
52	(d) The New Common Equity shall have been authorized and issued in accordance with Section 6.3 of this Plan.
53	(e) The DIP Facility shall have been repaid in full or converted in accordance with the terms thereof and the DIP Facility order.
54	(f) The Reorganized Debtor shall have sufficient Cash on hand to make all distributions required to be made on the Effective Date under this Plan.
55	**[[INS:(g) The Debtor shall have filed with the Bankruptcy Court, and the Bankruptcy Court shall have approved, a supplemental disclosure statement containing adequate information (within the meaning of Section 1125 of the Bankruptcy Code) regarding the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization, including (i) a detailed description of the transaction and its terms, including the identity of all parties who received distributions in connection therewith, (ii) an analysis of the potential avoidability of the transaction under Sections 544, 548, and 550 of the Bankruptcy Code and applicable state law, including an assessment of the Debtor's solvency at the time of the transaction, (iii) the estimated range of recoverable damages, (iv) the Committee's position regarding the claims that may be asserted in connection therewith, and (v) a description of the impact that the preservation or release of such claims would have on distributions to creditors under the Plan.]]**
56	[COMMENT – D. Chen: Adequate disclosure regarding the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization is essential for creditors to make an informed voting decision. The current Disclosure Statement (Dkt. No. 345) contains only a cursory, two-sentence mention of the transaction on page 14 and does not address its potential avoidability, the solvency of the Debtor at the time of the transaction, or the impact of the proposed releases on creditor recoveries. This supplemental disclosure requirement is non-negotiable. The Committee anticipates that the supplemental disclosure can be prepared and filed on an expedited basis and should not materially delay the plan timeline. The Committee is prepared to cooperate with the Debtor in preparing such disclosure to the extent the Debtor is willing to engage constructively.]
57	Section 9.2 — Waiver of Conditions
58	The conditions set forth in Sections 9.1(a) through (f) may be waived by the Debtor, with the consent of Timberline and First Meridian (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), without notice, leave, or order of the Bankruptcy Court and without any formal action other than proceeding to consummate the Plan.
59	**[[INS:Notwithstanding the foregoing, the condition set forth in Section 9.1(g) may not be waived without the prior written consent of the Committee.]]**
60	[COMMENT – D. Chen: The Committee must have veto authority over any waiver of the supplemental disclosure requirement. Without this protection, the Debtor could unilaterally waive the disclosure condition and proceed to the Effective Date without providing creditors the information necessary to evaluate the fairness of the Plan, including the proposed releases of the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization claims.]
61	Section 9.3 — Effect of Non-Occurrence of Conditions
62	If the Effective Date does not occur within one hundred twenty (120) days after the Confirmation Date (subject to extension by order of the Bankruptcy Court for cause shown upon motion of the Debtor), then, upon motion by any party in interest made before the Effective Date, the Confirmation Order shall be vacated by the Bankruptcy Court, the Plan shall be deemed null and void in all respects, and nothing contained in the Plan or the Disclosure Statement shall (a) constitute a waiver or release of any Claims by or against, or any Equity Interests in, the Debtor, or (b) prejudice in any manner the rights of the Debtor, any holder of a Claim or Equity Interest, or any other party in interest.
63	ARTICLE X — EFFECT OF CONFIRMATION
64	Section 10.1 — Binding Effect
65	On and after the Confirmation Date, the provisions of this Plan shall bind all holders of Claims against and Equity Interests in the Debtor, whether or not the Claim or Equity Interest of such holder is Impaired under the Plan and whether or not such holder has accepted the Plan. All provisions of the Plan, including the releases, exculpation, and injunction provisions set forth in Article VIII, shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, any holder of a Claim against or Equity Interest in the Debtor, the Released Parties, and all other parties in interest.
66	Section 10.2 — Vesting of Assets
67	On the Effective Date, all property of the Estate, including all claims, rights, and causes of action (other than those transferred to the Litigation Trust pursuant to Section 6.7), shall vest in the Reorganized Debtor free and clear of all Claims, Liens, charges, encumbrances, and other interests, except as otherwise expressly provided in the Plan or the Confirmation Order. From and after the Effective Date, the Reorganized Debtor may operate its business and use, acquire, and dispose of property and settle and compromise Claims and Equity Interests without supervision or approval by the Bankruptcy Court and free of any restrictions of the Bankruptcy Code or the Bankruptcy Rules.
68	Section 10.3 — Discharge
69	Pursuant to Section 1141(d)(1) of the Bankruptcy Code, except as otherwise provided in this Plan, the distributions, rights, and treatment that are provided in this Plan shall be in complete satisfaction, discharge, and release of all Claims (whether known or unknown, matured or unmatured, contingent or noncontingent, liquidated or unliquidated, disputed or undisputed, legal or equitable, secured or unsecured) arising before the Effective Date against, and all debts of, the Debtor, the Estate, and the Reorganized Debtor, and shall terminate all Equity Interests in the Debtor **[[INS:; provided that the discharge shall not affect claims expressly preserved under Article VIII of this Plan, including the claims and causes of action related to the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization that are carved out from the releases in Sections 8.1 and 8.2]]**. Confirmation of this Plan does not discharge the Reorganized Debtor from any debt arising after the Confirmation Date.
70	ARTICLE XI — RETENTION OF JURISDICTION
71	Section 11.1 — General Retention of Jurisdiction
72	Notwithstanding the entry of the Confirmation Order and the occurrence of the Effective Date, the Bankruptcy Court shall retain exclusive jurisdiction over all matters arising out of, and related to, the Chapter 11 Case and this Plan, including jurisdiction to:
73	(a) allow, disallow, determine, liquidate, classify, estimate, or establish the priority, secured or unsecured status, or amount of any Claim or Equity Interest;
74	(b) resolve any matters related to the assumption, assignment, or rejection of executory contracts and unexpired leases and the allowance of any cure amounts or rejection damages claims;
75	(c) hear and determine all controversies, suits, and disputes that may arise in connection with the interpretation, implementation, or enforcement of this Plan;
76	(d) hear and determine all applications for compensation and reimbursement of expenses of professionals; and
77	(e) enter and implement such orders as may be necessary or appropriate if the Confirmation Order is modified, stayed, reversed, revoked, or vacated.
78	Section 11.2 — Disputes Concerning Claims
79	The Bankruptcy Court shall retain jurisdiction to resolve any disputes concerning the allowance, disallowance, estimation, classification, priority, or amount of any Claim or Equity Interest, including any objections to Claims or applications to estimate Claims for distribution purposes pursuant to Section 502(c) of the Bankruptcy Code.
80	Section 11.3 — Executory Contracts and Unexpired Leases
81	The Bankruptcy Court shall retain jurisdiction over all disputes arising from or related to the assumption, assumption and assignment, or rejection of executory contracts and unexpired leases, including disputes regarding the amount of any cure payments and the determination of rejection damages claims.
82	Section 11.4 — Avoidance Actions
83	The Bankruptcy Court shall retain jurisdiction over all Avoidance Actions and Retained Actions, including any Avoidance Actions or Retained Actions transferred to the Litigation Trust pursuant to Section 6.7 of this Plan **[[INS:, including jurisdiction over disputes concerning the distribution of Avoidance Action Recovery Pool proceeds under Section 4.3(c)]]**. Nothing in this Plan shall limit the Bankruptcy Court's jurisdiction to hear and determine motions to compromise or settle Avoidance Actions or Retained Actions pursuant to Bankruptcy Rule 9019.
84	Section 11.5 — Plan Modification
85	The Bankruptcy Court shall retain jurisdiction to hear and determine any requests to modify the Plan pursuant to Section 1127 of the Bankruptcy Code, whether before or after the Effective Date.
86	Section 11.6 — Annual Operating Reports
87	The Reorganized Debtor shall file quarterly operating reports with the Bankruptcy Court and the United States Trustee for a period of two (2) years following the Effective Date, or until the Chapter 11 Case is closed by entry of a final decree, whichever occurs first. Such reports shall include financial statements, a summary of distributions made under the Plan, and such other information as the Bankruptcy Court or the United States Trustee may require.
88	Section 11.7 — Final Decree
89	The Bankruptcy Court shall retain jurisdiction to enter a final decree closing the Chapter 11 Case upon motion of the Reorganized Debtor or any party in interest, upon a showing that the Plan has been substantially consummated and all distributions required to be made under the Plan have been made or provided for.
90	Section 11.8 — Enforcement of Plan Provisions
91	The Bankruptcy Court shall retain jurisdiction to enforce all provisions of this Plan and the Confirmation Order, including the releases, exculpation, and injunction provisions set forth in Article VIII, and to issue such orders as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the provisions of this Plan.
92	**[INSERTED: Section 11.9 — Cramdown and Absolute Priority Rule Compliance]**
93	**[INSERTED: In the event that Class 3 (General Unsecured Claims) votes to reject the Plan, and the Debtor seeks to confirm the Plan over the rejection of Class 3 pursuant to Section 1129(b) of the Bankruptcy Code, the following provisions shall apply:**
94	(a) The Debtor shall bear the burden of demonstrating, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the Plan does not discriminate unfairly and is fair and equitable with respect to Class 3, in accordance with Section 1129(b)(2)(B) of the Bankruptcy Code.
95	(b) For purposes of determining whether the Plan satisfies the absolute priority rule under Section 1129(b)(2)(B)(ii), the Court shall consider whether any holder of a Claim or Interest that is junior to Class 3 receives or retains any property under the Plan on account of such junior Claim or Interest. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the parties acknowledge that the Key Employee Retention Bonus Program (to the extent it is authorized and funded under the Plan) constitutes value that may be characterized as property retained by insiders who hold Claims or Interests junior to Class 3, and the Debtor shall address whether such payments are consistent with the absolute priority rule. The Debtor shall further address whether the Management Incentive Plan, to the extent it confers equity on officers and employees who are also equity holders or insiders, constitutes a transfer of value to junior parties in violation of the absolute priority rule.
96	(c) Nothing in this Section 11.9 shall be construed to limit the Committee's rights to object to confirmation of the Plan under Section 1129(a) or (b) of the Bankruptcy Code, or to assert any and all defenses, claims, and causes of action that are preserved under the Plan. The Committee expressly reserves all rights to argue that the Plan fails to satisfy any requirement for confirmation, including but not limited to the requirements of Section 1129(a)(1) (plan compliance with applicable provisions of the Bankruptcy Code), Section 1129(a)(3) (good faith), Section 1129(a)(7) (best interests of creditors), and Section 1129(b) (cramdown).]
97	[COMMENT – D. Chen: This provision is designed to protect the Committee's cramdown rights in the event unsecured creditors vote to reject the Plan. The $3.4M retention bonus program represents value flowing to insiders (management) who, as equity participants via the MIP, hold interests junior to unsecured creditors. If the Debtor seeks cramdown over the rejection of Class 3, it must demonstrate compliance with the absolute priority rule under Section 1129(b)(2)(B)(ii), and these retention payments may constitute a disqualifying transfer of value to junior parties. See, e.g., In re Jevic Holding Corp., 580 U.S. 455 (2017) (emphasizing the importance of the absolute priority rule in protecting the rights of dissenting creditors). This is a critical protection and is non-negotiable. The Committee is prepared to litigate this issue at the confirmation hearing if necessary.]
98	ARTICLE XII — MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
99	Section 12.1 — Payment of Statutory Fees
100	All fees payable pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1930 shall be paid by the Debtor on or before the Effective Date and shall continue to be paid by the Reorganized Debtor on a quarterly basis thereafter until the earlier of the closing of the Chapter 11 Case by entry of a final decree or the conversion of the Chapter 11 Case to a case under Chapter 7 of the Bankruptcy Code. The Reorganized Debtor shall provide the United States Trustee with such reports and information as may be required to calculate and verify the amounts of such fees.
101	Section 12.2 — Plan Supplement
102	The Debtor shall file a Plan Supplement with the Bankruptcy Court no later than seven (7) days before the Voting Deadline. The Plan Supplement shall contain, at a minimum, the following: (a) the forms of the amended and restated certificate of incorporation and bylaws of the Reorganized Debtor; (b) the MIP term sheet; (c) the identity of the proposed members of the Board of Directors of the Reorganized Debtor; (d) the forms of any material contracts, instruments, or other agreements to be entered into in connection with the Plan; (e) the identity of the proposed Litigation Trustee; and (f) such other documents and information as may be necessary to effectuate the transactions contemplated by the Plan **[[INS:, including the supplemental disclosure required under Section 9.1(g)]]**. The Debtor reserves the right to amend or supplement the Plan Supplement at any time prior to the Effective Date, subject to the requirements of the Bankruptcy Code and Bankruptcy Rules.
103	Section 12.3 — Severability
104	If, prior to the entry of the Confirmation Order, any term or provision of this Plan is held by the Bankruptcy Court to be invalid, void, or unenforceable, the Bankruptcy Court, at the request of the Debtor, shall have the power to alter and interpret such term or provision to make it valid or enforceable to the maximum extent practicable, consistent with the original purpose of the term or provision held to be invalid, void, or unenforceable, and such term or provision shall then be applicable as altered or interpreted. Notwithstanding any such holding, alteration, or interpretation, the remainder of the terms and provisions of this Plan shall remain in full force and effect and shall in no way be affected, impaired, or invalidated by such holding, alteration, or interpretation.

130	Section 12.6 — Governing Law
131	Except to the extent the Bankruptcy Code or the Bankruptcy Rules are applicable, the rights and obligations arising under this Plan shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, (a) the laws of the State of Delaware, without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws thereof, with respect to all matters concerning the corporate governance of the Reorganized Debtor, and (b) the laws of the State of Oregon, without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws thereof, with respect to all contractual matters and all other matters not specifically governed by the Bankruptcy Code, Bankruptcy Rules, or Delaware corporate law.

["Contract rejection","Protects counterparties, “including Committee members”; “does not meaningfully impair” flexibility.","Replaces the business-judgment test with a novel “material net burden” standard that invites litigation over every rejection.","Self-interested; inconsistent with prevailing law."],
]

d.add_heading("III. Threshold Finding: The Redline Is Not a Markup of the Filed Plan",level=1)
para(d,"The Redline states that it reflects proposed modifications \u201cto the Second Amended Plan of Reorganization filed by the Debtor on April 28, 2025 (Dkt. No. 387).\u201d Its unmarked text, however, departs from the Filed Plan in structure, numbering, dates and substance. This indicates that the Committee worked from a different draft. Filed Plan Section 6.4 concerns unclaimed distributions, and Article IX concerns conditions precedent.")
para(d,"The practical risk is this. If the Debtor \u201caccepts\u201d agreed tracked changes in the Committee\u2019s file, every untracked difference below becomes part of the operative plan text without having been negotiated. The table lists the material untracked deviations we identified.")
rows=[["#","Topic","Filed Plan (Apr. 28, 2025)","Redline base text (untracked)","Why it matters / recommended action"],
["U-1","Petition Date; Committee appointment","Petition Date Mar. 3, 2025; Committee appointed Mar. 17, 2025 (Plan \u00a7 1.1; DS \u00a7\u00a7 3.4\u20133.5).","Petition Date Jan. 6, 2025; Committee appointed Jan. 24, 2025.","Shifts the 90-day preference window (Oct. 8, 2024\u2013Jan. 6, 2025 instead of Dec. 3, 2024\u2013Mar. 3, 2025), which changes which of the ~$9.5M of identified preferences exist. It also turns the Feb. 15, 2025 board approval of the retention program into a post-petition act. **Reject; conform to the record.**"],
["U-2","DIP Facility","Approved by order entered Mar. 21, 2025 (Plan \u00a7 1.1). DS \u00a7 3.5: up to $40M; interim Mar. 12, final Apr. 2, 2025.","Agreement dated Jan. 15, 2025; $25M; interim/final orders Jan. 16 and Feb. 10, 2025.","Wrong facility amount and orders. Repayment and roll-up mechanics are tied to the DIP order. **Reject.** (Note: the Plan and DS are also inconsistent with each other; see Section VIII.)"],
["U-3","Senior credit facility","Credit Agreement dated Mar. 28, 2018; $275M facility; maturity June 2028.","Senior Secured Credit Agreement dated June 15, 2018; maturity June 15, 2028.","Wrong agreement date. The reinstatement and Amended Credit Agreement terms depend on correct identification of the facility. **Reject.**"],
["U-4","Classification","Seven classes: Cl. 1 Priority Non-Tax (unimpaired); **Cl. 2 First Meridian (impaired, votes)**; Cl. 3 Timberline; Cl. 4 GUCs; Cl. 5 Intercompany; Cl. 6 Equity; Cl. 7 \u00a7 510(b).","Five classes: **Cl. 1 First Meridian \u201cUnimpaired \u2026 conclusively presumed to have accepted\u201d**; Cl. 2 Timberline; Cl. 3 GUCs; Cl. 4 Intercompany; Cl. 5 Equity. Priority non-tax claims become unclassified. No \u00a7 510(b) class.","First Meridian\u2019s maturity is extended and its rate reduced, so its legal rights are altered and it is impaired under \u00a7 1124. Timberline would then be the only possible accepting impaired class if GUCs reject, and the Committee\u2019s comments are already laying groundwork to call Timberline an insider (see V.B, VII.4). \u00a7 510(b) claims would be left unaddressed. **Reject; retain the Filed Plan structure.**"],
["U-5","\u201cReleased Parties\u201d","\u00a7 10.4(a) includes First Meridian (as lender, agent and DIP lender), Timberline (as noteholder and Plan Sponsor), and their affiliates and professionals.","Definition lists only the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor, the Committee and its members, D&Os and professionals. **First Meridian and Timberline are omitted entirely.** The tracked Timberline carve-out is then layered on top.","This is the most consequential untracked change. If accepted, neither plan-support party would receive any release, not merely a Dividend Recap carve-out. Timberline\u2019s support is expressly conditioned on its treatment (Plan \u00a7 4.3; DS \u201cTimberline Support Risk\u201d). **Reject; negotiate any carve-out against the Filed Plan definition.**"],
["U-6","Debtor release carve-outs","\u00a7 10.5 preserves (a) enforcement of the Plan and (b) Avoidance Actions preserved for the Litigation Trust (limited to preferences against non-Released Parties). \u00a7 10.4(d) expressly covers Dividend Recap claims.","\u00a7 8.1 Debtor release has no carve-out for preserved Avoidance Actions or Plan enforcement. The express Dividend Recap coverage is gone.","The Debtor release could be read to release the very preference claims the Committee wants to monetize, including claims against Committee members, who are Released Parties in their Committee capacity. **Retain the Filed Plan carve-outs.**"],
["U-7","Retention bonuses","\u00a7 5.8: $3.4M program for 12 senior employees, approved pre-petition, assumed by the Reorganized Debtor and paid per its original terms.","\u00a7 2.1(d): treated as Allowed Administrative Claims. \u00a7 6.6: approved by the board Feb. 15, 2025; paid $1.7M on the Effective Date and $1.7M six months later. (Both then struck.)","The Committee struck a provision that is not in the Filed Plan. Its \u00a7 503(c) and administrative-priority framing depends on the untracked recharacterization. Respond to the Filed Plan \u00a7 5.8 (see V.A-7)."],
["U-8","Litigation Trust; Avoidance Actions","\u00a7 5.9: trust pursues Avoidance Actions (\u00a7\u00a7 544\u2013553) for the benefit of the Reorganized Debtor; trustee appointed by the Reorganized Debtor with Committee consent; net proceeds retained by the Reorganized Debtor. \u00a7 5.10: other causes of action retained by the Reorganized Debtor.","\u00a7 6.7(b): **all Avoidance Actions and all \u201cRetained Actions\u201d** (every other estate claim) vest in the trust, and the trustee has \u201cexclusive authority.\u201d \u201cAvoidance Actions\u201d is expanded to \u00a7\u00a7 502, 510, 541\u2013543, 551, 552 and common law. The \u201cRetained Actions\u201d definition says such claims vest in the Reorganized Debtor, which contradicts \u00a7 6.7(b).","Strips the Reorganized Debtor of its ordinary commercial claims and defenses and gives them to a Committee-selected trustee. Bringing \u00a7\u00a7 502(d) and 510 within the definition gives the trust leverage over claims allowance and subordination. **Reject; retain Filed Plan \u00a7\u00a7 5.9\u20135.10 and negotiate only the proceeds allocation.**"],
["U-9","Effective Date; conditions","ED = 30 days after the Confirmation Order becomes a Final Order (est. Aug. 15, 2025). \u00a7 9.1 confirmation conditions include a Confirmation Order acceptable to the Debtor, First Meridian and Timberline. \u00a7 9.2 ED conditions include an executed Amended Credit Agreement, adopted Governance Documents, and an established Litigation Trust with a trustee appointed.","ED = first Business Day on which conditions are satisfied. No confirmation conditions. ED conditions omit the Amended Credit Agreement, Governance Documents and Litigation Trust conditions.","Removes First Meridian\u2019s and Timberline\u2019s consent rights over the Confirmation Order and the lender-documentation condition. ["U-10","Non-occurrence of ED","Confirmation Order vacated only \u201cupon motion by the Debtor\u201d (\u00a7 9.4).","\u201cUpon motion by any party in interest\u201d (\u00a7 9.3).","Combined with the new 9.1(g) condition and the Committee veto in 9.2, this would let the Committee withhold waiver and then move to vacate confirmation after 120 days. **Reject.**"],
["U-11","Plan Supplement timing","No later than 14 days before the Confirmation Hearing (\u00a7 13.5). (DS \u00a7 6.3 says 10 days; see Section VIII.)","No later than 7 days before the Voting Deadline.","Changes the solicitation timetable. **Conform to the Disclosure Statement Order.**"],
["U-12","Executory contracts","Assumption subject to court approval; cure notice at least 21 days before the Confirmation Hearing; unlisted contracts deemed assumed (\u00a7\u00a7 8.1, 8.3, 8.5).","Assumption effective \u201cwithout the need for any \u2026 order\u201d; no cure-notice procedure; no deemed-assumption clause.","Due-process and \u00a7 365(b) problems. Contracts left off the schedule would have no treatment. **Reject.**"],
["U-13","Exhibit C","12 assumed contracts and 6 rejected contracts (e.g., Willamette Valley Power, Pacific NW Rail, Greenleaf, Deschutes Equipment Leasing lease, Northshore, Timberpoint).","A different schedule of 7 assumed and 5 rejected contracts (e.g., Cascade Range Logistics, Douglas Fir Land Management, Redmond Equipment Leasing, Deschutes River Environmental). Only Olympic and PacWest appear in both.","Every other counterparty on the Debtor\u2019s schedule loses its treatment. The lease of Committee member Deschutes Equipment Leasing ($210K cure) disappears. **Reject; the Committee must mark the filed Exhibit C.**"],
["U-14","Omitted operative provisions","Arts. VI\u2013VII (distributions, disputed-claims reserve, setoff, unclaimed property); \u00a7 5.5 cancellation; \u00a7 5.6 credit amendment; \u00a7 5.10 preservation of claims; \u00a7 5.11 \u00a7 1146 transfer-tax exemption; \u00a7\u00a7 11.6\u201311.7 modification/revocation; \u00a7 13.4 Committee dissolution.","Not present.","Without these, the plan has no distribution mechanics or \u00a7 1146 exemption, and the **Committee never dissolves**. That matters because the Redline also gives the Committee board-designation rights. **Reject.**"],
["U-15","New untracked obligations","None.","\u00a7 11.6: quarterly operating reports to the Court and U.S. Trustee for two years after the ED. \u00a7 4.3: cap at face amount. \u00a7 4.2: recital that Timberline\u2019s equity is \u201cvalued at approximately $60,000,000.\u201d","The reporting covenant is an untracked post-emergence burden. A $310M\u2013$347M; GUC recovery ~2%\u20135%. Ex. B Year 1 revenue $312M, EBITDA $52M, FCF $6M; debt service $28M.","Different evidentiary exhibits under the Debtor\u2019s name. On the Redline\u2019s own Ex. B, the Committee\u2019s Year-1 payment is even less fundable. **Reject.**"],

Notices: First Meridian, 1000 Second Ave., 30th Fl., Seattle; Timberline, 555 California St., Ste. 4200; W&C tel. (503) 555-7200.","James R. Hargrove, CEO; First Meridian, 701 Fifth Ave., Ste. 4000; Timberline, 560 California St., Ste. 3200; W&C tel. para(d,"Each tracked change is mapped below to the Filed Plan provision it would modify. Change numbers refer to the Committee’s change log (reconciled in full in Appendix A). Severity: **High** means a confirmation, feasibility or plan-support risk, or more than $5M of value; **Medium** means a material negotiating point; **Low** means drafting. d.add_heading("A. Plan Economics",level=2)
rows=[H,
["A-1 GUC pool size (#14)","§ 1.1 / § 4.4: $18.7M cash pool; 10.0% recovery on $187M.","$28.0M pool; 14.97% recovery. Comment reserves rights to seek more.","+$9.3M cash (+50%). The DS liquidation analysis puts Chapter 7 GUC recovery at $0, so the best-interests test is met either way. The increase is purely a negotiated allocation. The Transmittal calls the $28.0M headline “firmly held” but says timing is negotiable. That is the opening to use.","High","**Counter**: hold Effective Date cash; consider reaching a higher headline through deferred and/or non-cash consideration (Section IX)."],
["A-2 Payment split (#14, #20, #21)","50/50: $9.35M on the ED; $9.35M at the first anniversary.","75/25: $21.0M on the ED; $7.0M at the first anniversary.","Effective Date cash need rises to $74.5M against $68.0M of projected cash, a $6.5M shortfall. The Redline’s § 6.2 still recites $62.85M. The Plan would fail Filed Plan condition § 9.2(e) and the § 1129(a)(11) feasibility test unless exit financing is drawn on the ED, and the DS says no draw is anticipated.","High","**Reject** 75/25. Effective Date payment capped at ~$9.35M–$11.0M."],
["A-3 Interest on deferred amount (#14, #21)","No interest (§ 4.4).","Federal judgment rate (28 U.S.C. § 1961) as of the Confirmation Date, “currently 5.24%.”","About $0.37M on $7.0M over one year ($0.49M on $9.35M). Economically small. Verify the 5.24% rate before relying on it.","Low","**Trade**: concede if the split and pool are resolved favorably."],
["A-4 Avoidance proceeds (#9, #22, #29, #37)","§ 5.9(d): net proceeds retained by the Reorganized Debtor “for the benefit of … all stakeholders.” Clearview excludes the ~$9.5M gross preference estimate from TEV.","New “Avoidance Action Recovery Pool”: 100% of net proceeds to GUCs, in addition to the pool, distributed semi-annually by the trustee. Recovery stated as “up to 20.05%.”","Net value per the Committee’s own comment is $6.0M–$7.5M (3.2–4.0 points of recovery). 20.05% assumes $9.5M gross with no costs. Because “Avoidance Actions” includes fraudulent-transfer claims, any Dividend Recap recovery would also go 100% to GUCs. Preference suits against go-forward trade vendors can damage the business. Committee members (trade vendors and lessors) may be among the ~15 defendants.","High","**Counter**: GUCs share in **net preference** proceeds (e.g., 50%, or 100% above a threshold, or a capped amount); Dividend Recap claims handled separately; the Reorganized Debtor keeps a waiver right for critical go-forward vendors."],
["A-5 Timberline equity % (#6, #19, #24)","§§ 4.3(b), 5.3(a): 55% of New Common Equity for $60M converted; 45% “authorized but unissued,” subject to the MIP reserve.","41.07% to Timberline; 58.93% “held by the Reorganized Debtor.”","Section VI.E has the detail. 55% gives Timberline $115.4M on a $95M claim at the midpoint, which is a fair-and-equitable exposure. 41.07% assumes the $35M cash payment does not reduce equity value; on a net basis ($111.1M) the ratio is 54.0%, close to 55%. Under both versions the residual stays unissued, so unless it is issued to someone, Timberline holds 100% of the outstanding shares. Neither version gives the residual to GUCs.","High","**Do not accept as a “correction.”** Reconcile with Clearview and Timberline (Section IX). Fix the unissued-share drafting in any event."],
["A-6 MIP pool (#11, #25)","§ 5.7: 10% fully diluted; vests 25% per year.","7%.","The dilution falls on equity holders, i.e., Timberline. GUCs hold no equity, so the stated rationale fails. At the midpoint the 3-point change is worth about $4.4M of equity value to Timberline, not to GUCs.","Medium","**Hold at 10%, or let Timberline trade it** (e.g., 8%) for movement elsewhere. Do not concede to the Committee for free."],
["A-7 Retention bonuses (#17, #27)","§ 5.8: Reorganized Debtor assumes the $3.4M program for 12 senior employees, approved pre-petition. The DS says it is paid in cash on or promptly after the ED.","Strikes both § 2.1(d) and § 6.6, provisions that exist only in the Redline base. Comment invokes § 503(c)(1) and calls the payments “disguised priority payments.”","The Filed Plan is vulnerable here. Prepetition bonus entitlements are unsecured claims, and paying them in full under the Plan while other GUCs receive 10% raises § 1123(a)(4) / § 1122 and unfair-discrimination issues. For insiders (COO, CFO), § 503(c)(1) requires bona fide competing offers. For non-insiders, § 503(c)(3) applies a facts-and-circumstances standard. No evidentiary record has been built. The $3.4M is also absent from the Effective Date uses table.","High","**Accept-Mod**: remove the assumption from the Plan. Either (i) file a § 503(c) motion with an evidentiary record, or (ii) replace the program with a post-emergence retention/KEIP adopted by the New Board and disclosed under § 1129(a)(5). Reject the § 11.9 framing."],
]

d.add_heading("B. Releases, Exculpation, Injunction and the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization",level=2)
rows=[H,
["B-1 Non-consensual third-party release (#32)","§ 10.4(c): releases bind all holders except those who opt out by ballot or form; the DS describes this as “non-consensual.”","Struck. Consensual release (§ 8.2(a)) retained for accepting voters and non-opt-outs.","After Purdue (144 S. Ct. 2071 (2024)), a plan cannot impose non-consensual releases of non-debtors under § 1123(b)(6). Ninth Circuit authority was already restrictive (e.g., In re Lowenschuss, 67 F.3d 1394 (9th Cir. 1995)). The Redline’s retained § 8.2(a) is itself an opt-out construct, so the practical difference is largely the label and the treatment of non-voting and deemed-rejecting holders.","High","**Accept** the deletion. Recast as a consensual release: opt-out for voting classes, with conspicuous ballot disclosure, or opt-in for non-voting classes. Delete § 10.4(d)’s statement that the Committee concurred."],
["B-2 Dividend Recap carve-out (#31, #47)","§ 10.4(d) and § 10.5 release all claims against Released Parties, including Timberline, expressly including Dividend Recap claims.","Debtor/estate release and consensual third-party release exclude claims against Timberline (and affiliates, officers, members, agents) arising from the 2021 Dividend Recap. Those claims vest in the Litigation Trust.","See VII.2. The § 548 claims are time-barred (two-year reach-back; the transaction closed Sept. 14, 2021, and the petition was filed Mar. 3, 2025). Only § 544(b) and state-law (UVTA, four-year) theories remain, preserved for two years post-petition by § 546(a). The natural constructive-fraud defendants are the dividend recipients; Timberline advanced $95M of cash. A release of Timberline without disclosure or an investigation record is very hard to defend at confirmation. Timberline’s support is the counterweight.","High","**Counter** (Timberline consent required). Options: (i) carve-out limited to claims against dividend recipients and insiders, with Timberline released in exchange for a defined contribution; (ii) an independent investigation with a 9019 settlement before confirmation; (iii) preserve claims against Timberline only, subject to a cap or a standstill on lien and claim challenges."],
["B-3 Supplemental disclosure condition (#34)","No such condition. DS § 3.3 describes the transaction and the solvency opinion.","New ED condition § 9.1(g): court-approved supplemental DS covering structure, recipients, avoidability, solvency, damages, the Committee’s position and the impact on recoveries.","Procedurally backwards. Adequate information must be approved before solicitation (§ 1125(b)). A disclosure statement approved after confirmation cannot inform votes already cast, and as an ED condition it creates post-confirmation hold-up risk. The legitimate concern can be met by expanding DS § 3.3 before June 12.","High","**Reject** as a condition. **Offer** an expanded DS section (and a Committee letter in the solicitation package) before the June 12 hearing."],
["B-4 Committee veto on waiver (#35)","§ 9.3: conditions waivable by the Debtor with Timberline and First Meridian consent where for their benefit.","The 9.1(g) condition cannot be waived without the Committee’s written consent.","Gives a non-proponent a veto over consummation. With U-10 (any party may move to vacate), this becomes leverage to unwind confirmation.","High","**Reject.**"],
["B-5 Injunction exception (#33)","§ 10.2 enjoins actions against the Debtor, the Reorganized Debtor and Released Parties.","Injunction does not bar claims preserved under §§ 8.1–8.2, including Dividend Recap claims.","Acceptable only as a conforming change if a carve-out is agreed and limited to estate claims prosecuted by the trust. As drafted it could also let third parties sue on recap theories.","Medium","**Accept-Mod**: limit to estate causes of action vested in the Litigation Trust."],
["B-6 Discharge proviso (#36)","§ 10.1 discharge under § 1141(d).","Discharge “shall not affect claims expressly preserved under Article VIII … including … the 2021 Dividend Recapitalization.”","Dividend Recap claims are claims **of** the estate, not claims **against** the Debtor, so no discharge exception is needed. As drafted, the proviso could be read to preserve claims **against** the Debtor arising from the recap (e.g., indemnification or contribution claims of dividend recipients or the noteholder), which would undermine the discharge.","High","**Reject**; if necessary, add a clarifying sentence that estate causes of action vest in the trust."],
["B-7 Exculpation (no change)","§ 10.3: Debtor, Reorganized Debtor, Committee and their professionals; carve-out for willful misconduct, gross negligence and fraud.","Unchanged in substance.","Note: the Committee keeps its own exculpation while stripping Timberline’s release. The DS summary omits the “fraud” carve-out (Section VIII).","Low","Conform the DS."],

["C-1 Board (#26)","§ 5.4: 3 Timberline / 1 Committee / 1 independent (mutually selected).","2 Timberline / 2 Committee / 1 independent. d.add_heading("E. Confirmation Mechanics and Reservations",level=2)
rows=[H,
["E-1 New § 11.9 (#38) and § 5.3 cross-reference (#46)","§ 11.5 reserves cramdown under § 1129(b).","If Class 3 rejects: the Debtor bears the burden by a preponderance; the parties “acknowledge” that the retention program “constitutes value that may be characterized as property retained by insiders” junior to GUCs; the Debtor must address the MIP.","The burden already rests on the proponent, so (a) is surplusage. Clause (b) is an admission against interest on a legally weak theory. The absolute priority rule (§ 1129(b)(2)(B)(ii)) concerns property received “on account of” a junior claim or interest. Old equity is cancelled, and post-emergence compensation for services is not on account of junior interests. The comment’s citation should be Czyzewski v. Jevic Holding Corp., 580 U.S. 451 (2017), not 580 U.S. 455, and Jevic concerned structured dismissals. A plan is not the place to pre-try cramdown.","High","**Reject** in full."],

["E-3 Committee reservation of rights (#41)","None.","New § 12.8 paragraph reserving Committee objections under §§ 1129(a)(3), (4), (7), (9) and (b).","A Debtor’s plan should not carry an objector’s reservation. It belongs in the Committee’s objection or a stipulation.","Low","**Reject.**"],

]

d.add_heading("F. “Cosmetic” Changes That Are Not Cosmetic",level=2)
for t in [
 "**Effective Date definition (#7).** The comment says “[n]o substantive change.” In fact the rewritten list of conditions omits the Amended Credit Agreement, Governance Documents and Litigation Trust conditions, and it sits on a base definition that drops the Filed Plan’s 30-days-after-Final-Order mechanic. **Reject.**",
 "**“Reorganized Company” (#1).** Creates two defined terms for one entity. The Redline already uses them inconsistently (e.g., the MIP refers to the “Reorganized Company” while § 6.4 uses “Reorganized Debtor”), which invites interpretive disputes over the MIP and governance documents. **Reject.**",
 "**Allowed Claim cross-reference (#3).** “Article V, Section 5.1” is the Redline’s Voting Classes section and has nothing to do with claims allowance. The Filed Plan’s allowance and disputed-claims provisions are in Article VII. **Reject; fix the cross-reference correctly.**",
 "**Plan Supplement (#13).** Refers to “the list of Exhibits attached hereto,” which does not exist. **Reject** unless a list is added.",
 "**Administrative Claim (#2) and Rules of Interpretation (#16).** These are redundant: the definition already cites §§ 503(b) and 507(a)(2), and § 1.2(g) already covers section references. They are harmless; accept or reject for economy.",
 "**Acceptable as drafted, subject to conforming to the Filed Plan’s definitions:** Ballot (#4); Business Day, which adds court closure days and slightly affects timing (#5); Equity Conversion Amount spelled out, though the term must first be defined in the Filed Plan (#8); Confirmation Date by docket entry (#10); Person, adding governmental entity (#12); Voting Deadline time (#15), subject to the solicitation order; classification table amounts (#18), conformed to the seven-class structure; and notice emails (#40), which must be verified and conformed to the filed notice addresses.",
]: bullet(d,t)

S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/bankruptcy-restructuring/analyze-counterparty-markup-of-plan-of-reorganization/claude-code-session/20261016-024711; $S $R 'cat > /workspace/build/part5.py <<"EOF"
d.add_heading("VII. Key Legal Issues",level=1)
d.add_heading("1. Third-party releases after Purdue",level=2)
para(d,"Purdue holds that the Bankruptcy Code does not authorize a release and injunction that extinguishes claims against non-debtors without the consent of the affected claimants. The Filed Plan’s § 10.4(c) is labeled “Non-Consensual” and the DS describes it that way. That label alone gives the Committee and the U.S. Trustee a clean objection. Mechanically, § 10.4(b)–(c) operate through an opt-out. Whether silence or a failure to opt out amounts to consent is contested after Purdue, and courts are divided. Opt-out mechanics are most defensible for creditors who actually receive a ballot and vote, with conspicuous disclosure. They are least defensible for deemed-rejecting classes (Classes 5–7), which receive nothing and do not vote.")
para(d,"**Recommendation.** Concede the Committee’s point in principle. Retitle and restructure § 10.4 as a consensual release: opt-out for voting Classes 2–4 with a prominent ballot election, and opt-in or no release for non-voting classes. Keep the Debtor release (§ 10.5), which is an estate settlement under § 1123(b)(3)(A) and is not affected by Purdue, but support it with a record. This is the cheapest of the Committee’s three “non-negotiable” items and gives us credibility on the other two.")
d.add_heading("2. The 2021 Dividend Recapitalization",level=2)
for t in [
 "**What the record shows.** On Sept. 14, 2021, Timberline purchased $95M of Second Lien Notes, and approximately $88M of the proceeds funded a special dividend to existing equity holders (the Whitaker family at ~40%, plus institutional holders). Funded debt rose from ~$275M to ~$370M, and a solvency opinion was delivered at closing (DS §§ 3.2–3.3). Clearview and DS § 3.4(c) both identify the recap as a cause of distress, and Clearview notes it “is a subject of potential avoidance action scrutiny by the estate.”",
 "**Limitations.** Section 548(a) reaches transfers and obligations within two years before the petition, so the Sept. 2021 transaction falls outside that window (petition Mar. 3, 2025). The viable theories are § 544(b) claims under applicable state fraudulent-transfer law. Choice of law (Oregon UVTA, ORS 95.200 et seq., or Delaware) must be analyzed; constructive-fraud limitation periods are generally four years. A claim timely as of the petition date can be brought within the § 546(a) period (two years after the order for relief, i.e., by Mar. 3, 2027). The Committee’s references to § 548 should be corrected in any disclosure.",
 "**Defendants.** The constructive-fraud theory runs most naturally against the dividend recipients (§ 550(a)), not the lender that advanced cash. Exposure for Timberline would turn on theories such as avoiding the obligation and lien, collapsing the transaction based on Timberline’s knowledge, recharacterization, or equitable subordination. The Committee’s assertion that dividend recipients included “entities affiliated with Timberline” is not supported by the DS. If it were true, it would also bear on Timberline’s insider status (Issue 4).",
 "**The Filed Plan’s weakness.** Filed Plan § 10.4(d) releases the Dividend Recap claims against Timberline and recites that “the Debtor and the Committee have reviewed the relevant facts … and have concluded that the releases … are appropriate.” The Committee plainly has not so concluded. No independent investigation is described, and no value attributable to the release is identified. A court evaluating an estate release under § 1123(b)(3)(A) and Rule 9019 will expect a record. Without one, this is the Committee’s strongest confirmation objection.",
 "**Recommendation.** Do not give up the release to Timberline unilaterally; it is Timberline’s deal. Do (a) expand DS § 3.3 before June 12 to cover transaction steps, the dividend recipients and amounts, the solvency opinion provider and conclusions, the limitations analysis, and the Debtor’s and the Committee’s positions; (b) propose to Timberline either an independent-director investigation with a 9019-quality record supporting the release, or a carve-out limited to dividend recipients and insiders; and (c) remove the inaccurate Committee-concurrence sentence immediately.",
]: bullet(d,t)
d.add_heading("3. A post-confirmation “supplemental disclosure” condition",level=2)
para(d,"Section 1125(b) bars post-petition solicitation unless a court-approved disclosure statement is transmitted first. A disclosure approved after confirmation, as proposed § 9.1(g) would require, cannot inform votes already cast. Using it as an Effective Date condition, waivable only by the Committee (§ 9.2), with any party able to move to vacate after 120 days (U-10), would give the Committee leverage over consummation. Supplementing the disclosure to address the Committee’s legitimate points before solicitation fully answers the concern. We can also offer the Committee a letter in the solicitation package stating its position.")
d.add_heading("4. Impairment, classification and § 1129(a)(10)",level=2)
para(d,"Section 1129(a)(10) requires acceptance by at least one impaired class, determined without counting acceptances by insiders. The Filed Plan correctly treats First Meridian (Class 2) as impaired and voting: its maturity is extended and its rate reduced, which alters its rights, so it is not unimpaired under § 1124. The DS (Class 4: “unimpaired by virtue of reinstatement … deemed to accept”) and the Redline base (Class 1: unimpaired) both get this wrong. DS § 13.3 relies on Timberline’s class as the accepting impaired class if GUCs reject. If First Meridian were deemed to accept rather than voting, and the Committee succeeded in characterizing Timberline as an insider or non-statutory insider (plan sponsor, majority board designee, alleged affiliation with dividend recipients), the Debtor could lose its only accepting impaired class. **Action:** correct the DS. Keep First Meridian as an impaired voting class and obtain its affirmative vote. Assess Timberline’s insider status now.")
d.add_heading("5. Fair and equitable: the Debtor’s 55% exposure",level=2)
para(d,"If Class 4 rejects, the Debtor must show the plan is fair and equitable as to Class 4. Clearview’s own waterfall shows Timberline receiving more than par at every point in the range at 55%, and potentially all outstanding equity if the 45% remains unissued (VI.E). Meanwhile, DS Art. XI shows Timberline recovering at most 53.8% in liquidation. The Committee has framed this narrowly, as an arithmetic error, but the underlying argument is stronger: value above Timberline’s allowed claim belongs to the next junior class. The Debtor’s answers are (a) Timberline’s role as plan sponsor and any new-value or cash commitment, which must be documented; DS § 6.1 refers to a “significant cash contribution,” but the Plan describes the $35M as a payment to Timberline that Timberline itself funds, which is circular and must be clarified; (b) valuation risk; and (c) the MIP. These answers need evidence. A cleaner fix is to allocate part of the residual equity, or warrants, to Class 4. That also creates non-cash currency for settlement.")
d.add_heading("6. Retention bonuses and § 503(c)",level=2)
para(d,"Section 503(c)(1) bars retention payments to insiders unless the court finds a bona fide job offer at the same or greater compensation, that the services are essential to the survival of the business, and that the amount is within statutory caps. Section 503(c)(3) limits other transfers outside the ordinary course that are not justified by the facts and circumstances. The DS asserts competitor recruitment efforts and an average of 18 years of experience, but the record has no offer evidence and no insider analysis. Paying a prepetition, board-approved program in full under the Plan also raises same-treatment (§ 1123(a)(4)) and unfair-discrimination issues against 10% GUCs. **Recommendation:** remove the assumption from the Plan. Either file a § 503(c) motion supported by evidence, or move retention to a post-emergence program adopted by the New Board and disclosed under § 1129(a)(5). This also frees $1.7M–$3.4M of Effective Date cash. Reject proposed § 11.9: post-emergence compensation for services is not property received “on account of” a junior claim or interest.")
d.add_heading("7. Avoidance action proceeds",level=2)
para(d,"The Committee’s position has some equitable force. Avoidance recoveries are for the benefit of the estate (§ 550(a)) and are excluded from TEV (Clearview § IV), so leaving them with a Reorganized Debtor owned by Timberline invites the argument that they are a further value transfer to the senior class. Countervailing points: preference suits against ~15 counterparties, many likely ongoing trade vendors, can impair go-forward supply relationships; the Committee members are themselves likely preference targets; and net recoveries are uncertain and delayed. **Recommendation:** offer a sharing formula for net preference proceeds, a vendor-waiver right for the Reorganized Debtor, an independent trustee, and a conflicts protocol.")
d.add_heading("8. Contract rejection standard",level=2)
para(d,"Rejection is governed by the business-judgment test. A plan-imposed “material net burden” standard would invite counterparties, including Committee members, to litigate each rejection and would cloud the Debtor’s projected $8M of annual cost savings, which rely in part on “the rejection of uneconomical contracts” (Plan Ex. B). Rejection operates as a breach (Mission Product Holdings v. Tempnology, 587 U.S. 370 (2019)), and the resulting damages claims are already protected as Class 4 claims. **Reject.**")

para(d,"The comparison exposed inconsistencies among the Filed Plan, the DS and Clearview. The Committee will raise these at the DS hearing as adequacy-of-information objections under § 1125, or as feasibility objections. We recommend correcting them in an amended DS/Plan filing, ideally together with any agreed Committee changes.")
